body.text: // atha baudhāyanadharmasūtram //
body.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Baudhāyanadharmasūtra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.1.1.1/ upadiṣṭo dharmaḥ prati.vedam //
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (law) has been taught in accordance with each <s>Veda</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.1.1.2/ tasya^anu (vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: We shall explain it in detail.

body.text: Baudh1.1.1.3/ smārto dvitīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The second [source of <s>dharma</s>] is that which is based on tradition (<s>smṛti</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.1.1.4/ tṛtīyaḥ śiṣṭa.āgamaḥ //
body.translated_text: The third is the tradition of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.1.1.5/ śiṣṭāḥ khalu vigata.matsarā nirahaṃkārāḥ kumbhī.dhānyāalolupā dambha.darpa.lobha.moha.krodha.vivarjitāḥ //
body.translated_text: The learned (<s>śiṣṭas</s>) are indeed those who are free from envy, free from egotism, who store only a pot's measure of grain, who are free from hypocrisy, arrogance, greed, delusion, and anger.

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.6ab/ dharmeṇa^adhigato yeṣāṃ vedaḥ saparibṛṃhaṇaḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.6cd/ śiṣṭās tad.anumāna.jñāḥ śruti.pratyakṣa.hetavaḥ // iti //[cf. Va 6.43; ṃ 12.109]
Baudh1.1.1.7/ tad.abhāve daśa.avarā pariṣat //
body.translated_text: Those who have obtained the <s>Veda</s> together with its supplements through <s>dharma</s> — those are the learned; knowledge of that [<s>dharma</s>] is inferred from them, and its proofs are scripture and direct perception. // In the absence of such [learned ones], an assembly of no fewer than ten [shall decide]. //

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.8/ atha^api^(udāharanti /
Baudh1.1.1.8ab/ cāturvaidyaṃ vikalpī ca aṅga.vid dharma.pāṭhakaḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.8cd/ āśrama.sthās trayo viprāḥ parṣad eṣā daśa.avarā //
body.translated_text: And on this they also cite: 'One versed in the four <s>Vedas</s>, a dialectician, one versed in the ancillary sciences, one who recites the <s>dharma</s> texts, and brahmins in three <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) — this is an assembly of no fewer than ten.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.9ab/ pañca vā (syus trayo vā (syur eko vā (syād aninditaḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.9cd/ prativaktā tu dharmasya na^itare tu sahasraśaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'There may be five, or three, or even one blameless [person] who can pronounce on <s>dharma</s> — but not others, even though they be thousands.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.10ab/ yathā dārumayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.10cd/ brāhmaṇaś ca^anadhīyānas trayas te nāma.dhārakāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'As a wooden elephant, as a leather deer, and a brahmin who has not studied — these three are bearers of [mere] names.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.11ab/ yad (vadanti tamas.mūḍhā mūrkhā dharmam ajānataḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.11cd/ tat pāpaṃ śatadhā (bhūtvā vaktqn (samadhigacchati //
body.translated_text: 'What those who are deluded by darkness, fools ignorant of <s>dharma</s>, declare — that sin, multiplied a hundredfold, falls upon the speakers.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.12ab/ bahu.dvārasya dharmasya sūkṣmā duranugā gatiḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.12cd/ tasmān na vācyo hy ekena bahujñena^api saṃśaye //
body.translated_text: 'The course of <s>dharma</s>, which has many doors, is subtle and hard to follow; therefore in doubt, [<s>dharma</s>] should not be declared by one person alone, even if learned in many [subjects].'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.13ab/ dharma.śāstra.ratha.ārūḍhā veda.khaḍga.dharā dvijāḥ /
Baudh1.1.1.13cd/ krīḍa.artham api yad (brūyuḥ sa dharmaḥ paramaḥ smṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Brahmins who ride the chariot of the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> and bear the sword of the <s>Veda</s> — what they say, even in jest, is regarded as the supreme <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.14ab/ yathā^aśmani sthitaṃ toyaṃ māruta.arkau (praṇāśayet /
Baudh1.1.1.14cd/ tadvat kartari yat pāpaṃ jalavat (saṃpralīyate //
body.translated_text: 'Just as wind and sun destroy water standing on a rock, so does sin in [a learned] doer dissolve like water.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.15ab/ śarīraṃ balam āyuś ca vayaḥ kālaṃ ca karma ca /
Baudh1.1.1.15cd/ samīkṣya dharmavid buddhyā prāyaścittāni (nirdiśet //
body.translated_text: 'Having considered the body, strength, lifespan, age, time, and the deed, the knower of <s>dharma</s> should prescribe penances with wisdom.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.1.16ab/ avratānām amantrāṇāṃ jāti.mātra.upajīvinām /
Baudh1.1.1.16cd/ sahasraśaḥ sametānāṃ pariṣattvaṃ na (vidyate // iti //
body.translated_text: 'Those without vows, without <s>mantras</s>, who subsist merely on the basis of birth — even when thousands of them assemble, they do not constitute an assembly.'

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.1/ pañcadhā vipratipattir dakṣiṇatas tathā^uttarataḥ //
body.translated_text: There is a fivefold divergence [of practice] between the south and the north.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.2/ yāni dakṣiṇatas tāni (vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: We shall explain those [practices] of the south.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.3/ yathā^etad anupetena saha bhojanaṃ striyā saha bhojanaṃparyuṣita.bhojanaṃ mātula.pitṛ.svasṛ.duhitṛ.gamanam iti //
body.translated_text: Such as: eating together with one who has not been initiated, eating together with a woman, eating leftover food, and intercourse with the daughter of a maternal uncle, father's sister, or [one's own] sister.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.4/ atha^uttarata ūrṇā.vikrayaḥ sīdhu.pānam ubhayatas.dadbhirvyavahāra āyudhīyakaṃ samudra.saṃyānam iti //
body.translated_text: And in the north: selling wool, drinking <s>sīdhu</s> (liquor), dealing with those who have both [sets of] teeth, [dealing in] weapons, and sea voyages.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.5/ itarad itarasmin kurvan (duṣyati^itarad itarasmin //
body.translated_text: One who practices [the customs of] one region in the other is considered at fault in [either] region.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.6/ tatra tatra deśa.prāmāṇyam eva (syāt //
body.translated_text: In each region, the authority of the local [custom] shall prevail.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.7/ mithyā^etad iti gautamaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Gautama</s> says this is wrong.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.8/ ubhayaṃ ca^eva / na^(ādriyeta śiṣṭa.smṛti.virodha.darśanāt //
body.translated_text: Both [views are stated]; one should not follow [local custom] when it contradicts the tradition of the learned.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.9/ prāg ādarśāt pratyak kanakhalād [K: kālakavanād] dakṣiṇenahimavantam udak pāriyātram etad āryāvartam / tasmin ya ācāraḥ sapramāṇam //
body.translated_text: From [Mount] <s>Ādarśa</s> in the east to <s>Kanakhala</s> in the west, south of the <s>Himavat</s> and north of <s>Pāriyātra</s> — this is <s>Āryāvarta</s>. The practice that prevails there is authoritative.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.10/ gaṅgā.yamunayor antaram ity eke //
body.translated_text: Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>, according to some.

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.11/ atha^apy atra bhāllavino gāthām (udāharanti //
body.translated_text: And on this the <s>Bhāllavins</s> also cite this verse:

body.text:
Baudh1.1.2.12ab/ paścāt sindhur vidharaṇī sūryasya^udayanaṃ puraḥ /
Baudh1.1.2.12cd/ yāvat kṛṣṇā (vidhāvanti tāvad dhi brahmavarcasam // iti //
body.translated_text: 'In the west the <s>Sindhu</s> as border, the rising of the sun in the east — as far as the dark [antelopes] run, that far extends the <s>brahmavarcas</s> (Vedic splendor).'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.2.13ab/ avantayas^aṅga.magadhāḥ surāṣṭrā dakṣiṇāpathāḥ /
Baudh1.1.2.13cd/ upāvṛt.sindhu.sauvīrā ete saṃkīrṇa.yonayaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Avantis</s>, <s>Aṅgas</s>, <s>Magadhas</s>, <s>Surāṣṭras</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇāpathas</s>, <s>Upavrṛt-Sindhus</s>, and <s>Sauvīras</s> — these are of mixed origin.'

body.text: Baudh1.1.2.14/ āraṭṭān kāraskarān puṇḍrān sauvīrān vaṅgān kaliṅgānprānūnān iti ca (gatvā punastomena (yajeta sarvapṛṣṭhayā vā //
body.translated_text: Having gone to the <s>Āraṭṭas</s>, <s>Kāraskaras</s>, <s>Puṇḍras</s>, <s>Sauvīras</s>, <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, and <s>Prānūnas</s>, one should offer the <s>Stoma</s> sacrifice or one with all the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [hymns].

body.text:
Baudh1.1.2.15-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.1.2.15-2ab/ padbhyāṃ sa (kurute pāpaṃ yaḥ kaliṅgān (prapadyate /
Baudh1.1.2.15-2cd/ ṛṣayo niṣkṛtiṃ tasya (prāhur vaiśvānaraṃ haviḥ //
body.translated_text: And they also cite: 'One who goes to the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> commits sin with his feet; the <s>ṛṣis</s> declare that his atonement is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> oblation.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.2.16ab/ bahūnām api doṣāṇāṃ kṛtānāṃ doṣa.nirṇaye /
Baudh1.1.2.16cd/ pavitra.iṣṭiṃ (praśaṃsanti sā [! disagreement] hi pāvanamuttamam // iti //
body.translated_text: 'Even for many faults committed, in the determination of fault, they praise the <s>Pavitreṣṭi</s> (purificatory sacrifice) — for it is the supreme purification.'

body.text:
Baudh1.1.2.17-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.1.2.17-2ab/ vaiśvānarīṃ vrātapatīṃ pavitra.iṣṭiṃ tathā^eva ca /
Baudh1.1.2.17-2cd/ ṛtau^ṛtau prayuñjānaḥ pāpebhyo (vipramucyate // pāpebhyovipramucyata iti //
body.translated_text: And they also cite: 'One who regularly performs the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s>, the <s>Vrātapatī</s>, and the <s>Pavitreṣṭi</s> at each season is freed from sins.'

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.1/ aṣṭācatvāriṃśad varṣāṇi paurāṇaṃ veda.brahmacaryam //
body.translated_text: The ancient [duration of] Vedic <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship) is forty-eight years.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.2/ caturviṃśatiṃ dvādaśa vā prati.vedam //
body.translated_text: Twenty-four or twelve [years] for each <s>Veda</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.3/ saṃvatsara.avamaṃ vā prati.kāṇḍam //
body.translated_text: Or a minimum of one year for each <s>kāṇḍa</s> (section).

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.4/ grahaṇa.antaṃ vā jīvitasya^asthiratvāt //
body.translated_text: Or until [the text is] mastered, because of the uncertainty of life.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.5/ kṛṣṇakeśas^agnīn (ādadhīta^iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: One should establish the sacred fires while one's hair is still black — [so says] the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).

body.text:
Baudh1.2.3.6ab/ na^asya karma (niyacchanti kiṃcid ā mauñji.bandhanāt /
Baudh1.2.3.6cd/ vṛttyā śūdra.samo hy eṣa yāvad vedena (jāyate //^iti //
body.translated_text: 'No rite governs him at all before the binding of the <s>mauñjī</s> (girdle of <s>muñja</s> grass); for in his conduct he is equal to a <s>śūdra</s> until he is born through the <s>Veda</s>.'

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.7/ garbha.ādiḥ saṃkhyā varṣāṇām / tad.aṣṭameṣu brāhmaṇam(upanayīta //
body.translated_text: The counting of years begins from conception. In the eighth [year] one should initiate a brahmin.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.8/ try.adhikeṣu rājanyam //
body.translated_text: In the eleventh [year], a <s>kṣatriya</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.9/ tasmād eka.adhikeṣu vaiśyam //
body.translated_text: One [year] more than that, a <s>vaiśya</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.10/ vasanto grīṣmaḥ śarad ity ṛtavo varṇa.ānupūrvyeṇa //
body.translated_text: Spring, summer, and autumn are the seasons [for initiation], in the order of the <s>varṇas</s> (classes).

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.11/ gāyatrī.triṣṭub.jagatībhir yathā.kramam //
body.translated_text: With the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, and <s>Jagatī</s> [meters], respectively.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.12/ ā ṣoḍaśād ā dvāviṃśād ā caturviṃśād anātyaya eṣāṃ krameṇa //
body.translated_text: Up to the sixteenth, the twenty-second, and the twenty-fourth [year] — there is no transgression for these, in order.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.13/ mauñjī dhanur.jyā śāṇī^iti mekhalāḥ //
body.translated_text: The girdles are of <s>muñja</s> grass, bowstring, and hemp.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.14/ kṛṣṇa.ruru.basta.ajināny ajināni //
body.translated_text: The skins are of black antelope, <s>ruru</s> deer, and goat.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.15/ mūrdha.lalāṭa.nāsāgra.pramāṇā yājñikasya vṛkṣasya daṇḍāḥ //
body.translated_text: The staffs are from a sacrificial tree, measuring [up to the] crown, the forehead, and the tip of the nose [respectively].

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.16/ bhavat.pūrvāṃ bhikṣā.madhyāṃ yācñā.antāṃ bhikṣāṃ (caretsapta.akṣarāṃ kṣāṃ ca hiṃ ca na (vardhayet //
body.translated_text: He should beg for alms [using a formula] beginning with '<s>bhavat</s>,' with the begging [word] in the middle and ending with the request — a seven-syllable begging [formula]; he should not increase the [word] 'give' or 'indeed.'

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.17/ bhavat.pūrvāṃ brāhmaṇo (bhikṣeta bhavan.madhyāṃ rājanyobhavad.antāṃ vaiśyaḥ sarveṣu varṇeṣu //
body.translated_text: A brahmin should beg [with '<s>bhavat</s>'] at the beginning; a <s>kṣatriya</s> with '<s>bhavat</s>' in the middle; a <s>vaiśya</s> with '<s>bhavat</s>' at the end — among all <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.18/ te brāhmaṇa.ādyāḥ svakarmasthāḥ //
body.translated_text: Those beginning with the brahmin, established in their own duties.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.19/ sadā^araṇyāt samidha (āhṛtya^(ādadhyāt //
body.translated_text: Always bringing firewood from the forest, he should offer [it on the fire].

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.20/ satyavādī hrīmān anahaṃkāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Truthful, modest, and free from egotism.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.21/ pūrva.utthāyī jaghanya.saṃveśī //
body.translated_text: Rising early, going to bed last.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.22/ sarvatra^apratihata.guruvākyas^anyatra pātakāt //
body.translated_text: Obedient to the teacher's words everywhere, except in the case of sinful [acts].

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.23/ yāvad.artha.saṃbhāṣī strībhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Speaking to women only as much as is necessary.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.24/nṛtta.gīta.vāditra.gandha.mālya.upānac.chattra.dhāraṇa.añjana.abhyañjana.varjī //
body.translated_text: Abstaining from dancing, singing, instrumental music, perfumes, garlands, sandals, carrying an umbrella, eye-ointment, and body-ointment.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.25/ dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇena savyaṃ savyena ca^(upasaṃgṛhṇīyāt //
body.translated_text: He should grasp the right [foot of the teacher] with the right [hand] and the left with the left.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.26/ dīrgham āyuḥ svargaṃ ca^īpsan kāmam anyasmai sādhu.vṛttāyaguruṇā^anujñātaḥ //
body.translated_text: Desiring long life and heaven, he may [go to study] from another [teacher] of good conduct, when permitted by the [previous] teacher.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.27/ asāv ahaṃ bho iti śrotre (saṃspṛśya manaḥ.samādhāna.artham //
body.translated_text: [Saying] 'I am so-and-so, sir,' touching the ears, for the purpose of concentrating the mind.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.28/ adhastāj jānvor ā padbhyām //
body.translated_text: Below the knees, down to the feet.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.29/ na^āsīno na^āsīnāya na śayāno na śayānāya na^aprayatona^aprayatāya //
body.translated_text: Not while sitting, not to one who is sitting; not while lying down, not to one lying down; not while impure, not to one who is impure.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.30/ śakti.viṣaye muhūrtam api na^aprayataḥ (syāt //
body.translated_text: Within one's capacity, one should not be impure even for a moment.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.31/ samid.dhārī^udakumbha.puṣpa.anna.hasto na^(abhivādayed yacca^anyad apy evaṃ.yuktam //
body.translated_text: One should not salute while carrying firewood, a water-pot, flowers, or food in hand — and whatever else is of such a kind.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.32/ na samavāye^(abhivādayed atyantaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: One should not salute excessively in an assembly.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.33/ bhrātṛ.patnīnāṃ yuvatīnāṃ ca guru.ptnīnāṃ jāta.vīryaḥ //
body.translated_text: [This rule applies] for brothers' wives who are young, and for young wives of the teacher, [when the student has] reached puberty.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.34/ nau.śilā.phalaka.kuñjara.prāsāda.kaṭeṣu cakravatsu ca^adoṣamsaha.āsanam //
body.translated_text: On boats, stones, wooden planks, elephants, terraces, and mats, and [on anything] with wheels — sitting together is no fault.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.35/ prasādhana.utsādana[K:ucchādana].snāpana.ucchiṣṭabojanāni^iti guroḥ //
body.translated_text: Adorning, massaging, bathing [the teacher], and eating his leftovers — these are [the duties] toward the teacher.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.36/ ucchiṣṭa.varjanaṃ[K: varjaṃ] tat.putre^anūcāne vā //
body.translated_text: Avoiding his leftovers — this [applies] to his son or to a learned [assistant teacher].

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.37/ prasādhana.utsādana[K: ucchādana].snāpana.varjanaṃ[K:varjaṃ] ca tat.patnyām //
body.translated_text: Avoiding the adorning, massaging, and bathing — this [applies] to the teacher's wife.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.38/ dhāvantam (anudhāved gacchantam (anugacchet tiṣṭhantam(anutiṣṭhet //
body.translated_text: When [the teacher] runs, one should run after him; when he walks, one should follow him; when he stands, one should stand by him.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.39/ na^apsu ślāghamānaḥ [K: ślaghamānaḥ] (snāyāt //
body.translated_text: One should not bathe while praising oneself in the water.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.40/ daṇḍa iva (plavet //
body.translated_text: One should float like a stick.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.41/ abrāhmaṇād adhyayanam āpadi //
body.translated_text: Study from a non-brahmin [is permitted only] in an emergency.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.42/ śuśrūṣā^anuvrajyā ca yāvad.adhyayanam //
body.translated_text: Service and following [such a teacher] last only as long as the study.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.43/ tayos tad eva pāvanam //
body.translated_text: For both [student and teacher in such a case], that same [study] is their purification.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.44/ bhrātṛ.putra.śiṣyeṣu ca^evam //
body.translated_text: The same applies to brother's sons and pupils.

body.text: Baudh1.2.3.45/ ṛtvij.śvaśura.pitṛvya.mātulānāṃ tu yavīyasāṃpratyutthāya.abhibhāṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For the younger [versions of] the officiating priest, father-in-law, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle — rising and greeting [is the rule].

body.translated_text: From the case of [the sage] <s>Āṅgirasa</s> as a child — [this is established] by observation.

body.translated_text: 'Where there is neither <s>dharma</s> nor <s>artha</s> (wealth), nor service of that kind, one should die with one's learning — one should not sow it in barren soil.' // 'The <s>brahman</s> (sacred knowledge), when asked [about] but disregarded, burns like fire burning a thicket; therefore one should not speak the sacred knowledge to those who do not respect it.'

body.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (the Creator) indeed gave creatures to Death; he did not give the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student). He [Death] said: 'Let me too have a share in this one.' [<s>Brahman</s> replied:] 'On whatever night he does not bring firewood [for the fire].'

body.text: Baudh1.2.4.5/ tasmād brahmacārī yāṃ rātriṃ samidhaṃ na^(āharaty āyuṣaeva tām (avadāya (vasati / tasmād brahmacārī samidham (āharen nedāyuṣas^(avadāya (vasāni^iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, on whatever night the <s>brahmacārin</s> does not bring firewood, he dwells having cut off that [portion] of his lifespan. Therefore the <s>brahmacārin</s> should bring firewood [thinking]: 'Let me not dwell having cut off [a portion] of my lifespan.'

body.translated_text: He indeed undertakes a long sacrificial session who undertakes <s>brahmacarya</s>. The [fire] on which he offers firewood upon initiation — that is the opening offering; and the one [on which he offers] when about to graduate [by bathing] — that is the concluding offering; and those in between are his session-offerings.

body.translated_text:
Baudh1.2.4.7-1/ A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> entering <s>brahmacarya</s> (religious studentship) divides himself into four parts among beings — one quarter into <s>Agni</s> (fire), one quarter into <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death), one quarter into the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), and the fourth quarter remains in himself.
Baudh1.2.4.7-2/ When he places a fuel-stick on <s>Agni</s>, he redeems that very quarter of himself that is in <s>Agni</s>; having refined it, he takes it into himself, and it enters him.
Baudh1.2.4.7-3/ And when, having made himself poor and without shame, he begs and practises <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), he redeems that very quarter of himself that is in <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death); having refined it, he takes it into himself, and it enters him.
Baudh1.2.4.7-4/ And when he carries out the word of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), he redeems that very quarter of himself that is in the <s>ācārya</s>; having refined it, he takes it into himself, and it enters him.
Baudh1.2.4.7-5/ And when he studies the <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study of the Veda), he redeems that very quarter of himself that is in himself; having refined it, he takes it into himself, and it enters him.
Baudh1.2.4.7-6/ After completing the bath (graduation), one should not beg. Yet even after bathing, one may go begging — for the sake of feeding relatives, for the sake of the ancestors, and for other ritual purposes.
Baudh1.2.4.7-7/ If he cannot find anyone else from whom to beg, he should beg from the wife of his own <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), or else from his own mother.
Baudh1.2.4.7-8/ The seventh day should not pass without his having begged.
Baudh1.2.4.7-9ab/ There is fault in not going for <s>bhaikṣa</s> (alms), and in not kindling the sacred fire;
Baudh1.2.4.7-9cd/ Having failed to do this for seven nights, one should perform the <s>avakīrṇi-vrata</s> (penance for a lapsed student).

body.text: Baudh1.2.4.7-10/ tam evaṃ vidvāṃsam evaṃ carantaṃ sarve vedā (āviśanti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.2.4.7-10/ Him who knows thus and conducts himself thus — all the <s>Vedas</s> enter.

body.text: Baudh1.2.4.8/ yathā ha vā agniḥ samiddho (rocate^evaṃ ha vai^eṣa (snātvā(rocate ya evaṃ vidvān brahmacaryaṃ (carati^iti brāhmaṇam / itibrāhmaṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.2.4.8/ Just as a fire, when kindled, blazes forth, so indeed does one who has bathed (graduated) blaze forth — one who, knowing thus, practises <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship): thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (text). Thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.3.5.1/ atha snātakasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.1/ Now, the rules for the <s>snātaka</s> (Vedic graduate).

body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.2/ An undergarment and an upper garment.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.6/ A turban, a deerskin as upper garment, sandals, a parasol, and the <s>upāsana</s> (worship) of the <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices).

body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.9/ He should seek to obtain uncooked food from <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>rathakāras</s> (chariot-makers).

body.text: Baudh1.3.5.10/ bhaikṣaṃ vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.10/ Or <s>bhaikṣa</s> (alms-food).

body.text: Baudh1.3.5.11/ vāgyatas (tiṣṭhet //

body.text: Baudh1.3.5.12/ sarvāṇi ca^asya deva.pitṛ.saṃyuktāni pākayajña.saṃsthānibhūtikarmāni (kurvīta^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.12/ And he should perform all <s>pākayajña</s> (domestic sacrifice) rites connected with the gods and ancestors, as well as rites for prosperity.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.3.5.13/ By this rule, the supreme <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) of <s>Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin</s> attain the highest goal — thus says <s>Baudhāyana</s>.

Baudh1.4.6.2-1ab/ In the right ear of a goat, in the right hand of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
Baudh1.4.6.2-1cd/ in water and in a bunch of <s>kuśa</s> grass — fire is declared to reside.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.6.3/ Therefore, after performing purification, one should wipe with the hand; encircling with fire is beneficial. 'Blaze up, O <s>Jātavedas</s>' — thus it is distinguished by re-kindling.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.6.3/ If one suspects that something therein has been contaminated, one should kindle <s>kuśa</s> grass or other grass and burn around it clockwise.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.6.5/ For those polluted by urine, excrement, blood, semen, and the like — abandonment (of the vessel).

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.6.6/ When the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water vessel) is broken, one should offer a hundred oblations with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), or recite them.

body.text:
Baudh1.4.6.7-1/ bhūmir bhūmim (agān mātā mātaram apy (agāt / (bhūyāsmaputraiḥ paśubhir yo no (dveṣṭi sa (bhidyatām iti // [= Asṣṣ 3.14.12, Apṣṣ30.20.9, ApṃP 2.15.17; cf. ṣadvBaudh 1.6.20, Kausṣṣ 30.20.9, Kausṣ 136.2]

Baudh1.4.6.7-1/ 'Earth has gone to earth, mother has gone to mother; may we prosper with offspring and cattle; may he who hates us be destroyed' — thus.
Baudh1.4.6.7-2/ Having gathered the fragments and thrown them into water, and having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (mantra) ten times at minimum, one should take another (vessel).

Baudh1.4.6.9ab/ śūdrād (gṛhya śataṃ (kuryād vaiśyād ardhaśataṃ smṛtam /

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.6.14/ One who has sprinkled his hands and feet with water from the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water vessel) — as long as they remain wet, he is impure for others. He purifies only himself. One should not perform any other rite — thus it is known.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.6.15/ Or, with each act of purification, one is pure up to the wrist — thus says <s>Baudhāyana</s>.

Baudh1.4.7.1-1ab/ The <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water vessel) was ordained of old for the twice-born for the purpose of purification,
Baudh1.4.7.1-1cd/ by <s>Brahman</s> and the chief sages; therefore one should always carry it.

Baudh1.4.7.1-2ab/ tataḥ śaucaṃ tataḥ pānaṃ saṃdhyā.upāsanam eva ca /
Baudh1.4.7.1-2cd/ nir.viśaṅkena kartavyaṃ yadi^(icchet ^śreya ātmanaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.4.7.1-2ab/ From it comes purification, from it comes drinking, and the <s>sandhyā-upāsana</s> (twilight worship) as well;
Baudh1.4.7.1-2cd/ these should be performed without hesitation, if one desires one's own welfare.

body.text: Baudh1.4.7.2/ (kuryāt^śuddhena manasā na cittaṃ (dūṣayed budhaḥ / sahakamaṇḍalunā^utpannaḥ svayaṃ.bhūs tasmāt kamaṇḍalunā (caret [^ācaret]//
body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.7.2/ One should perform (rites) with a pure mind; the wise one should not corrupt the mind. The Self-existent One (<s>Svayambhū</s>) was born together with the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s>; therefore one should conduct oneself with the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.4.7.3/ mūtra.purīṣe kurvan dakṣiṇe haste (gṛhṇāti savya ācamanīyam/ etat (sidhyati sādhūnām //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.7.3/ When answering the calls of nature, one holds (the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) in the right hand, and water for sipping in the left. This practice succeeds for the virtuous.

body.text:
Baudh1.4.7.4ab/ yathā hi soma.saṃyogāc camaso medhya (ucyate /

body.translated_text:
Baudh1.4.7.4ab/ Just as the <s>camasa</s> (sacrificial cup) is called pure through its contact with <s>Soma</s>,
Baudh1.4.7.4cd/ so too the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water vessel) is always pure through its contact with water.

body.text: Baudh1.4.7.5/ pitṛ.deva.agni.kāryeṣu tasmāt taṃ (parivarjayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.7.5/ Therefore one should avoid it (the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) in rites for the ancestors, the gods, and the sacred fire.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.7.6/ Therefore, without the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s>, one should not travel a road, nor cross a boundary, nor go from house to house.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.7.7/ One should not go even a single step, or (as some say) an arrow's distance, without it.

body.translated_text: Baudh1.4.7.8/ If one desires the continuity of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) — thus says <s>Baudhāyana</s>.

Baudh1.5.8.1/ Now, the rules regarding <s>śauca</s> (purification).

Baudh1.5.8.2ab/ adbhiḥ (śudhyanti gātrāṇi buddhir jñānena (śudhyati /
