Baudh1.5.8.2ab/ The limbs are purified by water; the intellect is purified by knowledge;
Baudh1.5.8.2cd/ the soul of beings is purified by non-violence; the mind is purified by truth — thus.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.3/ manaḥ.śuddhir antaḥ.śaucam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.3/ Purity of mind is internal purification.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.4/ bahiḥ.śaucaṃ (vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.4/ We shall explain external purification.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.5/ kauśaṃ sautraṃ vā tris.trivṛd yajñopavītam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.5/ The <s>yajñopavīta</s> (sacred thread) should be made of silk or cotton, threefold and thrice-twisted.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.6/ ā nābheḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.6/ It should reach down to the navel.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.7/ dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum (uddhṛtya savyam (avadhāya śiras^(avadadhyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.7/ Raising the right arm and lowering (the thread under) the left, one should place it over the head.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.8/ viparītaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.8/ The reverse for rites to the ancestors.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.9/ kaṇṭhe^avasaktaṃ nivītam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.9/ Hung around the neck is the <s>nivīta</s> (garland-fashion wearing).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.10/ adhas^avasaktaṃ adhovītam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.10/ Hung below is the <s>adhovīta</s> (low-hanging fashion).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.11/ prāṅ.mukha udaṅ.mukho vā^āsīnaḥ śaucam (ārabheta śucau deśedakṣiṇam bāhuṃ jānu.antarā (kṛtvā (prakṣālya pādau pāṇī ca^āmaṇibandhāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.11/ Sitting facing east or facing north, one should begin purification in a clean place, placing the right arm between the knees, and washing the feet and hands up to the wrist.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.12/ pāda.prakṣālana.uccheṣaṇena na^(ācāmet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.12/ One should not sip water (<s>ācamana</s>) with the residual water from washing the feet.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.13/ yady (ācāmed bhūmau (srāvayitvā^(ācāmet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.13/ If one does sip, one should pour it on the ground first and then sip.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.14/ brāhmeṇa tīrthena^(ācāmet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.14/ One should perform <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) with the <s>brāhma tīrtha</s> (the base of the thumb).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.15/ aṅguṣṭha.mūlaṃ brāhmaṃ tīrtham //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.15/ The base of the thumb is the <s>brāhma tīrtha</s> (sacred part for <s>Brahman</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.16/ aṅguṣṭha.agraṃ pitryam aṅguly.agraṃ daivam aṅguli.mūlam ārṣam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.16/ The tip of the thumb is the <s>pitrya</s> (sacred part for ancestors); the tip of the fingers is the <s>daiva</s> (sacred part for gods); the base of the fingers is the <s>ārṣa</s> (sacred part for sages).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.17/ na^aṅgulībhir na sa.budbudābhir na sa.phenābhir na^uṣṇābhirna kṣārābhir na lavaṇābhir na kaluṣābhir na vivarṇābhir nadur.gandha.rasābhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.17/ Not with the fingers (cupped), not with water containing bubbles, not with foam, not with hot water, not with alkaline water, not with salty water, not with turbid water, not with discoloured water, not with water of bad smell or taste.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.18/ na hasan na jalpan na tiṣṭhan na vilokayan na prahvo na praṇatona mukta.śikho na prāvṛta.kaṇṭho na veṣṭita.śirā na tvaramāṇona^ayajñopavītī na prasārita.pādo na baddha.kakṣyo na bahir.jānuḥśabdam akurvan //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.18/ Not laughing, not chatting, not standing, not looking around, not bending forward, not bowing down, not with hair untied, not with the throat covered, not with the head wrapped, not in haste, not without the sacred thread, not with feet outstretched, not with the garment tucked up, not with knees apart — making no sound.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.19/ trir apo hṛdayaṃ.gamāḥ (pibet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.19/ One should drink water three times, (such that it) reaches the heart.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.20/ triḥ (parimṛjet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.20/ One should wipe (the lips) three times.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.21/ dvir ity eke //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.21/ Twice, according to some.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.22/ sakṛd ubhayaṃ śūdrasya striyāś ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.22/ Once each (sipping and wiping) for a <s>śūdra</s> and a woman.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.8.23-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.8.23-2ab/ gatābhir hṛdayaṃ vipraḥ kaṇṭhyābhiḥ kṣatriyaḥ śuciḥ /
Baudh1.5.8.23-2cd/ vaiśyas^adbhiḥ prāśitābhiḥ (syāt strī.śūdrau (spṛśyaca^antataḥ // iti //

Baudh1.5.8.24ab/ dantavad danta.sakteṣu dantavat teṣu dhāraṇāt /
Baudh1.5.8.24cd/ srasteṣu teṣu na^(ācāmet teṣāṃ saṃsrāvavat^śuciḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.5.8.24ab/ As long as particles cling to the teeth, (one is considered as still having) teeth (in them) and must retain (the water);
Baudh1.5.8.24cd/ when they have fallen away, one should not sip again; one is pure like the residual flow — thus.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.8.25-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.8.25-2ab/ dantavad danta.lagneṣu yac ca^apy antar mukhe (bhavet /
Baudh1.5.8.25-2cd/ ācāntasya^avaśiṣṭaṃ syān nigirann eva tat^śuciḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.5.8.25-1/ And now they cite (the following):
Baudh1.5.8.25-2ab/ As long as particles cling to the teeth and whatever remains inside the mouth,
Baudh1.5.8.25-2cd/ if it is a remnant after <s>ācamana</s> (sipping), one is pure even while swallowing it — thus.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.26/ khāny adbhiḥ (saṃspṛśya pādau nābhiṃ śiraḥ savyaṃ pāṇimantataḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.26/ After touching the orifices (of the body) with water — the feet, the navel, the head, and finally the left hand.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.27/ taijasaṃ ced (ādāya^ucchiṣṭī (syāt tad(udasya^(ācamya^ādāsyann adbhiḥ (prokṣet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.27/ If, having taken a metal vessel, one becomes <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (impure from eating), one should set it aside, perform <s>ācamana</s>, and before taking it up again, sprinkle it with water.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.28/ atha ced annena^ucchiṣṭī (syāt tad (udasya^(ācamya^ādāsyannadbhiḥ (prokṣet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.28/ And if one becomes <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (impure) through food, one should set it aside, perform <s>ācamana</s>, and before taking it up again, sprinkle it with water.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.29/ atha ced adbhir ucchiṣṭī (syāt tad (udasya^ācamya^ādāsyannadbhiḥ (prokṣet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.29/ And if one becomes <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (impure) through water, one should set it aside, perform <s>ācamana</s>, and before taking it up again, sprinkle it with water.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.30/ etad eva viparītam amatre //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.30/ The reverse procedure applies for earthen vessels.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.31/ vānaspatye vikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.31/ For wooden vessels, there is an option (between the two methods).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.32/ taijasānām ucchiṣṭānāṃ gośakṛn.mṛd.bhasmabhiḥ parimārjanamanyatamena vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.32/ For metal vessels that have become <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (impure), cleansing is done with cow dung, earth, or ashes — or with any one of them.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.33/ tāmra.rajata.suvarṇānām amlaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.33/ For copper, silver, and gold vessels — with acidic substances.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.34/ amatrāṇāṃ dahanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.34/ For earthen vessels — burning (in fire).

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.35/ dāravāṇāṃ takṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.35/ For wooden vessels — planing.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.36/ vaiṇavānāṃ gomayena //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.36/ For bamboo vessels — with cow dung.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.37/ phalamayānāṃ go.vāla.rajjvā //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.37/ For vessels made of fruit (gourds) — with a rope of cow hair.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.38/ kṛṣṇa.ajinānāṃ bilva.taṇḍulaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.38/ For black antelope skins — with <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) seeds.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.39/ kutapānām ariṣṭaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.39/ For woollen blankets (<s>kutapa</s>) — with <s>ariṣṭa</s> (soapberry) fruits.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.40/ aurṇānām ādityena //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.40/ For woollen (garments) — by exposure to sunlight.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.41/ kṣaumāṇāṃ gaura.sarṣapa.kalkena //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.41/ For linen garments — with a paste of white mustard seeds.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.42/ mṛdā celānām //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.42/ For cloth garments — with earth.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.43/ cela.vac carmaṇām //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.5.8.43/ For leather — in the same manner as for cloth.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.44/ taijasa.vad upala.maṇīnām //
body.translated_text: For articles made of stone and gems, [purification is] like that of metal objects.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.45/ dāru.vad asthnām //
body.translated_text: For articles made of bone, [purification is] like that of wooden objects.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.46/ kṣauma.vat^śaṅkha.śṛṅga.śukti.dantānām //
body.translated_text: For articles made of linen, conch, horn, mother-of-pearl, and ivory, [purification is] like that of linen.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.47/ payasā vā //
body.translated_text: Or [purification may be done] with milk.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.48/ cakṣur.ghrāṇa.ānukūlyād vāmūtra.purīṣa.asṛj.śukra.kuṇapa.spṛṣṭānāṃ pūrva.uktānām anyatamenatriḥsapta.kṛtvaḥ parimārjanam //
body.translated_text: For objects [among] the previously mentioned [categories] that have been touched by urine, feces, blood, semen, or a corpse, and are pleasing to the eye and nose—wiping twenty-one times with one of [the prescribed substances].

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.49/ ataijasānām evaṃ.bhūtānām utsargaḥ //
body.translated_text: For non-metallic objects that have been [contaminated] in this way, [the rule is] abandonment.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.50/ vacanād yajñe camasa.pātrānām //
body.translated_text: By [Vedic] injunction, [this rule does not apply to] the <s>camasa</s> and <s>pātra</s> vessels [used] in sacrifice.

body.text: Baudh1.5.8.51/ na somena^ucchiṣṭā (bhavanti^iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: "They are not rendered impure by <s>Soma</s>"—so says the <s>Śruti</s>.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.8.52ab/ kālas^agnir manasaḥ śuddhir udaka.ādy.upalepanam /
Baudh1.5.8.52cd/ avijñātaṃ ca bhūtāṇāṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ śaucam (ucyate // iti //
body.translated_text: Time, fire, purification of the mind, anointing with water and the like, and the unknown [purification] of beings—purification is declared to be sixfold.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.8.53-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.8.53-2/ kālaṃ deśaṃ tathā^ātmānaṃ dravyaṃ dravya.prayojanam /upapattim avasthāṃ ca (vijñāya śaucaṃ śauca.jñaḥ kuśalo dharma.īpsuḥ(samācaret //
body.translated_text: And furthermore they cite: "Having ascertained the time, place, one's own [condition], the substance, the purpose of the substance, the logical basis, and the circumstance, the knower of purity, skilled and desirous of <s>dharma</s>, should practice purification."

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.1ab/ nityaṃ śuddhaḥ kāru.hastaḥ paṇyaṃ yac ca prasāritam /
Baudh1.5.9.1cd/ brahmacāri.gataṃ bhaikṣaṃ nityaṃ medhyam iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: The hand of an artisan is always pure; merchandise that is displayed [for sale is pure]; alms received by a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) are always ritually clean—so says the <s>Śruti</s>.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.2ab/ vatsaḥ prasnavane medhyaḥ śakuniḥ phala.śātane /
Baudh1.5.9.2cd/ striyaś ca rati.saṃsarge śvā mṛga.grahaṇe śuciḥ //
body.translated_text: A calf is ritually clean in the act of suckling; a bird in the act of making fruit fall; women in the act of sexual intercourse; and a dog in the act of catching game—these are pure.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.3ab/ ākarāḥ śucayaḥ sarve (varjayitvā surā.karam /
Baudh1.5.9.3cd/ adūṣyāḥ saṃtatā dhārā vāta.udbhūtāś ca reṇavaḥ //
body.translated_text: All mines are pure, except a liquor-distillery. Continuous flowing streams are not defiled, nor are dust particles raised by the wind.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.4ab/ amedhyeṣu ca ye vṛkṣā uptāḥ puṣpa.phala.upagāḥ /
Baudh1.5.9.4cd/ teṣām api na (duṣyanti puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca //
body.translated_text: Even trees that are planted in impure [places] and bear flowers and fruits—their flowers and fruits are not defiled.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.5ab/ caitya.vṛkṣaṃ citiṃ yūpaṃ caṇḍālaṃ veda.vikrayam /
Baudh1.5.9.5cd/ etāni brāhmaṇaḥ spṛṣṭvā sa.celo jalam (āviśet //
body.translated_text: Having touched a sacred tree, a funeral pyre, a sacrificial post, a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, or the selling of the <s>Veda</s>—a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should enter water with his clothes on.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.6ab/ ātma.śayyā.āsanaṃ vastraṃ jāyā.apatyaṃ kamaṇḍaluḥ /
Baudh1.5.9.6cd/ śucīny ātmana etāni pareṣām aśucīni tu //
body.translated_text: One's own bed, seat, garment, wife, offspring, and water-vessel are pure for oneself; but they are impure for others.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.7ab/ āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ nāvaḥ pathi tṛṇāni ca /
Baudh1.5.9.7cd/ caṇḍāla.patita.spṛṣṭaṃ mārutena^eva (śudhyati //
body.translated_text: A seat, bed, vehicle, boat, and grass on the road—if touched by a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> or an outcast, they are purified by the wind alone.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.8ab/ khalakṣetreṣu yad dhānyaṃ kūpa.vāpīṣu yaj jalam /
Baudh1.5.9.8cd/ abhojyād api tad bhojyaṃ yac ca goṣṭha.gataṃ payaḥ //
body.translated_text: Grain in threshing-floors and fields, water in wells and tanks—these are fit to eat even from one from whom food is [normally] not to be accepted; likewise, milk obtained from the cow-pen.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.9ab/ trīṇi devāḥ pavitrāṇi brāhmaṇānām (akalpayan /
Baudh1.5.9.9cd/ adṛṣṭam adbhir nirṇiktaṃ yac ca vācā (praśasyate //
body.translated_text: Three things the gods have ordained as purifiers for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>: what is unseen [by defilers], what is washed with water, and what is praised by speech.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.9.10ab/ āpaḥ pavitraṃ bhūmi.gatā go.tṛptir yāsu (jāyate /
Baudh1.5.9.10cd/ avyāptāś ced amedhyena gandha.varṇa.rasa.anvitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Waters on the ground are purifiers—those from which cattle drink to satisfaction—provided they are not pervaded by impurity, and retain [their natural] smell, color, and taste.

body.text: Baudh1.5.9.11/ bhūmes tu saṃmārjana.prokṣaṇa.upalepana.avastaraṇa.ullekhanairyathā.sthānaṃ doṣa.viśeṣāt prāyatyam //
body.translated_text: For the ground, purification is through sweeping, sprinkling, anointing, covering, and scraping, according to the place and according to the specific fault—[this constitutes] the expiation.

body.text: Baudh1.5.9.12/ atha^apy (udāharanti //
body.translated_text: And furthermore they cite:

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.1ab/ go.carma.mātram ab.bindur bhūmeḥ (śudhyati pātitaḥ /
Baudh1.5.10.1cd/ samūḍham asamūḍhaṃ vā yatra^amedhyaṃ na (lakṣyate // iti //
body.translated_text: A drop of water the size of a cow-hide, falling on the ground, purifies it—whether the impurity has been removed or not removed—wherever impurity is not [visibly] perceived.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.2/ parokṣam adhiśritasya^annasya^avadyotya.abhyukṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For cooked food that has been [contaminated] out of sight, [the purification is] drying off and sprinkling with water.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.3/ tathā^āpaṇeyānāṃ ca bhakṣāṇām //
body.translated_text: The same for eatables from the market.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.4/ bībhatsavaḥ śuci.kāmā hi devā na^aśraddadhānasya havir(juṣanta iti //
body.translated_text: For the gods are fastidious and desirous of purity; they do not partake of the oblation of one without faith.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.5-1ab/ śucer aśraddadhānasya śraddadhānasya ca^aśuceḥ /
Baudh1.5.10.5-1cd/ (mīmāṃsitvā^ubhayaṃ devāḥ samam annam (akalpayan //
body.translated_text: "Between the food of one who is pure but without faith, and one who has faith but is impure, having weighed both, the gods ordained the food equal."

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.5-2ab/ prajāpatis tu tān (āha na samaṃ viṣamaṃ hi tat /
Baudh1.5.10.5-2cd/ hatam aśraddadhānasya śraddhā.pūtaṃ (viśiṣyate // iti //
body.translated_text: "But <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them: 'It is not equal; it is unequal. The [offering] of one without faith is destroyed; that which is purified by faith is superior.'"

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.6-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.10.6-2ab/ aśraddhā paramaḥ pāpmā śraddhā hi paramaṃ tapaḥ /
Baudh1.5.10.6-2cd/ tasmād aśraddhayā dattaṃ havir na^(aśnanti devatāḥ //
body.translated_text: And furthermore they cite: "Lack of faith is the greatest sin; faith is the greatest austerity (<s>tapas</s>). Therefore the gods do not partake of an oblation given without faith."

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.7/ (iṣṭvā (dattvā^api vā mūrkhaḥ svargaṃ nahi sa (gacchati //
body.translated_text: A fool, even having sacrificed and given, does not go to heaven.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.8ab/ śaṅkā.vihata.cāritro yaḥ sva.abhiprāyam āśritaḥ /
Baudh1.5.10.8cd/ śāstra.atigaḥ smṛto mūrkho dharma.tantra.uparodhanāt // iti //
body.translated_text: "One whose conduct is marred by doubt, who relies on his own opinion, and who transgresses the <s>śāstra</s>—he is considered a fool, because he obstructs the system of <s>dharma</s>."

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.9/ śāka.puṣpa.phala.mūla.oṣadhīnāṃ tu prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: For vegetables, flowers, fruits, roots, and herbs—washing [is the purification].

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.10/ śuṣkaṃ tṛṇam ayājñikaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ loṣṭaṃ vā(tiraskṛtya^ahorātrayor udag.dakṣiṇā.mukhaḥ (pravṛtya śira (uccared(avamehed vā //
body.translated_text: Having placed dry grass, non-sacrificial wood, a clod of earth, or [similar material] as a screen, facing north or south, one should relieve oneself day or night.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.11/ mūtre mṛdā^adbhiḥ prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: For urine, [purification is] wiping with earth and then washing with water.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.12/ triḥ pāṇeḥ //
body.translated_text: Three times for the hand.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.13/ tadvat purīṣe //
body.translated_text: The same for feces.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.14/ paryāyāt tris triḥ pāyoḥ pāṇeś ca //
body.translated_text: Alternately, three times each for the posterior and the hand.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.15/ mūtra.vad retasa utsarge //
body.translated_text: For the emission of semen, [purification is] the same as for urine.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.16/ nīvīṃ (visrasya (paridhāya^apa (upaspṛśet //
body.translated_text: Having loosened the lower garment and then retying it, one should sip water (<s>ācamana</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.17/ ārdraṃ tṛṇaṃ gomayaṃ bhūmiṃ vā (samupaspṛśet //
body.translated_text: One should touch wet grass, cow-dung, or the ground.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.18/ nābher adhaḥ sparśanaṃ karma.yukto (varjayet //
body.translated_text: One engaged in ritual work should avoid touching below the navel.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.19/ ūrdhvaṃ vai puruṣasya nābhyai medhyam avācīnam amedhyam itiśrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: "Above the navel of a person is ritually clean; below is ritually unclean"—so says the <s>Śruti</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.20/ śūdrāṇām ārya.adhiṣṭhitānām ardhamāsi māsi vā vapanamārya.vadācamana.kalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: For <s>Śūdras</s> under the supervision of <s>Āryas</s>: shaving every half-month or month; the rules for sipping water (<s>ācamana</s>) are as for <s>Āryas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.21/ vaiśyaḥ kusīdam (upajīvet //
body.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> should live by money-lending.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.22/ pañcaviṃśatis tv eva pañca.māṣikī (syāt //
body.translated_text: But twenty-five [<s>paṇas</s> should yield] five <s>māṣas</s> [as interest].

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.23-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.10.23-2ab/ yaḥ samargham ṛṇaṃ (gṛhya mahā.arghaṃ (saṃprayojayet /
Baudh1.5.10.23-2cd/ sa vai vārddhuṣiko nāma sarva.dharmeṣu garhitaḥ //
body.translated_text: And furthermore they cite: "He who, having borrowed a loan at one rate, lends it at a higher rate—he is called a usurer (<s>vārddhuṣika</s>), condemned in all <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.23-3ab/ vṛddhiṃ ca bhrūṇa.hatyāṃ ca tulayā (samatolayat /
Baudh1.5.10.23-3cd/ (atiṣṭhad bhrūṇa.hā koṭyāṃ vārddhuṣiḥ (samakampata // iti //
body.translated_text: "[The sages] weighed usury and embryo-killing on a balance: the embryo-killer hung at the tip [being lighter], while the usurer [being heavier] shook [the balance]."

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.24ab/ gorakṣakān vāṇijakāṃs tathā kāru.kuśīlavān /
Baudh1.5.10.24cd/ preṣyān vārddhuṣikāṃś caiva viprān^śūdra.vad (ācaret //
body.translated_text: Cowherds, merchants, artisans, actors, servants, and usurers—<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [of these occupations] should be treated like <s>Śūdras</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.10.25/ kāmaṃ tu parilupta.kṛtyāya kadaryāya nāstikāya pāpīyasepūrvau (dadyātām //
body.translated_text: But [gifts] may freely be given even to one whose duties have lapsed, to a miser, to an unbeliever, or to a wicked person—the first two [categories of gifts apply].

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.26ab/ ayajñena^avivāhena vedasya^utsādanena ca /
Baudh1.5.10.26cd/ kulāny akulatāṃ (yānti brāhmaṇa.atikrameṇa ca //
body.translated_text: Through not performing sacrifice, not performing marriage, the neglect of <s>Veda</s>-study, and transgression against <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>—families go to a state of non-family.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.27ab/ brāhmaṇa.atikramo na^(asti mūrkhe mantra.vivarjite /
Baudh1.5.10.27cd/ jvalantam agnim (utsṛjya nahi bhasmani (hūyate //
body.translated_text: There is no transgression against a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [who is] a fool devoid of <s>mantras</s>; for one does not offer oblations in ashes, having abandoned a blazing fire.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.28ab/ gobhir aśvaiś ca yānaiś ca kṛṣyā rāja.upasevayā /
Baudh1.5.10.28cd/ kulāny akulatāṃ (yānti yāni hīnāni mantrataḥ //
body.translated_text: With cattle, horses, vehicles, agriculture, and service of the king,

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.29ab/ mantratas tu samṛddhāni kulāny alpa.dhanāny api /
Baudh1.5.10.29cd/ kula.saṃkhyāṃ ca (gacchanti (karṣanti ca mahad.yaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: even families of little wealth that are rich in <s>mantras</s> enter the count of [worthy] families and gain great renown.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.30ab/ vedaḥ kṛṣi.vināśāya kṛṣir veda.vināśinī /
Baudh1.5.10.30cd/ śaktimān ubhayaṃ (kuryād aśaktas tu kṛṣiṃ (tyajet //
body.translated_text: The <s>Veda</s> leads to the destruction of agriculture; agriculture leads to the destruction of the <s>Veda</s>. One who is capable should practice both; but one who is incapable should abandon agriculture.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.31ab/ na vai devān pīvaras^a.saṃyata.ātmā rorūyamāṇaḥ kakudī(samaśnute /
Baudh1.5.10.31cd/ calat.tundī rabhasaḥ kama.vādī kṛśāsa ity aṇavas tatra(yānti //
body.translated_text: "Indeed, the gods are not pleased with an unrestrained, corpulent, weeping, hump-backed [person]; the trembling-bellied, impetuous, desire-speaking, emaciated one—[only] the fine ones go there."

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.32ab/ yad yauvane (carati vibhrameṇa sad vā^asad vā yādṛśaṃ vāyadā vā /
Baudh1.5.10.32cd/ uttare ced vayasi sādhu.vṛttas tad eva^asya (bhavatina^itarāṇi //
body.translated_text: Whatever one practices in youth, through [youthful] error—whether good or bad, of whatever kind, whenever—if in later age one's conduct is virtuous, that alone is his, not the former [deeds].

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.33ab/ (śoceta manasā nityaṃ duṣkṛtāny anucintayan /
Baudh1.5.10.33cd/ tapasvī ca^apramādī ca tataḥ pāpāt (pramucyate //
body.translated_text: One should always grieve in mind, reflecting on one's misdeeds; being ascetic and vigilant, one is then freed from sin.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.10.34ab/ (spṛśanti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān /
Baudh1.5.10.34cd/ na tair ucchiṣṭa.bhāvaḥ (syāt tulyās te bhūmi.gaiḥ saha// iti //
body.translated_text: "The drops that touch the feet of one who performs <s>ācamana</s> (water-sipping) for others—there is no state of being left-over (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) from them; they are equal to [water drops] on the ground."

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.1/ sapiṇḍeṣv ā daśa.aham āśaucam iti janana.maraṇayor (adhikṛtya(vadanty ṛtvig.dīkṣita.brahmacāri.varjam //
body.translated_text: For <s>sapiṇḍas</s> (blood-relatives), impurity (<s>āśauca</s>) lasts ten days at birth and death—so they say; excluding the sacrificial priest, the consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>), and the <s>brahmacārin</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.2/ sapiṇḍatā tv ā saptamāt sapiṇḍeṣu //
body.translated_text: <s>Sapiṇḍa</s> relationship extends up to the seventh [generation] among <s>sapiṇḍas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.3/ ā sapta.māsād ā danta.jananād vā^udaka.upasparśanam //
body.translated_text: Up to seven months [of age], or until the appearance of teeth—[the purification is merely] touching water.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.4ab/ piṇḍa.udaka.kriyā prete na^atrivarṣe (vidhīyate /
Baudh1.5.11.4cd/ ā danta.jananād vā^api dahanaṃ ca na (kārayet //
body.translated_text: "The offering of rice-balls and water for the deceased is not prescribed for one not yet three years old; until the appearance of teeth, cremation too should not be performed."

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.5/ aprattāsu ca kanyāsu //
body.translated_text: And for unmarried girls [the impurity period is also brief].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.6/ prattāsv eke ha (kurvate //
body.translated_text: Some perform [the full rites] for married [girls] too.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.7/ loka.saṃgrahaṇa.arthaṃ hi tad amantrāḥ striyo matāḥ //
body.translated_text: For the purpose of maintaining social order, women are considered [ritually] without <s>mantras</s>.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.8ab/ strīṇām akṛta.vivāhānāṃ try.ahāt^(śudhyanti bāndhavāḥ /
Baudh1.5.11.8cd/ yathā^uktena^eva kalpena (śudhyanti ca sanābhaya iti //
body.translated_text: "The relatives of unmarried women are purified after three days; and the <s>sanābhi</s> (close blood-relations) are purified according to the previously stated rule."

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.9/ api ca prapitāmahaḥ pitāmahaḥ pitā svayaṃ sodaryā bhrātaraḥsavarṇāyāḥ putraḥ pautraḥ prapautras tat.putra.varjaṃ teṣāṃ caputra.pautram avibhakta.dāyam sapiṇḍān (ācakṣate //
body.translated_text: And furthermore: the great-grandfather, grandfather, father, oneself, full brothers, the son of a wife of the same <s>varṇa</s>, grandson, and great-grandson—excluding their sons—they declare these, together with sons and grandsons of undivided inheritance, to be <s>sapiṇḍas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.10/ vibhakta.dāyān api sakulyān (ācakṣate //
body.translated_text: Those of divided inheritance they declare to be <s>sakulyas</s> (clan-members).

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.11/ asatsv anyeṣu tad.gāmī hy artho (bhavati //
body.translated_text: In the absence of other [heirs], the property goes to them.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.12/ sapiṇḍa.abhāve sakulyaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the absence of <s>sapiṇḍas</s>, the <s>sakulya</s> [inherits].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.13/ tad.abhāve pitā^ācāryo^antevāsy ṛtvig vā (haret //
body.translated_text: In their absence, the father, the teacher, the pupil, or the sacrificial priest takes [the property].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.14/ tad.abhāve rājā tat.svaṃ [K: satsvaṃ] traividya.vṛddhebhyaḥ(saṃprayacchet //
body.translated_text: In their absence, the king should distribute that property to learned elders versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.15/ na tv eva kadā cit svayaṃ rājā brāhmaṇa.svam (ādadīta //
body.translated_text: But the king should never himself take the property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.16-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.11.16-2ab/ brahma.svaṃ putra.pautra.ghnaṃ viṣam ekākinaṃ (haret /
Baudh1.5.11.16-2cd/ na viṣaṃ viṣam ity (āhur brahma.svaṃ viṣam (ucyate //
body.translated_text: And furthermore they cite: "The property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> destroys sons and grandsons; poison kills only one person. They do not call poison 'poison'—the property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is called poison."

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.16-3/ tasmād rājā brāhmaṇa.svaṃ na^(ādadīta / paramaṃ hy etadviṣaṃ yad brāhmaṇa.svam iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore a king should not take the property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; for the property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is the supreme poison.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.17/ janana.maraṇayoḥ (saṃnipāte samāno daśa.rātraḥ //
body.translated_text: When birth and death coincide, the same ten-day [impurity period applies].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.18/ atha yadi daśa.rātrāḥ (saṃnipateyur ādyaṃ daśa.rātramāśaucam ā navamād divasāt //
body.translated_text: And if [multiple] ten-day periods coincide, the first ten-day impurity [suffices], up to the ninth day.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.19/ janane tāvan mātā.pitror daśa.aham āśaucam //
body.translated_text: At birth, the impurity for both mother and father lasts ten days.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.20/ mātur ity eke tat.pariharaṇāt //
body.translated_text: Some say [it is] for the mother [alone], because of her [greater] involvement.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.21/ pitur ity apare śukra.prādhānyāt //
body.translated_text: Others say [it is] for the father, because of the primacy of the semen.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.22/ ayonijā hy api putrāḥ (śrūyante //
body.translated_text: For sons born not from the womb are also heard of [in the <s>Śruti</s>].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.23/ mātā.pitror eva tu saṃsarga.sāmānyāt //
body.translated_text: But [the impurity applies to] both mother and father, because of their common association.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.24/ maraṇe tu yathā.bālaṃ (puraskṛtya yajñopavītāny apasavyāni(kṛtvā tīrtham (avatīrya sakṛt sakṛt trir (nimajjya^(unmajjya^(uttīrya^(ācamya tat.pratyayam udakam (āsicya^ata eva^uttīrya^(ācamya gṛha.dvāryaṅgāram udkam iti (saṃspṛśya^a.kṣāra.lavaṇa.āśino daśa.ahaṃ kaṭam(āsīran //
body.translated_text: In the case of death, [one should observe the following]: placing the young one at the front, making the sacred threads left-to-right (<s>apasavya</s>), descending to the water (<s>tīrtha</s>), plunging and emerging three times each, coming out, sipping water (<s>ācamana</s>), pouring water [as offering] with [proper] intent for the deceased, coming out again and sipping water, touching charcoal and water at the house-door—they should sit on a mat for ten days, eating food without alkali or salt.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.25/ ekādaśyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ vā śrāddha.karma //
body.translated_text: On the eleventh or twelfth day, the <s>śrāddha</s> ceremony (memorial rite) [should be performed].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.26/ śeṣa.kriyāyāṃ lokas^anuroddhavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the remaining observances, one should follow local custom.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.27/ atra^apy asapiṇḍeṣu yathā.āsannaṃ tri.rātram aho.rātrameka.aham iti (kurvīta //
body.translated_text: And here too, for non-<s>sapiṇḍa</s> [relatives], one should observe according to proximity: three nights, one day-and-night, or one day.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.28/ ācārya.upādhyāya.tat.putreṣu tri.rātram //
body.translated_text: For the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor), and their sons—three nights.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.29/ ṛtvijāṃ ca //
body.translated_text: And for <s>ṛtvijs</s> (officiating priests) also.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.30/ śiṣya.satīrthya.sabrahmacāriṣu tri.rātram aho.rātrameka.aham iti (kurvīta //
body.translated_text: For pupils, co-disciples (<s>satīrthya</s>), and fellow students (<s>sabrahmacārin</s>)—one should observe three nights, one day-and-night, or one day.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.31/ garbha.srāve garbha.māsa.saṃmitā rātrayaḥ strīṇām //
body.translated_text: In the case of a miscarriage, the [period of impurity for] women [is] nights equal to the months of pregnancy.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.32/ para.śava.upasparśane^an.abhisaṃdhi.pūrvaṃ sa.celas^apaḥ(spṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ śuddho (bhavati //
body.translated_text: If one touches another's corpse without intention, having touched water with one's garment on, one becomes pure immediately.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.33/ abhisaṃdhi.pūrvaṃ tri.rātram //
body.translated_text: If with intention—three nights [of impurity].

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.34/ ṛtumatyāṃ ca //
body.translated_text: And [the same] for a menstruating woman.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.35/ yas tato jāyate sas^abhiśasta iti vyākhyātāny asyaivratāni [K: bratāni] //
body.translated_text: The one who is born from that [union with a menstruating woman] is condemned—thus the observances for this are explained.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.36ab/ veda.vikrayiṇaṃ yūpaṃ patitaṃ citim eva ca /
Baudh1.5.11.36cd/ (spṛṣṭvā (samācaret snānaṃ Zvānaṃ caṇḍālam eva ca //
body.translated_text: Having touched a seller of the <s>Vedas</s>, a sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>), a fallen person, a funeral pyre, a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, or a dog, one should perform a bath.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.37ab/ brāhmaṇasya vraṇa.dvāre pūya.śoṇita.saṃbhave /
Baudh1.5.11.37cd/ kṛmir (utpadyate tatra prāyaścittaṃ kathaṃ (bhavet //
body.translated_text: If in the wound-opening of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, arising from pus and blood, a worm is produced—what should be the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation)?

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.38ab/ go.mūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśa.udakam /
Baudh1.5.11.38cd/ try.ahaṃ (snātvā ca (pītvā ca kṛmi.daṣṭaḥ śucir (bhavet //
body.translated_text: Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, and water [infused with] <s>kuśa</s> grass— having bathed and drunk [these] for three days, one bitten by worms becomes pure.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.39/ śunā^upahataḥ sa.celas^(avagāheta //
body.translated_text: One contaminated by a dog should immerse [in water] with one's garment on.

body.text: Baudh1.5.11.40/ (prakṣālya vā taṃ deśam agninā saṃspṛśya punaḥ prakṣālyapādau ca^(ācamya prayato (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Or, having washed that spot, touching it with fire, washing again, and washing the feet, and sipping water (<s>ācamana</s>)—one becomes purified.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.41-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.5.11.41-2ab/ śunā daṣṭas tu yo vipro nadīṃ gatvā samudra.gām /
Baudh1.5.11.41-2cd/ prāṇa.āyāma.śataṃ kṛtvā ghṛtaṃ (prāśya (viśudhyati //
body.translated_text: And moreover, they cite: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> bitten by a dog, having gone to a river flowing to the ocean, having performed a hundred <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls), and having consumed ghee—becomes purified.

body.text:
Baudh1.5.11.41-3ab/ suvarṇa.rajatābhyāṃ vā gavāṃ śṛṅga.udakena vā /
Baudh1.5.11.41-3cd/ navaiś ca kalaśaiḥ snātvā sadya eva śucir bhavet // iti //
body.translated_text: Or, having bathed with [water poured from] gold, silver, water [poured over] cow-horns, or with nine new jars—one becomes pure immediately. Thus [ends the section].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.1/ abhakṣyāḥ paśavo grāmyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Domestic animals are not to be eaten.

body.text: Baudh1.5Baudh1.5.12.2/ kravyādāḥ śakunayaś ca //
body.translated_text: And carnivorous birds [are also not to be eaten].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.3/ tathā kukkuṭa.sūkaram //
body.translated_text: Likewise chicken and pork.

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.4/ anyatra^aja.avibhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Except for goat and sheep.

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.5/ bhakṣyāḥ śvāvid.godhā.śaśa.śalyaka.kacchapa.khaṅgāḥkhaṅga.varjāḥ pañca pañcanakhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Edible [animals] are: porcupine, iguana, hare, hedgehog, tortoise, and rhinoceros— five five-nailed animals excluding the rhinoceros [in some lists].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.6/ tathā^ṛśya.hariṇa.pṛṣata.mahiṣa.varāha.kuluṅgāḥkuluṅga.varjāḥ pañca dvikhuriṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Likewise: black deer (<s>ṛśya</s>), spotted deer (<s>hariṇa</s>), <s>pṛṣata</s> (dappled deer), buffalo, boar, and <s>kuluṅga</s> (a type of antelope)—five two-hoofed animals excluding the <s>kuluṅga</s> [in some lists].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.7/ pakṣiṇas.tittiri.kapota.kapiñjala.vārdhrāṇasa.mayūra.vāraṇāvāraṇa.varjāḥ pañca viṣkirāḥ //
body.translated_text: Birds: partridge (<s>tittiri</s>), pigeon (<s>kapota</s>), francolin (<s>kapiñjala</s>), crane (<s>vārdhrāṇasa</s>), and peacock (<s>mayūra</s>), and <s>vāraṇa</s>—five scratching-birds (<s>viṣkirā</s>) excluding the <s>vāraṇa</s> [in some lists].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.8/ matsyāḥ sahasradaṃṣṭraś cilicimovarmi.bṛhacchiro.maśakari.rohita.rājīvāḥ //
body.translated_text: Fish: the thousand-toothed, <s>cilicima</s>, the armored one (<s>varmin</s>), big-headed (<s>bṛhacchiras</s>), <s>maśakari</s>, <s>rohita</s>, and <s>rājīva</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.9/ anirdaśāha.saṃdhinī.kṣīram apeyam //
body.translated_text: The milk of a cow within ten days [of calving] and of one with a divided [afterbirth] is not to be drunk.

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.10/ vivatsa.anyavatsayoś ca //
body.translated_text: And [the milk] of one whose calf has died or one suckling another's calf [is also not to be drunk].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.11/ āvikam auṣṭrikam aikaśapham apeyam //
body.translated_text: Sheep's [milk], camel's [milk], and that of one-hoofed animals are not to be drunk.

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.12/ apeya.payaḥ.pāne kṛcchro^anyatra gavyāt //
body.translated_text: For drinking the milk of those whose milk is forbidden—a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance), except for cow's [milk].

body.text:
Baudh1.5.12.13/ gavye tu tri.rātram upavāsaḥ /
Baudh1.5.12.14/ paryuṣitaṃśāka.yūṣa.māṃsa.sarpiḥ.śṛtadhānā.guḍa.dadhi.madhu.saktu.varjam //
body.translated_text: But for cow's [milk that is forbidden]—a three-night fast. Stale food is [forbidden], except for vegetables, broth, meat, ghee, cooked grain, <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), curds, honey, and flour.

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.15/ śuktāni tathā.jāto guḍaḥ //
body.translated_text: Fermented [foods are also forbidden]; likewise <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) produced in that manner [by fermentation].

body.text: Baudh1.5.12.16/ śrāvaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyām āṣāḍhyāṃ vā^(upākṛtya taiṣyāṃmāghyāṃ vā^(utsṛjeyuḥ / (utsṛjeyuḥ //
body.translated_text: Having begun [the Vedic study] on the full moon of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> or <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, they should suspend [it] on [the full moon of] <s>Taiṣa</s> or <s>Māgha</s>. They should suspend [it].

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.1/ śucim adhvaraṃ devā (juṣante //
body.translated_text: The gods enjoy the sacrifice that is pure.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.2/ śuci.kāmā hi devāḥ śucayaś ca //
body.translated_text: For the gods desire purity and are themselves pure.

body.text:
Baudh1.6.13.3-1/ tad eśā^(abhivadati / [om.]
Baudh1.6.13.3-2ab/ śucī vo havyā marutaḥ śucīnāṃ śuciṃ (hinomy adhvaraṃśucibhyaḥ /
Baudh1.6.13.3-2cd/ ṛtena satyam ṛtasāpa (āyan^śuci.janmānaḥ śucayaḥpāvakāḥ // iti // (ṛV 7.56.12)
Baudh1.6.13.4-1/ ahataṃ vāsasāṃ śuci /
Baudh1.6.13.4-2/ tasmād yat kiṃ ca^ijyā.saṃyuktaṃ (syāt sarvaṃ tad ahatairvāsobhiḥ (kuryāt //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, this [<s>ṛc</s>] proclaims: 'Pure are your oblations, O <s>Maruts</s>, for the pure ones; pure is the sacrifice I impel for the pure ones. By <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order) they attained truth through <s>ṛta</s>; pure-born, pure, purifying' (<s>ṚV</s> 7.56.12). An unworn garment is pure. Therefore, whatever is connected with the sacrifice—all that should be done with unworn garments.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.5/ prakṣālita.upavātāny akliṣṭāni vāsāṃsi patnī.yajamānāvṛtvijaś ca (paridadhīran //
body.translated_text: Washed, aired [in the wind], and unstained garments should be worn by the wife, the sacrificer, and the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests).

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.6/ evaṃ prakramād ūrdhvam //
body.translated_text: Likewise from the beginning of the ceremony onward.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.7/ dīrgha.someṣu sattreṣu ca^evam //
body.translated_text: In extended <s>Soma</s> [sacrifices] and <s>sattras</s> (sessions)—likewise.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.8/ yathā.samāmnātaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: And as traditionally handed down.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.9/ yathā^etad abhicaraṇīyeṣv iṣṭi.paśu.someṣu lohita.uṣṇīṣālohita.vāsasaś ca^ṛtvijaḥ (pracareyuś citra.vāsasaś citra.āsaṅgāvṛṣākapāv iti ca //
body.translated_text: Just as in sorcery-rites (<s>abhicāra</s>), animal sacrifices, and <s>Soma</s> rites—the <s>ṛtvijs</s> should officiate wearing red turbans and red garments, and wearing variegated garments and variegated ornaments for the <s>vṛṣākapāva</s> [rite], and so forth.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.10/ agnyādhāne kṣaumāṇi vāsāṃsi teṣām alābhe kārpāsikānyaurṇāni vā (bhavanti //
body.translated_text: At the establishment of the sacred fire (<s>agnyādhāna</s>), the garments should be of linen; in their absence, cotton or wool may be used.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.11/ mūtra.purīṣa.lohita.retaḥ.prabhṛty.upahatānāṃ mṛdā^adbhiriti prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: For [items] contaminated by urine, excrement, blood, semen, and the like—purification is by [scrubbing with] earth and [rinsing with] water.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.12/ vāsovat tārpya.valkalānām [K: vṛkalānām] //
body.translated_text: For [articles of] bark-fibre and bark—[purification is] like that of garments.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.13/ valkalavat kṛṣṇa.ajinānām //
body.translated_text: For black antelope skins—like that of bark.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.14/ na parihitam adhirūḍham aprakṣālitaṃ prāvaraṇam //
body.translated_text: One should not [use as] an outer covering [anything] that has been [previously] worn, mounted upon, or not washed.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.15/ na^apalpūlitaṃ manuṣya.saṃyuktaṃ devatrā (yuñjyāt //
body.translated_text: One should not employ for divine [purposes anything] that is unwashed and has been in contact with humans.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.16/ ghanāyā bhūmer upaghāta upalepanam //
body.translated_text: For hard ground, when contaminated—smearing [with cow-dung] is [the purification].

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.17/ suṣirāyāḥ karṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For hollow [or loose] ground—digging [and removal of the soil].

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.18/ klinnāyā medhyam (āhṛtya pracchādanam //
body.translated_text: For wet [ground]—bringing pure [earth] and covering [it].

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.19/ caturbhiḥ śudhyate bhūmir gobhir ākramaṇāt khananāddahanād abhivarṣaṇāt //
body.translated_text: Ground is purified in four ways: by cows [treading on it], by digging, by burning, and by rain.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.20/ pañcamāc ca^upalepanāt ṣaṣṭhāt kālāt //
body.translated_text: And fifth, by smearing [with cow-dung]; sixth, by [the passage of] time.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.21/ asaṃskṛtāyāṃ bhūmau nyastānāṃ tṛṇānāṃ prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: Grass placed on unconsecrated ground—[requires] washing.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.22/ parokṣa.upahatānām abhyukṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For [items] contaminated out of sight—sprinkling [is the purification].

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.23/ evaṃ kṣudra.samidhām //
body.translated_text: Likewise for small kindling-sticks.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.24/ mahatāṃ kāṣṭhānām upaghāte prakṣālya^avaśoṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For large pieces of wood, when contaminated—washing and [then] drying.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.25/ bahūnāṃ tu prokṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: But for many [pieces]—[merely] sprinkling.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.26/ dārumayāṇāṃ pātrāṇām ucchiṣṭa.samanvārabdhānāmavalekhanam //
body.translated_text: For wooden vessels that have come into contact with leavings (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>)—scraping.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.27/ ucchiṣṭa.lepa.upahatānām avatakṣaṇam ///
body.translated_text: For those contaminated by smears of leavings—planing.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.28/ mūtra.purīṣa.lohita.retaḥ.prabhṛty.upahatānām utsargaḥ //
body.translated_text: For those contaminated by urine, excrement, blood, semen, and the like—discarding.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.29/ tad etad anyatra nirdeśāt //
body.translated_text: But this [rule applies] except where [otherwise] specified.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.30/ yathā^etad agnihotre gharmocchiṣṭe ca dadhigharme cakuṇḍapāyinām ayane ca^utsargiṇām ayane ca dākṣāyaṇa.yajñeca^iḍādadhe(ceḍādadhe) [K: caiḍādadhe] ca catuścakre ca brahmaudaneṣu cateṣu sarveṣu darbhair adbhiḥ prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: Just as in the <s>Agnihotra</s>, in the <s>Gharma</s> leavings, in the <s>Dadhigharma</s> [rite], in the <s>Kuṇḍapāyin</s> rite, in the session of the <s>Utsargins</s>, in the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice, in the <s>Iḍā</s>-<s>Dadhi</s> [rite], in the <s>Catuścakra</s>, and in the <s>Brahmaudana</s> [rites]—in all these, purification is by [scrubbing with] <s>darbha</s> grass and [rinsing with] water.

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.31/ sarveṣv eva soma.bhakṣeṣv adbhir eva mārjālīye prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: In all <s>Soma</s> vessels (<s>somabhakṣa</s>)—purification is with water alone in the <s>Mārjālīya</s> [shed].

body.text: Baudh1.6.13.32/ mūtra.purīṣa.lohita.retaḥ.prabhṛty.upahatānām utsargaḥ //
body.translated_text: For those contaminated by urine, excrement, blood, semen, and the like—discarding.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.1/ mṛnmayānāṃ pātrāṇām ucchiṣṭa.samanvārabdhānām avakūlanam //
body.translated_text: For earthen vessels that have come into contact with leavings—turning upside down.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.2/ ucchiṣṭa.lepa.upahatānāṃ punar.dahanam //
body.translated_text: For those contaminated by smears of leavings—re-firing.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.3/ mūtra.purīṣa.lohita.retaḥ.prabhṛty.upahatānām utsargaḥ //
body.translated_text: For those contaminated by urine, excrement, blood, semen, and the like—discarding.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.4/ taijasānāṃ pātrāṇāṃ pūrvavat parimṛṣṭānāṃ prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: For metal vessels—washing after being first wiped clean, as before.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.5/ parimārjana.dravyāṇi gośakṛn.mṛd.bhasma^iti //
body.translated_text: The materials for wiping are: cow dung, earth, and ashes.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.6/ mūtra.purīṣa.lohita.retaḥ.prabhṛty.upahatānāṃ punar.karaṇam //
body.translated_text: For those contaminated by urine, excrement, blood, semen, and the like—re-making [by melting down].

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.7/ gomūtre vā sapta.rātraṃ pariśāyanaṃ mahā.nadyāṃ vā [K:vaivam] //
body.translated_text: Or soaking in cow's urine for seven nights, or [immersing] in a great river—likewise.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.8/ evam aśmamayānām //
body.translated_text: Likewise for stone [vessels].

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.9/ alābu.bilva.vināḍānāṃ govālaiḥ parimārjanam //
body.translated_text: For [vessels of] gourd, <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), and bamboo-tubes—wiping with cow-tail hairs.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.10/ naḍa.veṇu.śara.kuśa.vyūtānāṃ gomayena^adbhir iti prakṣālanam //
body.translated_text: For [articles] woven from reed, bamboo, <s>śara</s> grass, and <s>kuśa</s> grass—washing with cow dung and water.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.11/ vrīhīṇām upaghāte prakṣālya.avaśoṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For rice grains, when contaminated—washing and drying.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.12/ bahūnāṃ tu prokṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: But for many [grains]—[merely] sprinkling.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.13/ taṇḍulānām utsargaḥ //
body.translated_text: For husked rice (<s>taṇḍula</s>)—discarding.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.14/ evaṃ siddha.haviṣām //
body.translated_text: Likewise for cooked oblations (<s>siddhahavis</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.15/ mahatāṃ śva.vāyasa.prabhṛty.upahatānāṃ taṃ deśaṃpuruṣa.annam uddhṛtya / pavamānaḥ suvarjana iti /etena^anuvākena^abhyukṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: For large [quantities of grain] contaminated by dogs, crows, and the like—removing that portion [along with] a man's [measure of] food, and sprinkling with the <s>anuvāka</s> (hymn section) '<s>pavamānaḥ suvarjana</s>' (the purifying one, the good separator).

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.16/ madhu.udake payo.vikāre ca pātrāt pātra.antara.ānayaneśaucam //
body.translated_text: For honey-water and milk-products, transferring from vessel to vessel constitutes purification.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.17/ evaṃ taila.sarpiṣī ucchiṣṭa.samanvārabdheudake^(avadhāya^(upayojayet //
body.translated_text: Likewise, oil and ghee that have come into contact with leavings should be placed in water and [then] used.

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.18/ amedhya.abhyādhāne (samāropya^agniṃ (mathitvā pavamāneṣṭiḥ //
body.translated_text: When impure [substances] are placed upon [the fire], one should pile up the fire, produce [new fire] by friction, and [perform] the <s>Pavamāneṣṭi</s> (purificatory sacrifice).

body.text: Baudh1.6.14.19/ śauca.deśa.mantra.āvṛd.artha.dravya.saṃskāra.kāla.bhedeṣupūrva.pūrva.prādhānyam / pūrva.pūrva.prādhānyam //
body.translated_text: In the distinctions of place of purification, <s>mantra</s>, repetition, substance, meaning, purificatory preparation, and time—the preceding [factor] takes precedence over the following. The preceding takes precedence over the following.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.1/ uttarata upacāro vihāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Movement and dwelling [should be conducted] toward the north.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.2/ tathā^apavargaḥ //
body.translated_text: Likewise the conclusion [of rites].

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.3/ viparītaṃ pitryeṣu //
body.translated_text: The reverse [applies] in rites for the ancestors (<s>pitṛ</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.4/ pāda.upahataṃ (prakṣālayet //
body.translated_text: What is trampled by the foot should be washed.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.5/ aṅgam upaspṛśya sicaṃ vā^apa (upaspṛśet //
body.translated_text: Having touched a limb or a sieve (?), one should touch water.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.6/ evaṃchedana.bhedana.khanana.nirasana.pitrya.rākṣasa.nairṛta.raudra.abhicaraṇīyeṣu //
body.translated_text: Likewise in [rites involving] cutting, splitting, digging, casting away, and in ancestral, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Nairṛta</s>, <s>Raudra</s>, and sorcery rites.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.7/ na mantravatā yajña.aṅgena^ātmānam (abhipariharet //
body.translated_text: One should not apply to oneself a sacrificial implement that bears a <s>mantra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.8/ abhyantarāṇi yajña.aṅgāni //
body.translated_text: The internal [implements are] sacrificial implements.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.9/ bāhyā ṛtvijaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) are external.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.10/ patnī.yajamānāv ṛtvigbhyo^antaratamau //
body.translated_text: The wife and sacrificer are more internal than the <s>ṛtvijs</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.11/ yajña.angebhya ājyam ājyād^havīṃṣi havirbhyaḥ paśuḥ paśoḥsomaḥ somād agnayaḥ //
body.translated_text: [In order of sanctity:] from sacrificial implements, <s>ājya</s> (ghee); from <s>ājya</s>, oblations (<s>havis</s>); from oblations, the animal (<s>paśu</s>); from the animal, <s>Soma</s>; from <s>Soma</s>, the sacred fires.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.12/ yathā.karma^ṛtvijo na (vihārād abhiparyāvarteran //
body.translated_text: The <s>ṛtvijs</s>, according to their [respective] duties, should not turn back from [the direction of] movement.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.13/ prāṅ.mukhaś ced dakṣiṇam aṃsam (abhiparyāvarteta //
body.translated_text: If facing east, one should turn toward the right (south) shoulder.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.14/ pratyaṅ.mukhaḥ savyam //
body.translated_text: If facing west—toward the left.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.15/ antareṇa cātvāla.utkarau yajñasya tīrtham //
body.translated_text: The <s>tīrtha</s> (passage) of the sacrifice [lies] between the pit (<s>cātvāla</s>) and the mound (<s>utkara</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.16/ a.cātvāla āhavanīya.utkarau //
body.translated_text: Without a pit—[the passage lies] between the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] and the mound.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.17/ tataḥ kartāro yajamānaḥ patnī ca (prapadyeran //
body.translated_text: From there, the agents—the sacrificer and [his] wife—should approach.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.18/ visaṃsthite //
body.translated_text: [This applies] when [the sacrifice is] not concluded.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.19/ saṃsthite ca saṃcaro^an.utkara.deśāt [K: 'nūtkaradeśāt] //
body.translated_text: When concluded, passage [is allowed] from a place other than the mound.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.20/ na^aprokṣitam aprapannaṃ klinnaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ samidhaṃvā^(abhyādadhyāt //
body.translated_text: One should not place on [the fire any] fuel-wood or kindling that is unsprinkled, not approached [ritually], or wet.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.21/ agreṇa^āhavanīyaṃ brahma.yajamānau (prapadyete //
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s> [priest] and the sacrificer approach in front of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.22/ jaghanena^āhavanīyam ity eke //
body.translated_text: Behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s>—according to some.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.23/ dakṣiṇena^āhavanīyaṃ brahma.āyatanaṃ tad.apareṇa yajamānasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.23/ The seat of <s>Brahman</s> (the Brahman priest) is to the south of the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), and behind that is the seat of the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.24/ uttarāṃ śroṇim uttareṇa hotuḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.24/ The seat of the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) is to the north of the northern hip (of the altar).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.25/ utkara āgnīdhrasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.25/ The rubbish heap is the seat of the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindling priest).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.26/ jaghanena gārhapatyaṃ patnyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.26/ The seat of the wife is behind the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.27/ teṣu kāle.kāla [K: kāle kāla] eva darbhān (saṃstṛṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.27/ On those seats, he strews <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) at the proper time. [K: at each proper time]

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.28/ ekaikasya ca^uda.kamaṇḍalur upāttaḥ (syād ācamana.arthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.28/ And for each one, a water vessel (<s>udakamaṇḍalu</s>) should be kept ready for the purpose of sipping water (<s>ācamana</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.29/ vrata.upeto dīkṣitaḥ (syāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.29/ One who has undertaken a vow should be consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.30/ na para.pāpaṃ (vaden na (krudhyen na (roden mūtra.purīṣena^(avekṣeta //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.30/ He should not speak of another's sin, should not become angry, should not weep, and should avoid looking at urine and excrement.

body.text: Baudh1.7.15.31/ amedhyaṃ (dṛṣṭvā (japati / abaddhaṃ mano daridraṃ cakṣuḥsūryo jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭho dīkṣe mā mā hāsīr iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.7.15.31/ If he sees something impure, he recites: "My mind is unbound, my eye is poor; <s>Sūrya</s> is the best of lights — O <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration), do not abandon me."

body.text:
Baudh1.7.15.32/ atha yady enam (abhivarṣati / undatīr balaṃ dhattaujo dhattabalaṃ dhatta mā me dīkṣāṃ mā tapo (nirvadhiṣṭa^iti // [K om.]
Baudh1.8.16.1/ catvāro varṇā brāhmaṇa.kṣatriya.viṭ.śūdrāḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.7.15.32/ And if it rains upon him, he recites: "O waters, bestow strength, bestow vigor, bestow strength — do not destroy my <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) or my <s>tapas</s> (austerity)." [K omits this]
Baudh1.8.16.1/ There are four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes): <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.2/ teṣāṃ varṇa.anupūrvyeṇa catasro bhāryā brāhmaṇasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.2/ Among them, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> may have four wives, in accordance with the order of the <s>varṇas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.3/ tisro rājanyasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.3/ A <s>Kṣatriya</s> may have three.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.4/ dve vaiśyasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.4/ A <s>Vaiśya</s> may have two.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.5/ ekā śūdrasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.5/ A <s>Śūdra</s> may have one.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.6/ tāsu putrāḥ savarṇa.anantarāsu savarṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.6/ Among those wives, the sons born of wives of the same <s>varṇa</s> or of the next lower <s>varṇa</s> are of the same <s>varṇa</s> as the father.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.7/ ekāntara.dvyantarāsv ambaṣṭha.Ugra.niṣādāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.7/ From wives one or two <s>varṇas</s> removed in the natural order (anuloma), the offspring are <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, and <s>Niṣāda</s> respectively.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.8/ pratilomāsv āyogava.māgadha.vaiṇa.kṣattṛ[K:kṣattu].pulkasa.kukkuṭa.vaidehaka.caṇḍālaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.8/ From unions in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>), the offspring are: <s>Āyogava</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, <s>Vaiṇa</s>, <s>Kṣattṛ</s> [K: <s>Kṣattu</s>], <s>Pulkasa</s>, <s>Kukkuṭa</s>, <s>Vaidehaka</s>, and <s>Caṇḍāla</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.9/ ambaṣṭhāt prathamāyāṃ śvapākaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.9/ From an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> with a woman of the first (i.e., highest) class, a <s>Śvapāka</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.10/ ugrād dvitīyāyāṃ vaiṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.10/ From an <s>Ugra</s> with a woman of the second class, a <s>Vaiṇa</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.11/ niṣādāt tṛtīyāyāṃ pulkasaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.11/ From a <s>Niṣāda</s> with a woman of the third class, a <s>Pulkasa</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.12/ viparyaye kukkuṭaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.12/ In the reverse case, a <s>Kukkuṭa</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.13/ niṣādena niṣādyām ā pañcamāj jāto^(apahanti śūdratām //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.13/ A child born of a <s>Niṣāda</s> man and a <s>Niṣādī</s> woman removes the <s>Śūdra</s> status by the fifth generation.

body.text: Baudh1.8.16.14/ tam (upanayet ṣaṣṭhaṃ (yājayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.8.16.14/ One should perform the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) for him and have the sixth generation perform sacrifices.

Baudh1.8.16.15/ The seventh is of unaltered seed, of equal seed, equal — these designations apply in succession. [K combines with 1.8.16.14: One should perform the initiation for him and have the sixth perform sacrifices; the seventh becomes unaltered.]
Baudh1.8.16.16-1ab/ In the three <s>varṇas</s>, those whom one begets without observance of vows, being alike in appearance,
Baudh1.8.16.16-1cd/ those who have fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (initiation), the wise call <s>Vrātyas</s> (degraded ones). [K omits]
Baudh1.8.16.16-2/ The wise call them <s>Vrātyas</s>. [K omits]
Baudh1.9.17.1/ <s>Rathakāra</s> (chariot-maker), <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, <s>Āyogava</s>, <s>Vaiṇa</s>, <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, <s>Pulkasa</s>, <s>Kukkuṭa</s>, <s>Vaidehaka</s>, <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, <s>Śvapāka</s>, and so forth — these are the mixed castes. [K omits]
Baudh1.9.17.2/ Among them, the offspring from wives of the same class are of the same class.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.3/ brāhmaṇāt kṣatriyāyāṃ brāhmaṇo vaiśyāyām ambaṣṭhaḥśūdrāyāṃ niṣādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.3/ From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is born; with a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman, an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>; with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, a <s>Niṣāda</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.4/ pāraśava ity eke //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.4/ Some say a <s>Pāraśava</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.5/ kṣatriyād vaiśyāyāṃ kṣatriyaḥ śūdrāyām ugraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.5/ From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> with a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> is born; with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, an <s>Ugra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.6/ vaiśyāt^śūdrāyāṃ rathakāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.6/ From a <s>Vaiśya</s> with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, a <s>Rathakāra</s> (chariot-maker) is born.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.7/ śūdrād vaiśyāyāṃ māgadhaḥ kṣatriyāyāṃ kṣattābrāhmaṇyāṃ caṇḍālaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.7/ From a <s>Śūdra</s> with a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman, a <s>Māgadha</s> is born; with a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman, a <s>Kṣattṛ</s>; with a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.8/ vaiśyāt kṣatriyāyām āyogavo brāhmaṇyāṃ vaidehakaḥ /kṣatriyād brāhmaṇyāṃ sūtaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.8/ From a <s>Vaiśya</s> with a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman, an <s>Āyogava</s> is born; with a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, a <s>Vaidehaka</s>. From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> with a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, a <s>Sūta</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.9/ tatra[K: atra]^ambaṣṭha.ugrayoḥ saṃyoge (bhavati^anulomaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.9/ In that context [K: here], the union of <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> and <s>Ugra</s> produces offspring in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.10/ kṣattṛ.vaidehakayoḥ pratilomaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.10/ The union of <s>Kṣattṛ</s> and <s>Vaidehaka</s> produces offspring in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>).

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.11/ ugrāj jātaḥ kṣattryāṃ śvapākaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.11/ A child born of an <s>Ugra</s> with a <s>Kṣattṛ</s> woman is a <s>Śvapāka</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.12/ vaidehakād ambaṣṭhāyāṃ vaiṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.12/ From a <s>Vaidehaka</s> with an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> woman, a <s>Vaiṇa</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.13/ niṣadāt^śūdrāyāṃ pulkasaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.13/ From a <s>Niṣāda</s> with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, a <s>Pulkasa</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.14/ śūdrān niṣādyāṃ kukkuṭaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.14/ From a <s>Śūdra</s> with a <s>Niṣādī</s> woman, a <s>Kukkuṭa</s> is born.

body.text: Baudh1.9.17.15/ varṇa.saṃkarād utpannān vrātyān (āhur manīṣiṇaḥ /vrātyān (āhur manīṣiṇa iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.9.17.15/ The wise call those born from the intermixture of <s>varṇas</s> as <s>Vrātyas</s> (degraded ones). The wise call them <s>Vrātyas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.1/ ṣaḍbhāgabhṛto rājā (rakṣet prajāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.1/ The king, receiving a sixth share (of the produce as tax), should protect his subjects.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.2/ brahma vai svaṃ mahimānaṃ brāhmaṇeṣv (adadhādadhyayana.adhyāpana.yajana.yājana.dāna.pratigraha.saṃyuktaṃ vedānāṃguptyai //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.2/ <s>Brahman</s> (the supreme principle) placed its own greatness in the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, endowed with study, teaching, sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving, and receiving gifts — for the protection of the <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.3/ kṣatre balamadhyayana.yajana.dāna.śastra.kośa.bhūta.rakṣaṇa.saṃyuktaṃ kṣatrasyavṛddhyai //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.3/ In the <s>Kṣatra</s> (warrior class), it placed strength, endowed with study, sacrificing, giving, bearing weapons, guarding the treasury, and protecting beings — for the increase of the <s>Kṣatra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.4/ viṭsvadhyayana.yajana.dāna.kṛṣi.vāṇijya.paśupālana.saṃyuktaṃ karmaṇāṃvṛddhyai //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.4/ In the <s>Vaiśyas</s>, it placed study, sacrificing, giving, agriculture, trade, and cattle-rearing — for the increase of productive activities.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.5/ śūdreṣu pūrveṣāṃ paricaryām //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.5/ In the <s>Śūdras</s>, it placed the service of the preceding classes.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.6/ patto hy (aṣṛjyanta^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.6/ For they were created from the feet.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.7/ sarvatodhuraṃ purohitaṃ (vṛṇuyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.7/ He should choose as <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) one who is capable in all respects.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.8/ tasya śāsane (varteta //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.8/ He should abide by his counsel.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.9/ saṃgrāme na (nivarteta //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.9/ He should not turn back in battle.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.10/ na karṇibhir na digdhaiḥ (praharet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.10/ He should not strike with barbed or poisoned arrows.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.11/bhīta.matta.unmatta.pramatta.visaṃnāha.strī.bāla.vṛddha.brāhmaṇair na(yudhyeta //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.11/ He should not fight with those who are frightened, intoxicated, insane, distracted, disarmed, women, children, the aged, or <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.12/ anyatra^ātatāyinaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.12/ Except in the case of an <s>ātatāyin</s> (violent aggressor).

body.text:
Baudh1.10.18.13-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.10.18.13-2ab/ adhyāpakaṃ kule jātaṃ yo (hanyād ātatāyinam /
Baudh1.10.18.13-2cd/ na tena bhrūṇahā (bhavati manyus tan manyum (ṛcchati //iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.18.13-1/ And on this they also cite:
Baudh1.10.18.13-2ab/ He who kills a violent aggressor (<s>ātatāyin</s>), even one who is a teacher or of noble birth,
Baudh1.10.18.13-2cd/ does not thereby become a slayer of an embryo (<s>bhrūṇahan</s>); wrath meets with wrath.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.14/ sāmudra.śulko varaṃ rūpam (uddhṛtya daśa.paṇaṃ śatam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.14/ The maritime customs duty: having selected the best form (of goods), one hundred of ten <s>paṇas</s> each.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.15/ anyeṣām api sāra.anurūpyeṇa^(anupahatya dharmyaṃ (prakalpayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.15/ For other goods as well, he should levy a righteous tax proportionate to their value, without causing harm.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.16/ abrāhmaṇasya pranaṣṭasvāmikaṃ rikthaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ(paripālya rājā (haret //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.16/ The property of a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> whose owner cannot be found — after keeping it for a year, the king may take it.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.17/ avadhyo vai brāhmaṇaḥ sarva.aparādheṣu //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.17/ Indeed, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is not to be killed for any offense whatsoever.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.18/ brāhmaṇasyabrahmahatyā.gurutalpagamana.suvarṇasteya.surāpāneṣu kusindha.bhaga.sṛgāla.surādhvajāṃs taptena^ayasā lalāṭe^(aṅkayitvā viṣayān nirdhamanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.18/ For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guilty of killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, intercourse with a teacher's wife, theft of gold, or drinking <s>surā</s> (liquor) — having branded on his forehead with hot iron the marks of a headless trunk, a female organ, a jackal, or a liquor sign respectively, he should be banished from the realm.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.19/ kṣatriyādīnāṃ brāhmaṇa.vadhe vadhaḥ sarvasvaharaṇam ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.19/ For <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and others, the punishment for killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is death and confiscation of all property.

body.text: Baudh1.10.18.20/ teṣām eva tulya.apakṛṣṭa.vadhe yathā.balam anurūpāndaṇḍān (prakalpayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.18.20/ For those same classes, in the case of killing one of equal or lower rank, he should impose appropriate penalties according to their ability.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.1/ kṣatriya.vadhe go.sahasram ṛṣabha.adhikaṃ rājña (utsṛjedvaira.niryātana.artham [K: vairaniryātanām] //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.1/ For killing a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, one should release to the king a thousand cows with an additional bull, for the purpose of expiating enmity. [K: for the expiation of enmity]

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.2/ śataṃ vaiśye daśa śūdra ṛṣabhaś ca^atra^adhikaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.2/ A hundred for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, ten for a <s>Śūdra</s>, and in each case a bull in addition.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.3/ śūdra.vadhena strī.vadho go.vadhaś cavyākhyāto^anyatra^ātreyyā vadhād dhenv.anaḍuhoś ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.3/ By the rules for killing a <s>Śūdra</s>, the killing of a woman and the killing of a cow are also explained — except for the killing of an <s>Ātreyī</s> (woman descended from <s>Atri</s>) and of a milch cow or draught ox.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.4/ vadhe dhenv.anaḍuhor ante cāndrāyaṇaṃ (caret //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.4/ For the killing of a milch cow or draught ox, one should perform a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance) at the end.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.5/ ātreyyā vadhaḥ kṣatriya.vadhena vyākhyātaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.5/ The killing of an <s>Ātreyī</s> is explained by the rules for killing a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.6/haṃsa.bhāsa.barhiṇa.cakravāka.pracalāka.kāka.ulūka.maṇḍūka[K:kaṇṭaka].ḍiḍḍika[K: ḍiḍḍika.maṇḍūka].ḍerikā.śva.babhru.nakula.ādīnāṃvadhe śūdravat //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.6/ For killing a goose, a heron, a peacock, a <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy shelduck), a <s>pracalāka</s> (a type of bird), a crow, an owl, a frog [K: a thorny creature], a <s>ḍiḍḍika</s> (a type of bird) [K: <s>ḍiḍḍika</s> and frog], a <s>ḍerikā</s> (a type of bird), a dog, a mongoose, an ichneumon, and the like — the penalty is as for killing a <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.7/ loka.saṃgrahaṇa.arthaṃ yathā dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā sākṣīsākṣyaṃ (brūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.7/ For the benefit of maintaining social order, a witness should give testimony as he has seen or heard it.

body.text:
Baudh1.10.19.8-1ab/ pādo^adharmasya kartāraṃ pādo (gacchati sākṣiṇam /
Baudh1.10.19.8-1cd/ pādaḥ sabhāsadaḥ sarvān pādo rājānam (ṛcchati //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.19.8-1ab/ A quarter of the sin goes to the perpetrator, a quarter goes to the witness,
Baudh1.10.19.8-1cd/ a quarter to all the members of the assembly, and a quarter reaches the king.

body.text:
Baudh1.10.19.8-2ab/ rājā (bhavaty anenāś ca (mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ /
Baudh1.10.19.8-2cd/ eno (gacchati kartāraṃ yatra nindyo ha (nindyate //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.19.8-2ab/ The king becomes free from blame, and the members of the assembly are released,
Baudh1.10.19.8-2cd/ the sin goes to the perpetrator alone — when the blameworthy one is indeed blamed.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.9/ sākṣiṇaṃ ca^evam uddiṣṭaṃ yatnāt (pṛcched vicakṣaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.9/ And a discerning person should carefully examine the witness thus designated.

body.text:
Baudh1.10.19.10ab/ yāṃ rātrim (ajaniṣṭhās tvaṃ yāṃ ca rātriṃ (mariṣyasi /
Baudh1.10.19.10cd/ etayor antarā yat te sukṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ (bhavet /
Baudh1.10.19.10e(/ tat sarvaṃ rājagāmi (syād anṛtaṃ bruvatas tava //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.19.10ab/ "On whatever night you were born, and on whatever night you shall die,
Baudh1.10.19.10cd/ whatever merit you may have earned between these two,
Baudh1.10.19.10e/ all of that shall go to the king, if you speak falsely."

body.text:
Baudh1.10.19.11ab/ trīn eva ca pitqn (hanti trīn eva ca pitāmahān /
Baudh1.10.19.11cd/ sapta jātān ajātāṃś ca sākṣī sākṣyaṃ mṛṣā vadan //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.19.11ab/ "A false witness destroys three generations of fathers and three generations of grandfathers,
Baudh1.10.19.11cd/ seven born and those yet unborn — the witness who speaks false testimony."

body.text:
Baudh1.10.19.12-1ab/ hiraṇya.arthe anṛte (hanti trīn eva ca pitāmahān /
Baudh1.10.19.12-1cd/ pañca paśv.anṛte (hanti daśa (hanti gava.anṛte //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.19.12-1ab/ "By speaking falsely about gold, he destroys three generations of grandfathers;
Baudh1.10.19.12-1cd/ five by false testimony about cattle, ten by false testimony about cows."

body.text:
Baudh1.10.19.12-2ab/ śatam aśva.anṛte (hanti sahasraṃ puruṣa.anṛte /
Baudh1.10.19.12-2cd/ sarvaṃ bhūmy.anṛte (hanti sākṣī sākṣyaṃ mṛṣā vadan //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.10.19.12-2ab/ "A hundred by false testimony about horses, a thousand by false testimony about a man;
Baudh1.10.19.12-2cd/ everything by false testimony about land — the witness who speaks false testimony."

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.13/ catvāro varṇāḥ putriṇaḥ sākṣiṇaḥ (syur anyatraśrotriya.rājanya.pravrajita.mānuṣyahīnebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.13/ Members of all four <s>varṇas</s> who have sons may be witnesses, except for a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (Śrotriya), a prince (<s>Rājanya</s>), a wandering ascetic (<s>pravrajita</s>), and those devoid of humanity.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.14/ smṛtau pradhānataḥ pratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.14/ In matters of recollection, the determination should be based on what is primary.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.15/ ato^anyathā kartapatyam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.15/ Otherwise, it constitutes a miscarriage of justice.

body.text: Baudh1.10.19.16/ dvādaśa.rātraṃ taptaṃ payaḥ (pibet kūśmāṇḍair vā(juhuyād iti / kūśmāṇḍair vā (juhuyād iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.10.19.16/ For twelve nights, one should drink heated milk, or offer oblations with <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> mantras. Or one should offer oblations with <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> mantras.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.1/ aṣṭau vivāhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.1/ There are eight forms of marriage.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.2/ śruta.śīle (vijñāya brahmacāriṇe^arthine (dīyate sa brāhmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.2/ When a daughter is given to a man of learning and good character, a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) who seeks her — that is the <s>Brāhma</s> (marriage).

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.3/ (ācchādya^(alaṃkṛtya / eṣā saha dharmaś[K: dharmaṃ](caryatām iti / prājāptyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.3/ Having clothed and adorned her, saying "May she practice <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) together with you" — that is the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (marriage).

body.text:
Baudh1.11.20.4/ pūrvāṃ lājāhutiṃ (hutvā gobhyāṃ saha^ārṣaḥ // [K:pūrvāṃ lājāhutiṃ (hutvā go.mithunaṃ kanyāvate (dattvā grahaṇamārṣaḥ ]
Baudh1.11.20.5/ dakṣiṇāsu (nīyamānāsv antarvedy ṛtvije sa daivaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.11.20.4/ Having offered the first oblation of parched grain, along with a pair of cows — that is the <s>Ārṣa</s> (marriage). [K: Having offered the first oblation of parched grain and giving a pair of cows to the father of the bride, the taking of her hand is the <s>Ārṣa</s> marriage.]
Baudh1.11.20.5/ When she is led away during the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial fees) being distributed and given to a priest within the sacrificial enclosure — that is the <s>Daiva</s> (marriage).

body.text:
Baudh1.11.20.6/ dhanena^upatoṣyā^āsuraḥ // [K: sakāmena sakāmāyā mithassaṃyogo gāndharvaḥ]
Baudh1.11.20.7/ sakāmena sakāmāyā mithaḥ saṃyogo gāndharvaḥ // [K:dhanenopatoṣyāsuraḥ]
Baudh1.11.20.8/ prasahya haraṇād rākṣasaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.11.20.6/ When one wins her over by means of wealth — that is the <s>Āsura</s> (marriage). [K: The mutual union of a willing man and a willing woman is the <s>Gāndharva</s> marriage.]
Baudh1.11.20.7/ The mutual union of a willing man and a willing woman is the <s>Gāndharva</s> (marriage). [K: Winning her over by means of wealth is the <s>Āsura</s> marriage.]
Baudh1.11.20.8/ Forcible abduction is the <s>Rākṣasa</s> (marriage).

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.9/ suptāṃ mattāṃ pramattāṃ vā^(upagacched iti paiśācaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.9/ Approaching a woman who is asleep, intoxicated, or distracted — that is the <s>Paiśāca</s> (marriage).

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.10/ teṣāṃ catvāraḥ pūrve brāhmaṇasya teṣv api pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥśreyān //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.10/ Of these, the first four are prescribed for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and among those, each earlier one is more meritorious.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.11/ uttareṣām uttara uttaraḥ [K: uttarottaraḥ] pāpīyān //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.11/ Among the latter forms, each successive one is more sinful.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.12/ atra^api ṣaṣṭha.saptamau kṣatradharma.anugatautat.pratyayatvāt kṣatrasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.12/ Moreover, the sixth and seventh are in accordance with <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>dharma</s> (warrior duty), because they arise from the nature of the <s>Kṣatra</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.13/ pañcama.aṣṭamau vaiśya.śūdrāṇām //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.13/ The fifth and eighth are for <s>Vaiśyas</s> and <s>Śūdras</s>.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.14/ ayantrita.kalatrā hi vaiśya.śūdrā (bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.14/ For <s>Vaiśyas</s> and <s>Śūdras</s> are those whose wives are unrestrained,

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.15/ karṣaṇa.śuśrūṣā.adhikṛtatvāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.15/ because they are engaged in agriculture and service.

body.text: Baudh1.11.20.16/ gāndharvam apy eke (praśaṃsanti sarveṣāṃ sneha.anugatatvāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.20.16/ Some also praise the <s>Gāndharva</s> (marriage) for all, because it is accompanied by mutual affection.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.1/ yathā yukto vivāhas tathā yuktā prajā (bhavati^itivijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.1/ It is known that as the form of marriage is, so will the offspring be.

body.text:
Baudh1.11.21.2-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti / [K adds: sādhavas tripuruṣam ārṣāddaśa daivād daśa prājāpatyād daśa pūrvān daśa^aparān ātmānaṃ cabrāhmīputra iti (vijñāyate // veda.svīkaraṇa.śaktir apy evaṃvidhānāmeva putrāṇām (bhavati^iti //]
