body.translated_text:
Baudh1.11.21.2-1/ And they also cite [K adds: The virtuous purify three generations; from an <s>ārṣa</s> (marriage by sages' rite) ten, from a <s>daiva</s> (divine rite) ten, from a <s>prājāpatya</s> (rite of Prajāpati) ten ancestors and ten descendants, and oneself — thus is the son of a <s>brāhmī</s> (Brahma marriage) known. And the capacity to appropriate the Vedas belongs only to sons of such kinds.]
Baudh1.11.21.2-2/ A woman who is purchased with wealth is not regarded as a wife; she is not fit for the rite to the gods nor for the rite to the ancestors — <s>Kaśyapa</s> declared her a slave.

body.text:
Baudh1.11.21.3-1ab/ śulkena ye (prayacchanti svasutāṃ lobha.mohitāḥ /
Baudh1.11.21.3-1cd/ ātma.vikrayiṇaḥ pāpā mahā.kilbiṣa.kārakāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.3-1/ Those who give away their own daughter for a bride-price, deluded by greed, are sinful sellers of themselves, committers of great offence.

body.text:
Baudh1.11.21.3-2ab/ (patanti narake ghore (ghnanti ca^ā^saptamaṃ kulam /
Baudh1.11.21.3-2cd/ gamana.āgamanaṃ caiva sarvaṃ śulke (vidhīyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.3-2/ They fall into a terrible hell and destroy the family up to the seventh generation; and all transactions of coming and going are ordained in the matter of bride-price.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.4/paurṇamasy.aṣṭakā.amāvāsyā.agnyutpāta.bhūmikampa.śmaśāna.deśapati.śrotriya.ekatīrtha.prayāṇeṣv ahorātram anadhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.4/ On the occasions of the full moon, the <s>aṣṭakā</s> (eighth-day rite), the new moon, the outbreak of fire, an earthquake, at a cremation ground, on the arrival of the lord of the region, a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned Brahmin), a fellow-pilgrim, or on a journey — <s>anadhyāya</s> (suspension of Vedic study) lasts for a day and a night.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.5/ vāte pūti.gandhe nīhāre canṛtta.gīta.vāditra.rudita.sāma.śabdeṣu tāvantaṃ kālam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.5/ During wind, foul smell, or fog, and during the sounds of dancing, singing, musical instruments, weeping, or <s>Sāman</s> chanting — for the same duration of time.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.6/ stanayitnu.varṣa.vidyut.saṃnipāte tryaham anadhyāyo^anyatravarṣā.kālāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.6/ When thunder, rain, and lightning occur together, <s>anadhyāya</s> (suspension of Vedic study) lasts for three days, except during the rainy season.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.7/ varṣā.kāle^api varṣa.varjam ahorātrayoś ca tat.kālam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.7/ Even during the rainy season, except when it is actually raining; and during both day and night, for the duration of that time.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.8/ pitrya.pratigraha.bhojanayoś ca tad.divasa.śeṣam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.8/ And after eating at ancestral rites or upon receiving gifts — for the remainder of that day.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.9/ bhojaneṣv ā jaraṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.9/ After meals — until digestion is complete.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.10/ pāṇi.mukho hi brāhmaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.10/ For the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has his hand as his mouth.

body.text:
Baudh1.11.21.11-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh1.11.21.11-2ab/ bhuktaṃ pratigṛhītaṃ ca nirviśeṣam iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh1.11.21.11-1/ And they also cite:
Baudh1.11.21.11-2/ "What has been eaten and what has been received are without distinction" — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture).

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.12/ pitary[K: pitury] uparate tri.rātram //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.12/ When the father [K: father] has died — three nights.

body.text:
Baudh1.11.21.13/ dvayam u ha vai suśravaso^anūcānasya retobrāhmaṇasya^ūrdhvaṃ nābher adhastād anyat / sa yad ūrdhvaṃ nābhestena ha^etat (prajāyate yad brāhmaṇān (upanayati yad (adhyāpayati yad(yājayati yat sādhu (karoti / sarvā^asya^eṣā prajā (bhavati / atha yadavācīṇaṃ nābhes tena ha^asya^aurasī prajā (bhavati / tasmāt^śrotriyamanūcānam aprajo^asi^iti
na (vadanti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.13/ Twofold indeed is the seed of <s>Suśravas</s>, the learned one, of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: one above the navel and the other below. That which is above the navel — by that he procreates when he initiates <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, when he teaches, when he officiates at sacrifices, when he does good deeds. All this is his progeny. But that which is below the navel — by that his bodily offspring comes into being. Therefore they do not say to a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned Brahmin) and learned one: "You are without progeny."

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.14/ tasmād dvi.nāmā dvi.mukho vipro dvi.retā dvi.janmā ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.14/ Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is called "of two names, of two mouths, of two seeds, and of two births."

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.15/ śūdra.apapātra.śravaṇa.saṃdarśanayoś ca tāvantaṃ kālam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.15/ And upon hearing or seeing a <s>Śūdra</s> or an outcaste — for the same duration of time.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.16/ naktaṃ śivā.virāve na^(adhīyīta svapna.antam //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.16/ At night, when a jackal howls, one should not study — until the end of sleep.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.17/ ahorātrayoś ca saṃdhyayoḥ parvasu ca na^(adhīyīta //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.17/ And at the two twilight junctions of day and night, and on <s>parvan</s> days (lunar junction days), one should not study.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.18/ na māṃsam (aśnīyān na striyam (upeyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.18/ One should not eat meat, nor should one approach a woman.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.19/ parvasu hi rakṣaḥ.piśācā vyabhicāravanto (bhavanti^itivijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.19/ For it is known that on <s>parvan</s> days (lunar junction days), <s>Rakṣas</s> (demons) and <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls) become active in transgression.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.20/ anyeṣu ca^adbhuta.utpāteṣv ahorātram anadhyāyo^anyatramānasāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.20/ And on occasions of other extraordinary portents, <s>anadhyāya</s> (suspension of Vedic study) lasts for a day and a night, except for mental disturbance.

body.text: Baudh1.11.21.21/ mānase^api janana.maraṇayor anadhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh1.11.21.21/ Even in the case of mental disturbance, <s>anadhyāya</s> (suspension of study) applies on occasions of birth and death.

Baudh1.11.21.22-1/ And they also cite:
Baudh1.11.21.22-2/ The eighth day destroys the teacher, the fourteenth destroys the pupil,
the fifteenth destroys learning — therefore one should abstain on <s>parvan</s> days (lunar junction days).
Baudh1.11.21.22-3/ Therefore one should abstain on <s>parvan</s> days.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.1/ atha^ataḥ prāyaścittāni //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.1/ Now, henceforth, the <s>prāyaścittas</s> (expiations).

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.2/ bhrūṇahā dvādaśa samāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.2/ The killer of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>bhrūṇahan</s>) — twelve years.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.3/ kapālī khaṭvā.aṅgī gardabha.carma.vāsā araṇya.niketanaḥśmaśāne dhvajaṃ śava.śiraḥ (kṛtvā kuṭīṃ (kārayet / tām (āvaset /sapta.āgārāṇi bhaikṣaṃ caran svakarma^ācakṣāṇas tena prāṇān(dhārayet / alabdhvā^upavāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.3/ Carrying a skull, with a bedstead leg as his staff, wearing a donkey's skin, dwelling in the forest — he should make a hut in a cremation ground, having set up a banner with a dead man's skull. He should live in that. Begging food at seven houses, declaring his own deed, he should sustain his life by that. If he obtains nothing, he should fast.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.4/ aśvamedhena gosavena^agniṣṭutā vā (yajeta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.4/ Or he should perform the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), the <s>Gosava</s> (cow sacrifice), or the <s>Agniṣṭut</s> sacrifice.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.5/ aśvamedha.avabhṛthe vā^ātmānaṃ (pāvayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.5/ Or he should purify himself at the concluding bath of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (<s>avabhṛtha</s>).

body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.12/ For an <s>Ātreyī</s> (woman of the Atri lineage), the same as for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.13/ One who violates the teacher's bed should lie on a heated iron bed.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.14/ Or he should embrace a blazing iron pillar.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.15/ Or, having cut off his penis together with the testicles and placed them in his joined palms, he should walk toward the space between the southern and western directions until he falls down.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.16/ stenaḥ prakīrya keśān saidhrakam musalam (ādāya skandhenarājānaṃ (gacched anena māṃ jahi^iti / tena^enaṃ (hanyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.16/ A thief, having loosened his hair and carrying an iron club on his shoulder, should go to the king saying, "Strike me with this." The king should strike him with it.

body.text:
Baudh2.1.1.17-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.1.1.17-2ab/ skandhena^ādāya musalaṃ steno rājānam (anviyāt /
Baudh2.1.1.17-2cd/ anena (śādhi māṃ rājan kṣatra.dharmam anusmaran //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.1.17-1/ And they also cite:
Baudh2.1.1.17-2/ Carrying the club on his shoulder, the thief should follow the king, saying: "Punish me with this, O king, mindful of the duty of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> (warrior class)."

body.text:
Baudh2.1.1.17-3ab/ śāsane vā visarge vā steno (mucyeta kilbiṣāt /
Baudh2.1.1.17-3cd/ aśāsanāt tu tad rājā stenād āpnoti kilbiṣam // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.1.17-3/ Whether by punishment or by release, the thief is freed from guilt;
but if the king does not punish him, the king incurs the guilt of the thief.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.18/ surāṃ (pītvā^uṣṇayā kāyaṃ (dahet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.18/ Having drunk <s>surā</s> (liquor), one should burn one's body with hot liquor.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.19/ amatyā pāne kṛcchra.abda.pādaṃ (caret punar.upanayanaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.19/ For unintentional drinking, one should perform a quarter of a year's <s>kṛcchra</s> (severe penance), and undergo re-initiation (<s>punarupanayana</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.20/ vapana.vrata.niyama.lopaś ca pūrva.anuṣṭhitatvāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.20/ And there is loss of shaving, vows, and observances, because they had been previously performed.

Baudh2.1.1.21-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.1.1.21-2ab/ amatyā vāruṇīṃ (pītvā (prāśya mūtra.purīṣayoḥ /
Baudh2.1.1.21-2cd/ brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ punaḥ.saṃskāram (arhati //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.1.21-1/ And they also cite:
Baudh2.1.1.21-2/ Having unintentionally drunk <s>vāruṇī</s> (wine), or having consumed urine or excrement,
a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or <s>Vaiśya</s> deserves re-consecration.

body.text:
Baudh2.1.1.22ab/ surā.dhāne tu yo bhāṇḍe apaḥ paryuṣitāḥ (pibet /
Baudh2.1.1.22cd/ śaṅkhapuṣpī.vipakvena ṣaḍahaṃ kṣīreṇa (vartayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.22/ One who drinks stale water from a vessel that held <s>surā</s> (liquor) should subsist for six days on milk boiled with <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> (a medicinal plant).

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.23/ guru.prayuktaś cen (mriyeta gurus trīn kṛcchrāṃś (caret //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.23/ If one sent by the teacher dies, the teacher should perform three <s>kṛcchras</s> (severe penances).

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.24/ etad eva^asaṃskṛte //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.24/ The same applies for one who has not received the sacraments.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.25/ brahmacāriṇaḥ śava.karmaṇā vrata.āvṛttir anyatramātā.pitror ācāryāc ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.25/ For a <s>brahmacārin</s> (Vedic student), carrying out funeral rites entails a renewal of vows, except for the mother, father, or teacher.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.26/ sa ced (vyādhīyīta kāmaṃ guror ucchiṣṭaṃ bhaiṣajya.arthesarvaṃ (prāśnīyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.26/ If he falls ill, he may freely eat the teacher's leftover food for medicinal purposes — all of it.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.27/ yena^(icchet tena (cikitset //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.27/ He may seek treatment by whatever means he wishes.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.28/ sa yadā gadī (syāt tad (utthāya^ādityam (upatiṣṭheta[K:upatiṣṭhate] / haṃsaḥ śuciṣad iti / etayā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.28/ When he is afflicted with disease, he should rise and worship the sun [K: worships] with the hymn "<s>Haṃsaḥ śuciṣad</s>" (The swan dwelling in purity) — with this verse.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.29/ divā retaḥ (siktvā trir apo hṛdayaṃ.gamāḥ (pibed retasyābhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.29/ If semen is discharged during the day, one should drink water three times with the verses "<s>āpo hṛdayaṃgamāḥ</s>" (waters that go to the heart) and the "<s>retasya</s>" verses.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.30/ yo brahmacārī striyam (upeyāt so^avakīrṇī //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.30/ A <s>brahmacārin</s> (Vedic student) who approaches a woman is an <s>avakīrṇin</s> (one who has broken his vow of chastity).

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.31/ sa gardabhaṃ paśum (ālabheta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.31/ He should sacrifice a donkey as an animal offering.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.32/ nairṛtaḥ paśuḥ puroḍāśaś ca rakṣo.devato[K: .daivato]yama.devato[K: .daivato] vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.32/ The animal and the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice cake offering) are dedicated to <s>Nirṛti</s> [K: same deity] or to <s>Yama</s> [K: same deity].

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.33/ śiśnāt prāśitram apsv avadānaiś (caranti^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.33/ It is known that "from the penis comes the <s>prāśitra</s> (portion for tasting), and in the waters with the <s>avadānas</s> (cut portions) they proceed."

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.34/ api vā^amāvāsyāyāṃ niśy agnim (upasamādhāyadārvihomikīṃ[K: dāviṃhomikīṃ] pariceṣṭāṃ (kṛtvā dve ājya.āhutī(juhoti / kāma^avakīrṇo^(asmy avakīrṇo^(asmi kāma kāmāya svāhā /kāma^abhidrugdho^(asmy abhidrugdho^(asmi kāma kāmāya svāhā^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.34/ Alternatively, on the new moon night, having prepared the fire and performed the ritual procedure of the <s>dārvihoma</s> [K: dāvihoma] (oblation with a wooden ladle), one offers two oblations of ghee: "I who am overcome by desire, I am overcome — to <s>Kāma</s>, to desire, <s>svāhā</s>! I who am assailed by desire, I am assailed — to <s>Kāma</s>, to desire, <s>svāhā</s>!"

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.35/ (hutvā prayata.añjaliḥ kavātiryaṅṅ agnim (abhimantrayeta[K:upatiṣṭheta] / saṃ mā (siñcantu marutaḥ sam indraḥ saṃ bṛhaspatiḥ / saṃmā^ayam agniḥ siñcatv āyuṣā ca balena ca^āyuṣmantaṃ (karota mā^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.35/ Having offered, with joined hands in a reverent posture, one should address the fire sideways [K: worship]: "May the <s>Maruts</s> sprinkle me, may <s>Indra</s>, may <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; may this <s>Agni</s> sprinkle me with long life and with strength — make me endowed with long life!"

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.36/ atha^asya [K: atha yasya] jñātayaḥ pariṣady uda.pātraṃ(ninayeyur asāv aham itthaṃ.bhūta iti / (caritvā^apaḥ payo ghṛtaṃ madhulavaṇam ity ārabdhavantaṃ brāhmaṇā (brūyuś caritaṃ tvayā^iti / omiti^itaraḥ (pratyāha / carita.nirveśaṃ savanīyaṃ (kuryuḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.36/ Then his [K: then whose] kinsmen should bring a water-vessel to the assembly, saying: "I am so-and-so, of such a condition." Having performed the penance, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> should say to him who has undertaken water, milk, ghee, honey, and salt: "The penance has been performed by you." The other replies "Yes." They should perform the <s>savanīya</s> (Soma-pressing rite) as the completion of the penance.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.37/ sagotrāṃ ced amatyā^(upagacchen[K: upayacchen] mātṛvad enāṃ(bibhṛyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.37/ If one unintentionally approaches a woman of the same <s>gotra</s> (clan) [K: marries], he should maintain her as he would a mother.

body.text: Baudh2.1.1.38/ prajātā cet kṛcchra.abda.pādaṃ[K: .ṣādaṃ] (caritvā / yan maātmano mindā^(abhūt / punar agniś cakṣur (adād iti / etābhyāṃ(juhuyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.1.38/ If she has given birth, having performed a quarter of a year's <s>kṛcchra</s> [K: variant], he should offer oblations with these two verses: "That which was a blemish of my self" and "<s>Agni</s> again gave sight."

body.text:
Baudh2.1.1.39ab/ parivittaḥ parivettā yā ca^enaṃ (parivindati /
Baudh2.1.1.39cd/ sarve te narakaṃ (yānti dātṛ.yājaka.pañcamāḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.1.39/ The elder brother who remains unmarried while a younger marries (<s>parivitti</s>), the younger brother who marries before the elder (<s>parivettṛ</s>), the woman who marries the younger,
all of them go to hell, together with the giver and the officiating priest as the fifth.

body.text:
Baudh2.1.1.40ab/ parivittaḥ parivettā dātā yaś ca^api yājakaḥ /
Baudh2.1.1.40cd/ kṛcchra.dvādaśa.rātreṇa strī tri.rātreṇa (śudhyati // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.1.40/ The <s>parivitti</s> (bypassed elder brother), the <s>parivettṛ</s> (younger brother who married first), the giver, and the officiating priest —
they are purified by a twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s> (severe penance); the woman by a three-night penance.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.1/ atha patanīyāni //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.1/ Now the offences causing loss of caste (<s>patanīya</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.2/ samudra.saṃyānam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.2/ Voyaging by sea.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.3/ brahmasva.nyāsa.apaharaṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.3/ Misappropriation of a deposit belonging to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmasva</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.4/ bhūmy.anṛtam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.4/ Falsehood regarding land.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.5/ sarva.paṇyair vyavaharaṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.5/ Trading in all kinds of merchandise.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.6/ śūdra.sevanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.6/ Serving a <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.7/ śūdrā.abhijananam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.7/ Begetting offspring on a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.8/ tad.apatyatvaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.8/ And being the offspring of such a union.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.9/ eteṣām [K: eṣām] anyatamaṃ [K: anyatamat] (kṛtvā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.9/ Having committed any one of these [K: of these],

body.text:
Baudh2.1.2.10ab/ caturtha.kālā mita.bhojinaḥ (syur apo^(abhyaveyuḥ [K omitsapo 'bhyaveyuḥ] savana.anukalpam /
Baudh2.1.2.10cd/ sthāna.āsanābhyāṃ (viharanta ete tribhir varṣais tad(apaghnanti [K: apahanti] pāpam //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.2.10/ They should eat at every fourth mealtime, be moderate in eating, and drink water [K omits: drink water] according to the pattern of the <s>savana</s> (Soma pressings);
performing standing and sitting postures, these men destroy that sin in three years.

body.text:
Baudh2.1.2.11ab/ yad eka.rātreṇa (karoti pāpaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ varṇaṃ brāhmaṇaḥsevamānaḥ /
Baudh2.1.2.11cd/ caturtha.kāla udaka.abhyavāyī tribhir varṣais tad (apahantipāpam // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.2.11/ Whatever sin a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> commits in a single night by consorting with the dark complexion (i.e., a <s>Śūdra</s>),
eating at every fourth mealtime and subsisting on water, he removes that sin in three years.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.12/ atha^upapātakāni //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.12/ Now the minor offences (<s>upapātaka</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.13/ agamyā.gamanaṃ gurvī.sakhīṃ guru.sakhīm apapātrāṃ patitāṃca (gatvā bheṣaja.karaṇaṃ grāma.yājanaṃ raṅga.upajīvanaṃnāṭya.ācāryatā go.mahiṣī.rakṣaṇaṃ yac ca^anyad apy evaṃ.yuktaṃkanyā.dūṣaṇam iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.13/ Intercourse with a forbidden woman; going to the wife of an elder, the wife of a friend, an outcaste woman, or a fallen woman; practicing medicine; serving as a village priest; living by stage performances; teaching drama; tending cows and buffaloes; and whatever else is of such a nature; and deflowering a maiden.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.14/ teṣāṃ tu nirveśaḥ patitavṛttir dvau saṃvatsarau //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.14/ The expiation for these is living the life of a fallen person for two years.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.15/ atha^aśucikarāṇi //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.15/ Now the acts that cause impurity (<s>aśucikaraṇa</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.16/ dyūtam abhicāro^anāhitāgner uñcha.vṛttitā samāvṛttasyabhaikṣacaryā tasya ca^eva guru.kule vāsa ūrdhvaṃ caturbhyo māsebhyastasya ca^adhyāpanaṃ nakṣatra.nirdeśaś ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.16/ Gambling, sorcery, not maintaining the sacred fires, living by gleaning for one who has not returned from studentship, begging for alms after completing studentship, and dwelling in the teacher's house beyond four months after that, and teaching such a person, and determination of auspicious stars (for him) —

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.17/ teṣāṃ tu nirveśo dvādaśa māsān dvādaśa ardha.māsāndvādaśa dvādaśa.ahān dvādaśa ṣaḍ.ahān dvādaśa try.ahān dvādaśāhaṃṣaḍ.ahaṃ try.aham ahorātram eka.aham iti yathā karma.abhyāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.17/ For these, the expiation is twelve months, twelve fortnights, twelve periods of twelve days, twelve periods of six days, twelve periods of three days, twelve days, six days, three days, a day and a night, or a single day — according to the repetition of the offense.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.18/ atha patitāḥ (samavasāya dharmāṃś (careyur itaretara.yājakāitaretara.adhyāpakā mitho vivahamānāḥ / putrān (saṃniṣpādya (brūyur(vipravrajata^asmat ta evam āryān (saṃpratipatsyatha^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.18/ Now, those who have fallen should assemble and practice the <s>dharmas</s> (religious duties), sacrificing for one another, teaching one another, intermarrying among themselves; having produced sons, they should say: 'Depart from us! Thus you shall be received among the noble ones.'

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.19/ atha^api na sendriyaḥ patati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.19/ Moreover, one who retains his senses does not fall.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.20/ tad etena veditavyam / aṅga.hīno^api [K: api hi] sa.aṅgaṃ(janayet [K: janayatīti] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.20/ This is to be understood by the following: even one who is deficient in a limb may beget one who has all limbs.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.21/ mithyā^etad iti hārītaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.21/ 'This is false,' says <s>Hārīta</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.22/ dadhi.dhānī.sadharmāḥ striyaḥ (syuḥ / yo hi dadhi.dhānyāmaprayataṃ paya (ātacya (manthati na tat^śiṣṭā dharmakṛtyeṣu^(upayojayanti//
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.22/ Women are like a vessel of curds; for if one pours impure milk into a curd vessel and churns it, the learned do not use that in religious rites.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.23/ evam aśuci śukraṃ yan (nirvartate na tena saha saṃprayogo (vidyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.23/ Likewise, the seed that is produced impurely — there should be no association with it.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.24/ aśuci.śukra.utpannānāṃ teṣām icchatāṃ prāyaścittiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.24/ For those born of impure seed, there is <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) if they desire it.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.25/ patanīyānāṃ tṛtīyo^aṃśaḥ strīṇām aṃśas tṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.25/ For offenses causing loss of caste, the penance for women is one-third of that prescribed.

body.text:
Baudh2.1.2.26-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti / [K om.]
Baudh2.1.2.26-2ab/ bhojana.abhyañjanād dānād yad anyat (kurute tilaiḥ /
Baudh2.1.2.26-2cd/ śva.viṣṭhāyāṃ kṛmir [K: krimir] (bhūtvā pitṛbhiḥ saha(majjati // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.2.26-1/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.1.2.26-2ab/ If one uses sesame seeds for purposes other than eating, anointing, and giving,
Baudh2.1.2.26-2cd/ he sinks with his ancestors, having become a worm in dog's excrement.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.27/ pitqn vā eṣa (vikrīṇīte yas tilān (vikrīṇīte / prāṇānvā eṣa (vikrīṇīte yas taṇḍulān (vikrīṇīte / sukṛta.aṃśān vā eṣa(vikrīṇīte yaḥ paṇamāno duhitaraṃ (dadāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.27/ He sells his ancestors who sells sesame seeds; he sells his vital breaths who sells rice grains; he sells his share of merit who gives his daughter for a price.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.28/ tṛṇa.kāṣṭham [K: tṛṇaṃ kāṣṭham] avikṛtaṃ vikreyam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.28/ Grass and wood in their unprocessed form may be sold.

body.text:
Baudh2.1.2.29-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti [K: udāranti] /
Baudh2.1.2.29-2ab/ paśavaś ca^ekato.dantā aśmā ca lavaṇa.uddhṛtaḥ /
Baudh2.1.2.29-2cd/ etad brāhmaṇa te paṇyaṃ tantuś ca^arajanīkṛtaḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.1.2.29-1/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.1.2.29-2ab/ Animals with teeth on one side only, and rock salt,
Baudh2.1.2.29-2cd/ these are the merchandise for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and thread that has not been dyed.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.30/ pātaka.varjaṃ vā babhruṃ piṅgalāṃ gāṃ romaśāṃsarpiṣā^(avasicya kṛṣṇais tilair (avakīrya^anūcānāya (dadyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.30/ Except for those who have committed a <s>pātaka</s> (major sin) — one should pour clarified butter over a brown or tawny cow with abundant hair, scatter black sesame seeds upon it, and give it to a learned man.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.31/ kūśmāṇḍair vā dvādaśāham //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.31/ Or one may recite the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> mantras for twelve days.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.32/ yad arvācīnam eno bhrūṇa.hatyāyās tasmān (mucyata iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.32/ By this one is freed from whatever sin is lesser than the killing of an embryo.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.33/ pātaka.abhiśaṃsane kṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.33/ For a false accusation of a <s>pātaka</s> (major sin), the penance is a <s>kṛcchra</s> (austerity).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.34/ tad.abdo[K: tadaśabdo]^abhiśaṃsituḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.34/ For the accuser, the same penance lasts one year.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.35/ saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena samācaran / yājana.adhyāpanādyaunān na tu yāna.āsana.aśanād iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.35/ One falls within a year by associating with a fallen person — through sacrificing for him, teaching him, or forming a marriage alliance; but not by riding together, sitting together, or eating together.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.36/ amedhya.prāśane prāyaścittir [K: prāyaścittaṃ] naiṣpurīṣyam/ tat saptarātreṇa^(avāpyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.36/ For eating impure food, the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) is complete purging; that is accomplished in seven nights.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.37/ apaḥ payo ghṛtaṃ parāka iti prati.tryaham uṣṇāni satapta.kṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.37/ Water, milk, and clarified butter, then fasting — each for three days of hot liquids: this is the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (hot penance).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.38/ tryahaṃ prātas tathā sāyam [K adds: tryaham anyad] ayācitaṃ[K adds: tryahaṃ paraṃ tu nāśnīyāt] parāka iti kṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.38/ Three days eating in the morning, then three days eating in the evening, three days eating unsolicited food, and then fasting — this is the <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.39/ prātaḥ sāyam ayācitaṃ parāka iti trayaś catūrātrāḥ sa eṣastrī.bāla.vṛddhānāṃ kṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.39/ Morning, evening, unsolicited food, and fasting — three periods of four nights each: this is the <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) for women, children, and the aged.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.40/ yāvat sakṛd (ādadīta tāvad (aśnīyāt pūrvavat so^atikṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.40/ One should eat only as much as one can take up at once, following the same pattern as before — this is the <s>atikṛcchra</s> (extreme penance).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.41/ ab.bhakṣas tṛtīyaḥ sa kṛcchrātikṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.41/ The third, subsisting only on water, is the <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> (penance of extreme austerity).

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.42/ kṛcchre triṣavaṇam udaka.upasparśanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.42/ During a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance), one should perform water ablutions three times a day.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.43/ adhaḥ.śayanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.43/ Sleeping on the ground.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.44/ eka.vastratā keśa.śmaśru.loma.nakha.vāpanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.44/ Wearing a single garment, and shaving the hair, beard, body hair, and nails.

body.text: Baudh2.1.2.45/ etad eva striyāḥ keśa.vapana.varjam / keśa.vapana.varjam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.1.2.45/ The same applies to a woman, except for the shaving of head hair. Except for the shaving of head hair.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.1ab/ nitya.udakī nitya.yajñopavītī nitya.svādhyāyīvṛṣala.anna.varjī /
Baudh2.2.3.1cd/ ṛtau ca gacchan vidhivac ca juhvan na brāhmaṇaś (cyavatebrahmalokāt //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.1ab/ Always carrying water, always wearing the sacred thread, always engaged in <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), abstaining from the food of a <s>vṛṣala</s> (outcaste),
Baudh2.2.3.1cd/ approaching one's wife in the proper season, and offering oblations according to rule — a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> does not fall from the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.2/ manuḥ putrebhyo dāyaṃ (vyabhajad iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.2/ <s>Manu</s> divided the inheritance among his sons — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.3/ samaśaḥ sarveṣām aviśeṣāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.3/ In equal shares for all, because there is no distinction.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.4/ varaṃ vā rūpam (uddharej jyeṣṭhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.4/ Or the eldest may take the best item.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.5/ tasmāj jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ dhanena (niravasāyayanti^iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.5/ Therefore they endow the eldest son with wealth — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.6/ daśānāṃ vā^ekam (uddharej jyeṣṭhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.6/ Or the eldest may take one out of ten.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.7/ samam itare (vibhajeran //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.7/ The others should divide equally.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.8/ pitur anumatyā dāya.vibhāgaḥ sati pitari //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.8/ The partition of inheritance, while the father lives, requires the father's consent.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.9/ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ go.aśva.aja.avayo jyeṣṭha.aṃśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.9/ For the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), cattle, horses, goats, and sheep constitute the eldest son's share.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.10/ nānā.varṇa.strī.putra.samavāye dāyaṃ daśa.aṃśān (kṛtvācaturas trīn dvāv ekam iti yathā.kramaṃ (vibhajeran //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.10/ When sons of wives of different <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) are assembled, the inheritance should be divided into ten shares — four, three, two, and one respectively, in order of rank.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.11/ aurase tu^utpanne savarṇās tṛtīya.aṃśa.harāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.11/ But when a son born of a wife of the same <s>varṇa</s> is present, sons of wives of the same class receive one-third of the share.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.12/ savarṇā.putra.anantarā.putrayor anantarā.putraś ced guṇavānsa jyeṣṭha.aṃśaṃ (haret //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.12/ Between the son of a wife of the same <s>varṇa</s> and the son of the next lower, if the son of the next lower is endowed with virtues, he shall take the eldest son's share.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.13/ guṇavān hi śeṣāṇāṃ bhartā (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.13/ For one endowed with virtues becomes the protector of the rest.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.14-1/ savarṇāyāṃ saṃskṛtāyāṃ svayam.utpāditam aurasaṃ putraṃ(vidyāt /
Baudh2.2.3.14-2/ atha^apy (udāharanti / [K om.]
Baudh2.2.3.14-3ab/ aṅgād aṅgāt (saṃbhavasi hṛdayād adhi (jāyase / [K om.]
Baudh2.2.3.14-3cd/ ātmā vai putra.nāma^asi sa (jīva śaradaḥ śatam // iti //[K om.]
Baudh2.2.3.15/ (abhyupagamya duhitari jātaṃ putrikā.putram anyaṃ dauhitram //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.14-1/ One should know as the <s>aurasa</s> (legitimate son) the one begotten by oneself on a wife of the same <s>varṇa</s> who has been duly married.
Baudh2.2.3.14-2/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.2.3.14-3ab/ 'From limb to limb you are born, from the heart you are produced;
Baudh2.2.3.14-3cd/ you are the self called son — may you live a hundred autumns.'
Baudh2.2.3.15/ One who, having agreed to give his daughter as a <s>putrikā</s> (appointed daughter), takes the son born to her as a <s>putrikā-putra</s> (son of an appointed daughter); another is the <s>dauhitra</s> (daughter's son).

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.16-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.3.16-2ab/ (ādiśet prathame piṇḍe mātaraṃ putrikā.sutaḥ /
Baudh2.2.3.16-2cd/ dvitīye pitaraṃ tasyās tṛtīye ca pitāmaham // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.16-1/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.2.3.16-2ab/ The son of an appointed daughter should offer the first <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral oblation) to his mother,
Baudh2.2.3.16-2cd/ the second to her father, and the third to her grandfather.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.17/ mṛtasya prasūto yaḥ klība.vyādhitayor vā^anyena^anumate [K:'numatena] sve kṣetre sa kṣetrajaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.17/ The son who is born on the wife of one who is dead, or of one who is impotent or diseased, by another man with permission, on his own field — that is the <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.18/ sa eṣa dvi.pitā dvi.gotraś ca dvayor api svadhā.riktha.bhāg(bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.18/ This one has two fathers and two <s>gotras</s> (lineages), and he receives the funeral offerings and inheritance from both.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.19-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.3.19-2ab/ dvi.pituḥ piṇḍa.dānaṃ (syāt piṇḍe.piṇḍe ca nāmanī /
Baudh2.2.3.19-2cd/ trayaś ca piṇḍāḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ (syur evaṃ kurvan na (muhyati // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.19-1/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.2.3.19-2ab/ The offering of <s>piṇḍas</s> (funeral oblations) for one with two fathers should include the names at each oblation,
Baudh2.2.3.19-2cd/ and there should be three <s>piṇḍas</s> for six persons — one who does thus is not confused.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.20/ mātā.pitṛbhyāṃ datto^anyatareṇa vā yo^apatya.arthe(parigṛhyate sa dattaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.20/ One who is given by both mother and father, or by either one, and is accepted for the purpose of having offspring — that is the <s>dattaka</s> (adopted son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.21/ sadṛśaṃ yaṃ sakāmaṃ svayaṃ (kuryāt sa kṛtrimaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.21/ One of equal status whom one makes one's own son willingly — that is the <s>kṛtrima</s> (made son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.22/ gṛhe gūḍha.utpanno^ante jñāto gūḍhajaḥ [K: gūḍhoḥ] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.22/ One born secretly in the house and later recognized — that is the <s>gūḍhaja</s> (secretly born son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.23/ mātā.pitṛbhyām utsṛṣṭo^anyatareṇa vā yo^apatya.arthe(parigṛhyate so^apaviddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.23/ One who has been abandoned by both mother and father, or by either one, and is accepted for the purpose of having offspring — that is the <s>apaviddha</s> (cast-off son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.24/ asaṃskṛtām anatisṛṣṭāṃ yām (upagacchet [K: upayacchet]tasyāṃ yo jātaḥ sa kānīnaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.24/ The son born to an unmarried girl who has not been given away by her father, whom a man approaches — that is the <s>kānīna</s> (son of an unmarried girl).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.25/ yā garbhiṇī (saṃskriyate vijñātā vā^avijñātā vā tasyāṃyo jātaḥ sa sahoḍhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.25/ A woman who is married while pregnant, whether this is known or unknown, the son born to her — that is the <s>sahoḍha</s> (son received with the bride).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.26/ mātā.pitror hastāt krīto^anyatareṇa vā yo^apatya.arthe(parigṛhyate sa krītaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.26/ One bought from the mother and father, or from either one, and accepted for the purpose of having offspring — that is the <s>krīta</s> (purchased son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.27/ klībaṃ (tyaktvā patitaṃ vā yā^anyaṃ patiṃ (vindet tasyāṃpunarbhvāṃ yo jātaḥ sa paunarbhavaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.27/ A woman who, having left an impotent or fallen husband, finds another husband — the son born to her, a remarried woman, is the <s>paunarbhava</s> (son of a remarried woman).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.28/ mātā.pitṛ.vihīno yaḥ svayam ātmānaṃ (dadyāt sa svayaṃ.dattaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.28/ One who, bereft of mother and father, gives himself — that is the <s>svayaṃdatta</s> (self-given son).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.29/ dvijāti.pravarāt^śūdrāyāṃ jāto niṣādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.29/ The son born to a <s>śūdrā</s> woman from a man of the highest <s>dvija</s> (twice-born) class is a <s>niṣāda</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.30/ kāmāt pāraśava iti putrāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.30/ One born of desire is a <s>pāraśava</s> — these are the types of sons.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.31-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.3.31-2ab/ aurasaṃ putrikā.putraṃ kṣetrajaṃ datta.kṛtrimau /
Baudh2.2.3.31-2cd/ gūḍhajaṃ ca^apaviddhaṃ ca riktha.bhājaḥ (pracakṣate //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.31-1/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.2.3.31-2ab/ The <s>aurasa</s> (legitimate son), the <s>putrikā-putra</s> (son of an appointed daughter), the <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born), the <s>dattaka</s> (adopted) and the <s>kṛtrima</s> (made son),
Baudh2.2.3.31-2cd/ the <s>gūḍhaja</s> (secretly born) and the <s>apaviddha</s> (cast-off) — these are declared to be sharers of the inheritance.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.32ab/ kānīnaṃ ca sahoḍhaṃ ca krītaṃ paunarbhavaṃ tathā /
Baudh2.2.3.32cd/ svayaṃ.dattaṃ niṣādaṃ ca gotra.bhājaḥ (pracakṣate //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.32ab/ The <s>kānīna</s> (son of an unmarried girl), the <s>sahoḍha</s> (son received with the bride), the <s>krīta</s> (purchased), the <s>paunarbhava</s> (son of a remarried woman),
Baudh2.2.3.32cd/ the <s>svayaṃdatta</s> (self-given), and the <s>niṣāda</s> — these are declared to be sharers of the <s>gotra</s> (lineage).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.33/ teṣāṃ prathama eva^ity (āha^aupajaṅghaniḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.33/ Of these, only the first is the true heir, says <s>Aupajaṅghani</s>.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.34-1ab/ idānīm aham (īrṣyāmi strīṇāṃ janaka no purā /
Baudh2.2.3.34-1cd/ yato yamasya sadane janayituḥ putram abruvan //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.34-1ab/ 'Now I am jealous regarding women, though not before,
Baudh2.2.3.34-1cd/ since in the abode of <s>Yama</s>, they declared the son to belong to the begetter.'

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.34-2ab/ retodhāḥ putraṃ nayati paretya yama.sādane /
Baudh2.2.3.34-2cd/ tasmāt sva.bhāryāṃ [K: tasmād bhāryāṃ] (rakṣantu [K:rakṣanti] bibhyataḥ [K: bibhyantaḥ] para.retasaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.34-2ab/ 'The giver of seed leads the son after death in the abode of <s>Yama</s>;
Baudh2.2.3.34-2cd/ therefore, let them guard their own wives, fearing the seed of another man.'

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.35ab/ apramattā rakṣata [K: rakṣatha] tantum etaṃ mā vaḥ kṣetreparabījāni (vāpsuḥ [K: vapsuḥ] /
Baudh2.2.3.35cd/ janayituḥ putro (bhavati sāṃparāye [K: sāmṣarāye] moghaṃvettā (kurute tantum etam // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.35ab/ 'Be vigilant and guard this lineage; let not others sow their seed in your field;
Baudh2.2.3.35cd/ in the next world the son belongs to the begetter — the knower who fails acts in vain regarding this lineage.'

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.36/ teṣām aprāpta.vyavahārāṇām aṃśān sa.upacayān suniguptān(nidadhyur ā vyavahāra.prāpaṇāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.36/ For those among them who have not attained the age of legal transactions, the shares should be kept safely with accumulated interest until they reach the age of legal competence.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.37/ atīta.vyavahārān grāsa.ācchādanair (bibhṛyuḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.37/ Those who have passed the age of legal competence should be maintained with food and clothing.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.38/ andha.jaḍa.klība.vyasani.vyādhita.ādīṃś ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.38/ And also the blind, the mentally deficient, the impotent, those afflicted by vice, the diseased, and others.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.39/ akarmiṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.39/ Those incapable of performing religious rites.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.40/ patita.taj.jāta.varjam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.40/ Except for the fallen and those born of them.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.41/ na patitaiḥ saṃvyavahāro (vidyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.41/ There should be no dealings with the fallen.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.42/ patitām api tu mātaraṃ (bibhṛyād anabhibhāṣamāṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.42/ But one should maintain even a fallen mother, without speaking to her.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.43/ mātur alaṃkāraṃ duhitaraḥ sāṃpradāyikaṃ (labherann anyad vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.43/ The daughters should receive the mother's ornaments as traditional property, or other things.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.44/ na striyāḥ [K: strī] svātantryaṃ (vidyate [K: vidante] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.44/ A woman has no independence.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.3.45-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.3.45-2ab/ pitā (rakṣati kaumāre bhartā (rakṣati yauvane /
Baudh2.2.3.45-2cd/ putras tu sthavirī.bhāve [K: sthāvire bhāve] na strīsvātantryam (arhati // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.3.45-1/ Moreover, they quote:
Baudh2.2.3.45-2ab/ The father protects her in childhood, the husband protects her in youth,
Baudh2.2.3.45-2cd/ the sons protect her in old age — a woman does not deserve independence.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.46/ nirindriyā hy adāyāś ca striyo matā iti śrutiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.46/ 'Women are without power and without share of the inheritance' — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.47/ bhartṛ.hite yatamānāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ (jayeran //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.47/ Striving for the welfare of their husbands, they shall win the heavenly world.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.48/ vyatikrame kṛcchraḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.48/ For transgression, the penance is a <s>kṛcchra</s> (austerity).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.49/ śūdre cāndrāyaṇaṃ (caret //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.49/ For a transgression with a <s>śūdra</s>, one should perform a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.50/ vaiśya.ādiṣu pratilomaṃ kṛcchra.atikṛcchra.ādīṃś (caret //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.50/ For transgressions with a <s>vaiśya</s> and others in the reverse order, one should perform <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance), <s>atikṛcchra</s> (severe penance), and so on.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.51/ puṃsāṃ brāhmaṇa.ādīnāṃ saṃvatsaraṃ brahmacaryam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.51/ For men, beginning with <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the period of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate penance) is one year.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.52/ śūdraṃ kaṭa.agninā [K: kaṭārinanā] (dahet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.52/ A <s>śūdra</s> should be cremated with the fire from a grass bundle.

body.text: Baudh2.2.3.53/ atha^apy (udāharanti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.3.53/ Moreover, they quote:

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.1ab/ abrāhmaṇasya śārīro daṇḍaḥ saṃgrahaṇe (bhavet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.1ab/ For a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>, corporeal punishment should be applied for the offense of seizing;

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.2ab/ sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ dārā rakṣyatamā dhanāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.2ab/ For all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), wives are to be guarded more than wealth.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.3ab/ na tu cāraṇa.dāreṣu na raṅga.avatare [K: raṅgāvatāre] vadhaḥ /
Baudh2.2.4.3cd/ (saṃsarjayanti tā hy etān niguptāṃś ca^(ālayanty api //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.3ab/ But there is no punishment regarding the wives of wandering performers or those who descend into the arena;
Baudh2.2.4.3cd/ for they themselves bring these men into contact with others, and they entice even those who are hidden.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.4ab/ striyaḥ pavitram atulaṃ na^etā (duṣyanti karhicit /
Baudh2.2.4.4cd/ māsi.māsi rajo hy āsāṃ duritāny (apakarṣati //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.4ab/ Women are an incomparable means of purification; they are never defiled,
Baudh2.2.4.4cd/ for month by month their menstrual flow removes their sins.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.5ab/ somaḥ śaucaṃ (dadau [K: dadat] tāsāṃ gandharvaḥ śikṣitāṃ giram /
Baudh2.2.4.5cd/ agniś ca sarvabhakṣatvaṃ [K: sarvabhakṣyatvaṃ] tasmānniṣkalmaṣāḥ striyaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.5ab/ <s>Soma</s> gave them purity, <s>Gandharva</s> gave them well-trained speech,
Baudh2.2.4.5cd/ and <s>Agni</s> gave them the quality of consuming everything; therefore women are free from stain.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.6ab/ aprajāṃ daśame varṣe strī.prajāṃ dvādaśe (tyajet /
Baudh2.2.4.6cd/ mṛta.prajāṃ pañcadaśe sadyas tv apriya.vādinīm //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.6ab/ One should abandon a wife who bears no children in the tenth year, one who bears only daughters in the twelfth,
Baudh2.2.4.6cd/ one whose children have died in the fifteenth, and one who speaks unpleasantly — immediately.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.7/ saṃvatsaraṃ preta.patnī madhu.māṃsa.madya.lavaṇāni (varjayedadhaḥ (śayīta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.7/ The wife of a deceased man should abstain from honey, meat, liquor, and salt for a year, and should sleep on the ground.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.8/ ṣaṇ.māsān iti maudgalyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.8/ For six months, according to <s>Maudgalya</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.9/ ata ūrdhvaṃ gurubhir anumatā devarāj (janayet putram aputrā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.9/ After that period, if she is without a son and has the permission of her elders, she should beget a son through the brother-in-law (<s>devara</s>).

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.10-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.4.10-2ab/ vaśā ca^utpanna.putrā ca nīrajaskā gata.prajā /
Baudh2.2.4.10-2cd/ na^akāmā saṃniyojyā (syāt phalaṃ yasyāṃ na (vidyate //iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.10-1/ Now they also cite the following:
Baudh2.2.4.10-2ab/ A barren woman, one who has already borne sons, one past menstruation, one whose offspring have died —
Baudh2.2.4.10-2cd/ such a woman should not be appointed against her will to bear a child, when no fruit can be expected from her. Thus it is said.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.11/ mātula.pitṛ.svasā bhaginī bhāgineyī snuṣā mātulānīsakhi.vadhūr ity agamyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.11/ The maternal uncle's wife, the father's sister, one's own sister, the sister's daughter, the daughter-in-law, the maternal uncle's wife, and the friend's wife — these are women with whom sexual relations are forbidden (<s>agamyā</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.12/ agamyānāṃ gamane kṛcchra.atikṛcchrau cāndrāyaṇam itiprāyaścittiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.12/ For sexual intercourse with forbidden women, the expiation is <s>Kṛcchra</s> (severe penance), <s>Atikṛcchra</s> (extra-severe penance), and <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.13/ etena caṇḍālī.vyavāyo vyākhyātaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.13/ By this, sexual intercourse with a <s>Caṇḍālī</s> (outcast woman) is also explained.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.14-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.4.14-2ab/ caṇḍālīṃ brāhmaṇo (gatvā (bhuktvā ca (pratigṛhya ca /
Baudh2.2.4.14-2cd/ ajñānāt patito vipro jñānāt tu samatāṃ (vrajet //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.14-1/ Now they also cite the following:
Baudh2.2.4.14-2ab/ A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has had intercourse with a <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, who has eaten her food, or who has accepted gifts from her,
Baudh2.2.4.14-2cd/ falls from his status if he did so unknowingly; but if knowingly, he becomes equal to her.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.15ab/ pitur guror narendrasya bhāryāṃ (gatvā pramādataḥ /
Baudh2.2.4.15cd/ gurutalpī (bhavet tena pūrva.uktas tasya niṣkrayaḥ [K:niścayaḥ] // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.15ab/ Having approached the wife of one's father, teacher, or king through carelessness,
Baudh2.2.4.15cd/ one becomes a defiler of the teacher's bed (<s>gurutalpin</s>); the atonement for him has been stated previously. Thus it is said.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.16/ adhyāpana.yājana.pratigrahair aśaktaḥ kṣatra.dharmeṇa (jīvetpratyanantaratvāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.16/ When unable to live by teaching, officiating at sacrifices, and accepting gifts, one may live by the duty of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, because it is the next in order.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.17/ na^iti gautamaḥ / atyugro hi kṣatra.dharmo brāhmaṇasya //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.17/ Not so, says <s>Gautama</s>; for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> duty is too harsh for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.18-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.4.18-2ab/ gava.arthe brāhmaṇa.arthe vā varṇānāṃ vā^api saṃkare /
Baudh2.2.4.18-2cd/ (gṛhṇīyātāṃ vipra.viśau śastraṃ dharma.vyapekṣayā //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.18-1/ Now they also cite the following:
Baudh2.2.4.18-2ab/ For the sake of cattle, for the sake of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, or in times of intermixture of the <s>varṇas</s>,
Baudh2.2.4.18-2cd/ the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>Vaiśya</s> may take up arms, with regard to <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.19/ vaiśya.vṛttir anuṣṭheyā pratyanantaratvāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.19/ The livelihood of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should be adopted, because it is the next in order.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.20/ prāk prātar.āśāt karṣī (syāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.20/ Before the morning meal, one should be a cultivator.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.21/ asyūta.nāsikābhyāṃ samuṣkābhyām atudann ārayāmuhur.muhur abhyucchandayan // [Baudh2.2.4.20-21 = Baudh3.2.3]
Baudh2.2.4.22/ bhāryā.ādir agniḥ / tasmin karma.karaṇaṃ prāg agnyādheyāt //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.21/ With the nostrils unsewn, with the testicles intact, not striking, gently, repeatedly urging on the oxen.
Baudh2.2.4.22/ The wife is the first fire. In that fire, ritual acts are to be performed before the establishment of the sacred fires (<s>Agnyādheya</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.23/ agnyādheya.prabhṛty atha^imāny ajasrāṇi (bhavanti yathā^etadagnyādheyam agnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsāv āgrayaṇamudagayana.dakṣiṇāyanayoḥ paśuś cāturmāsyāny ṛtumukhe ṣaḍḍhotā vasantejyotiṣtoma ity evaṃ kṣema.prāpaṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.23/ Beginning from the <s>Agnyādheya</s> (establishment of sacred fires), the following become perpetual obligations: namely, the <s>Agnyādheya</s>, the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon sacrifices), the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering), the animal sacrifice at the two solstices, the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal offerings), the <s>Ṣaḍḍhotā</s> at the turn of each season, the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> in spring — thus one attains prosperity.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.24/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.4.24ab/ na divā.svapna.śīlena na ca sarva.anna.bhojinā /
Baudh2.2.4.24cd/ kāmaṃ śakyaṃ nabho gantum ārūḍha.patitena vā //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.24/ Now they also cite the following:
Baudh2.2.4.24ab/ Not by one who habitually sleeps during the day, nor by one who eats all kinds of food,
Baudh2.2.4.24cd/ can heaven be reached — nor by one who has risen and then fallen.

body.text: Baudh2.2.4.25/ dainyaṃ śāṭhyaṃ jaihmyaṃ ca (varjayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.2.4.25/ One should avoid wretchedness, deceit, and crookedness.

body.text:
Baudh2.2.4.26-1/ atha^apy atra^uśanasaś ca vṛṣaparvaṇaś ca duhitroḥ saṃvādegāthām (udāharanti /
Baudh2.2.4.26-2ab/ stuvato duhitā tvaṃ vai yācataḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ /
Baudh2.2.4.26-2cd/ atha^ahaṃ stūyamānasya dadato^apratigṛhṇataḥ /
Baudh2.2.4.26-3/ dadato^apratigṛhṇata iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.2.4.26-1/ Now, regarding this, they cite a verse from the dialogue between the daughters of <s>Uśanas</s> and <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>:
Baudh2.2.4.26-2ab/ "You are the daughter of one who praises, begs, and accepts,"
Baudh2.2.4.26-2cd/ "And I am the daughter of one who is praised, who gives, and who does not accept."
Baudh2.2.4.26-3/ "Of one who gives and does not accept" — thus it is said.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.1/ tapasyam apovagāhanam [apas.avagāhanam] [K: tapasyam avagāhanam] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.1/ The practice of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) consists in bathing in water.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.2/ devatās (tarpayitvā pitṛ.tarpaṇam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.2/ After satisfying the deities, one should perform <s>pitṛ-tarpaṇa</s> (libation to the ancestors).

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.3/ anutīrtham apa (utsiñcati [K: utsiñced] / ūrjaṃ vahantīr iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.3/ At each <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred bathing place), one pours water, reciting "<s>Ūrjaṃ vahantīḥ</s>" ("Carrying nourishment").

body.text:
Baudh2.3.5.4-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.3.5.4-2ab/ sravantīṣv aniruddhāsu trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ /
Baudh2.3.5.4-2cd/ prātar.utthāya [K: prātarutthāyāya] (kurvīrandeva.ṛṣi.pitṛ.tarpaṇam //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.5.4-1/ Now they also cite the following:
Baudh2.3.5.4-2ab/ When waters are flowing and unobstructed, the three twice-born <s>varṇas</s>
Baudh2.3.5.4-2cd/ should rise at dawn and perform the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) to the gods, sages, and ancestors.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.5/ niruddhāsu na (kurvīrann aṃśa.bhāk tatra setu.kṛt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.5/ When the waters are obstructed, they should not perform it; the one who built the dam has a share in the merit there.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.6/ tasmāt para.kṛtān setūn kūpāṃś ca (parivarjayed iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.6/ Therefore one should avoid dams and wells built by others. Thus it is said.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.5.7-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.3.5.7-2ab/ (uddhṛtya vā^api trīn piṇḍān (kuryād āpatsu na^u sadā /
Baudh2.3.5.7-2cd/ niruddhāsu tu mṛt.piṇḍān kūpāt trīn ab.ghaṭāṃs tathā// iti //
Baudh2.3.5.8/ bahu.pratigrāhyasya^apratigrāhyasya vā (pratigṛhya [K: bahupratigrāhyasya pratigṛhyāpratigrāhyasya vā]^ayājyaṃ vā(yājayitva^anāśya.annasya vā^annam (aśitvā taratsamandīyaṃ (japed iti//
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.8/ After accepting gifts from one who receives many gifts, or from one who is unworthy of receiving gifts, or after officiating at a sacrifice for one who is unfit to have sacrifices performed, or after eating the food of one whose food should not be eaten, one should recite the <s>Taratsamandīya</s> hymn.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.5.9-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.3.5.9-2ab/ guru.saṃkariṇaś ca^eva śiṣya.saṃkariṇaś ca ye /
Baudh2.3.5.9-2cd/ āhāra.mantra.saṃkīrṇā dīrghaṃ tama (upāsate // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.5.9-1/ Now they also cite the following:
Baudh2.3.5.9-2ab/ Those who corrupt their teachers, and those who corrupt their pupils,
Baudh2.3.5.9-2cd/ those who are defiled in food and sacred formulas — they dwell long in darkness. Thus it is said.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.10/ atha snātaka.vratāni //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.10/ Now follow the observances for the <s>Snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic study and taken the ritual bath).

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.11/ sāyaṃ prātar yad aśanīyaṃ (syāt tena^annena vaiśvadevaṃbalim (upahṛtya brāhmaṇa.kṣatriya.viṭ.śūdrān abhyāgatān yathā.śakti(pūjayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.11/ With whatever food is available in the evening and morning, having offered the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> <s>bali</s> (offering to all the gods), one should honor to the best of one's ability the guests who have arrived, whether <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, or <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.12/ yadi bahūnāṃ na (śaknuyād ekasmai guṇavate (dadyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.12/ If one is unable to provide for many, one should give to a single person of good qualities.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.13/ yo vā prathamam upagataḥ [K: upāgataḥ] (syāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.13/ Or to the one who has arrived first.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.14/ śūdraś ced āgatas taṃ karmaṇi (niyuñjyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.14/ If a <s>Śūdra</s> has come, one should engage him in work.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.15/ śrotriyāya vā^agraṃ (dadyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.15/ Or one should give the first portion to a <s>Śrotriya</s> (one learned in the Vedas).

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.16/ ye nityā bhāktikāḥ [K: nityābhaktikās] (syus teṣāmanuparodhena saṃvibhāgo vihitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.16/ For those who are permanent dependents receiving regular food shares, the distribution is prescribed without causing them hindrance.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.17/ na tv eva kadācid (adattvā [K: adatvā] (bhuñjīta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.17/ But one should never eat without first having given to others.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.5.18-1/ atha^apy atra^anna.gītau ślokāv (udāharanti /
Baudh2.3.5.18-2ab/ yo mām (adattvā [K: adatvā] pitṛ.devatābhyobhṛtya.atithīnāṃ ca suhṛj.janasya /
Baudh2.3.5.18-2cd/ saṃpannam aśnan viṣam (atti mohāt tam (admy ahaṃ tasya camṛtyur (asmi //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.5.18-1/ Now, regarding this, they cite two verses as the "Song of Food":
Baudh2.3.5.18-2ab/ "He who, without offering me to the ancestors and gods, to servants and guests, and to friends,
Baudh2.3.5.18-2cd/ eats me, though abundantly prepared, out of delusion eats poison — I consume him, and I am his death."

body.text:
Baudh2.3.5.18-3ab/ huta.agnihotraḥ kṛta.vaiśvadevaḥ (pūjya^atithīn bhṛtya.jana.avaśiṣṭam /
Baudh2.3.5.18-3cd/ tuṣṭaḥ śuciḥ śrad.dadhad (atti yo māṃ tasya^amṛtaṃ (syāṃsa ca māṃ (bhunakti [K: bhunaktīti] //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.5.18-3ab/ "He who, having offered the <s>Agnihotra</s>, having performed the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, having honored guests, eats what remains after feeding his dependents,
Baudh2.3.5.18-3cd/ contented, pure, and full of faith — for him I become <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality), and he truly enjoys me."

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.19/ subrāhmaṇa.śrotriya.vedapāragebhyogurv.artha.niveśa.auṣadha.artha.vṛtti.kṣīṇa.yakṣyamāṇa.adhyayana.adhva.saṃyoga.vaiśvajiteṣu dravya.saṃvibhāgo yathā.śakti kāryo bahirvedibhikṣamāṇeṣu //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.19/ To excellent <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars), those who have mastered the <s>Vedas</s>, those who seek to support their teacher, those who need medicine, those whose livelihood has been exhausted, those about to perform a sacrifice, those engaged in study, travelers, and those performing the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice — one should share one's wealth according to one's ability when they come begging outside the sacrificial enclosure.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.20/ kṛta.annam itareṣu //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.20/ Cooked food should be given to the rest.

body.text: Baudh2.3.5.21/ suprakṣālita.pāda.pāṇir ācāntaḥ śucau saṃvṛte deśe^annamupahṛtam (upasaṃgṛhya kāma.krodha.droha.lobha.mohān (apahatya sarvābhiraṅgulībhiḥ śabdam akurvan (prāśnīyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.5.21/ Having thoroughly washed one's hands and feet, having sipped water for purification, in a clean and enclosed place, having taken up the food that has been served, having dispelled desire, anger, malice, greed, and delusion, one should eat with all fingers, making no sound.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.1/ na piṇḍa.śeṣaṃ pātryām (utsṛjet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.1/ One should not throw the remnants of the food ball into the vessel.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.2/ māṃsa.matsya.tila.saṃsṛṣṭa.prāśane^apa (upaspṛśya^agnim(abhimṛśet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.2/ After eating food mixed with meat, fish, or sesame, one should sip water and touch fire.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.3/ astamite ca snānam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.3/ And one should bathe after sunset.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.4/ pālāśam āsanaṃ pāduke danta.dhāvanam iti (varjayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.4/ One should avoid a seat made of <s>Palāśa</s> wood, shoes, and a tooth-cleaning stick.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.5/ na^utsaṅge^annaṃ (bhakṣayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.5/ One should not eat food placed in one's lap.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.6/ āsandyāṃ na (bhuñjīta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.6/ One should not eat on a couch.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.7/ vaiṇavaṃ daṇḍaṃ (dhārayed rukma.kuṇḍale ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.7/ One should carry a bamboo staff and golden earrings.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.8/ padā pādasya prakṣālanam adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca (varjayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.8/ One should avoid washing one foot with the other foot, and standing on one foot with the other.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.9/ na bahir.mālāṃ (dhārayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.9/ One should not wear a garland on the outside.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.10/ sūryam udaya.astamaye na (nirīkṣeta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.10/ One should not gaze at the sun during its rising or setting.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.11/ na^indra.dhanur iti parasmai (prabrūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.11/ One should not point out a rainbow to another person by calling it "<s>Indra</s>'s bow."

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.12/ yadi (brūyān maṇi.dhanur ity eva (brūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.12/ If one must refer to it, one should call it "the jeweled bow."

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.13/ pura.dvāri^indrakīla.parighāv antareṇa na^(atīyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.13/ At the gate of a town, one should not pass between the <s>Indrakīla</s> (post of <s>Indra</s>) and the bolt.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.14/ pleṅkhayor [K: preṅkhayor] antareṇa na (gacchet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.14/ One should not pass between two swings.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.15/ vatsa.tantīṃ ca na^upari (gacchet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.15/ And one should not step over the rope tethering a calf.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.16/ bhasma.asthi.roma.tuṣa.kapāla.apasnānāni na^(adhitiṣṭhet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.16/ One should not step on ashes, bones, hair, husks, potsherds, or the water used for bathing.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.17/ gāṃ dhayantīṃ na parasmai (prabrūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.17/ One should not point out to another a cow that is suckling its calf.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.18/ na^adhenum adhenur iti (brūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.18/ One should not call a barren cow "barren."

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.19/ yadi (brūyād dhenuṃ bhavyā^ity [K: dhenubhavyety] eva (brūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.19/ If one must refer to her, one should say "one destined to become a milch cow."

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.20/ śuktā rūkṣāḥ paruṣā vāco na (brūyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.20/ One should not utter sour, harsh, or rough words.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.21/ na^eko^adhvānaṃ (vrajet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.21/ One should not travel alone.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.22/ na patitair na striyā na śūdreṇa //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.22/ Nor with outcasts, nor with a woman, nor with a <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.23/ na pratisāyaṃ (vrajet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.23/ One should not travel towards the evening.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.24/ na nagnaḥ (snāyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.24/ One should not bathe naked.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.25/ na naktaṃ (snāyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.25/ One should not bathe at night.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.26/ One should not cross a river using only one's arms.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.27/ One should not peer into a well.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.28/ na gartam (avekṣeta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.28/ One should not peer into a pit.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.29/ na tatra^(upaviśed yata enam anya (utthāpayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.29/ One should not sit in a place from which another person would make him get up.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.30ab/ panthā deyo brāhmaṇāya gave rājñe hy acakṣuṣe /
Baudh2.3.6.30cd/ vṛddhāya bhāra.taptāya garbhiṇyai durbalāya ca //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.30ab/ The path should be yielded to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to a cow, to a king, to a blind person,
Baudh2.3.6.30cd/ to an elder, to one burdened with a load, to a pregnant woman, and to a weak person.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.31/ prabhūta.edha.udaka[K:prabhūtadhodaka].yava.sasamit.kuśa.mālya.upaniṣkramaṇamāḍhya.jana.ākulam analasa.samṛddham ārya.jana.bhūyiṣṭhama.dasyu.praveśyaṃ grāmam (āvasituṃ (yateta dhārmikaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.31/ A righteous person should endeavor to dwell in a village that has abundant firewood, water, barley, sesame, sacrificial fuel, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and garlands available for going out; that is frequented by wealthy people; that is free from idleness and prosperous; that is inhabited mostly by <s>Ārya</s> people; and where brigands do not enter.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.32ab/ udapāna.udake grāme brāhmaṇo vṛṣalī.patiḥ /
Baudh2.3.6.32cd/ (uṣitvā dvādaśa samāḥ śūdra.sādharmyam (ṛcchati //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.32ab/ A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is the husband of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, living in a village with only well-water,
Baudh2.3.6.32cd/ after dwelling there for twelve years, attains the same status as a <s>Śūdra</s>.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.33ab/ pura.reṇu.kuṇṭhita.śarīras tat.paripurṇa[K:tatparipūrṇa].netra.vadanaś ca /
Baudh2.3.6.33cd/ nagare vasan suniyata.ātmā siddhim (avāpsyati^iti na tad(asti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.33ab/ With body covered by the dust of a city, eyes and face filled with it,
Baudh2.3.6.33cd/ one living in a city, even if well-restrained in soul, will attain perfection — that is not so.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.34ab/ ratha.aśva.gaja.dhānyānāṃ gavāṃ ca^eva rajaḥ śubham /
Baudh2.3.6.34cd/ apraśastaṃ samūhanyāḥ śva.aja.avi.khara.vāsasām //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.34ab/ The dust of chariots, horses, elephants, grain, and cows is auspicious;
Baudh2.3.6.34cd/ but the dust of sweepings, dogs, goats, sheep, donkeys, and garments is inauspicious.

body.text: Baudh2.3.6.35/ pūjyān (pūjayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.3.6.35/ One should honor those who are worthy of honor.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.36ab/ ṛṣi.vidvan.nṛpa.vara.mātula.śvaśura.ṛtvijaḥ /
Baudh2.3.6.36cd/ ete^arghyāḥ śāstra.vihitāḥ smṛtāḥ kāla.vibhāgaśaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.36ab/ Sages, learned men, distinguished kings, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, and officiating priests —
Baudh2.3.6.36cd/ these are declared by the scriptures to be worthy of the <s>arghya</s> (respectful offering), to be honored according to the proper time.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.37ab/ ṛṣi.vidvan.nṛpāḥ prāptāḥ kriyā.ārambhe vara.ṛtvijau /
Baudh2.3.6.37cd/ mātula.śvaśurau pūjyau saṃvatsara.gata.āgatau // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.37ab/ <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), learned men, and kings who have arrived, the best <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) at the commencement of a rite,
Baudh2.3.6.37cd/ the maternal uncle and father-in-law who are to be honored, and those who have come after a year's absence — thus it is stated.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.38ab/ agny.agāre gavāṃ madhye brāhmaṇānāṃ ca saṃnidhau /
Baudh2.3.6.38cd/ svādhyāye bhojane ca^eva dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum (uddharet //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.38ab/ In the fire-house, amidst cows, and in the presence of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
Baudh2.3.6.38cd/ during <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic recitation) and at meals, one should raise the right arm.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.39ab/ uttaraṃ vāsaḥ kartavyaṃ pañcasv eteṣu karmasu /
Baudh2.3.6.39cd/ svādhyāya.utsarga.dāneṣu bhojana.ācāmayos [K:bhojanācamanayos] tathā //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.39ab/ The upper garment should be worn over the left shoulder in these five acts:
Baudh2.3.6.39cd/ during <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic recitation), recitation of the Veda, gift-giving, eating, and <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping of water).

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.40ab/ havanaṃ bhojanaṃ dānam upahāraḥ pratigrahaḥ /
Baudh2.3.6.40cd/ bahir.jānu na kāryāṇi tadvad ācamanaṃ smṛtam //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.40ab/ Oblation, eating, giving, offering, and receiving —
Baudh2.3.6.40cd/ these should not be performed with the knees outside the arms; likewise <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping) is prescribed in the same manner.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.41ab/ anne śritāni bhūtāni annaṃ prāṇam iti śrutiḥ /
Baudh2.3.6.41cd/ tasmād annaṃ pradātavyam annaṃ hi paramaṃ haviḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.41ab/ In food all beings are sustained; food is <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture).
Baudh2.3.6.41cd/ Therefore food should be given, for food is the supreme oblation.

body.text:
Baudh2.3.6.42-1ab/ hutena (śāmyate pāpaṃ hutam annena (śāmyati /
Baudh2.3.6.42-1cd/ annaṃ dakṣiṇayā śāntim (upayāti^iti na śrutiḥ [K: naśśrutir iti] /
Baudh2.3.6.42-2/ upayāti^iti naḥ śrutir iti // [K om.]
Baudh2.4.7.1/ atha^ataḥ saṃdhyā.upāsana.vidhiṃ (vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.3.6.42-1ab/ By an oblation, sin is pacified; the oblation is pacified by food;
Baudh2.3.6.42-1cd/ food attains peace through <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) — thus is our <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture).
Baudh2.3.6.42-2/ "It attains" — thus is our <s>śruti</s>.
Baudh2.4.7.1/ Now we shall explain the rules for the worship of the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight prayer).

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.2/ tīrthaṃ (gatvā^aprayato^abhiṣiktaḥ prayato vā^anabhiṣiktaḥprakṣālita.pāda.pāṇir apa (ācamya surabhimatyā^abliṅgābhirvāruṇībhir hiraṇyavarṇābhiḥ pāvamānībhir vyāhṛtibhir anyaiś capavitrair ātmānaṃ (prokṣya prayato (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.2/ Having gone to a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred bathing place), whether impure but having bathed, or pure but not having bathed, having washed one's feet and hands, having sipped water, and having sprinkled oneself with the <s>Surabhimatī</s>, <s>Abliṅga</s>, <s>Vāruṇī</s>, <s>Hiraṇyavarṇa</s>, and <s>Pāvamānī</s> hymns, the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), and other purificatory mantras, one becomes ritually pure.

body.text:
Baudh2.4.7.3-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.4.7.3-2ab/ apovagāhanaṃ (apas.avagāhanaṃ) snānaṃ vihitaṃ sārvavarṇikam /
Baudh2.4.7.3-2cd/ mantravat.prokṣaṇaṃ ca^api dvijātīnāṃ (viśiṣyate // iti //

body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.4/ And at the commencement of all rites, before the time of <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) worship, having sprinkled oneself with this very collection of purificatory mantras, one becomes ritually pure.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.5/ atha^apy (udāharanti / darbheṣv āsīno darbhān dhārayamāṇaḥsa.udakena pāṇinā pratyaṅ.mukhaḥ sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva (āvartayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.5/ And moreover they cite: Seated on <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), holding <s>darbha</s> grass, with a wet hand, facing west, one should repeat the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (Gāyatrī mantra) a thousand times.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.6/ prāṇa.āyāma.śo vā śatakṛtvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.6/ Or with <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), a hundred times.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.7/ ubhayataḥ.praṇavāṃ sa.sapta.vyāhṛtikāṃ manasā vā daśakṛtvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.7/ With <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable Om) at both ends, accompanied by the seven <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), mentally ten times.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.8/ tribhiś ca prāṇa.āyāmais tānto brahmahṛdayena //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.8/ And with three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls), concluding with the <s>Brahmahṛdaya</s> (Heart of Brahman hymn).

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.9/ vāruṇībhyāṃ rātrim (upatiṣṭhate / imaṃ me varuṇa / tat tvā(yāmi^iti / dvābhyām //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.9/ One worships the night with the two <s>Vāruṇī</s> verses: "<s>imaṃ me Varuṇa</s>" (Hear this my prayer, O <s>Varuṇa</s>) and "<s>tat tvā yāmi</s>" (That I beseech of you) — with these two.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.10/ evam eva prātaḥ prāṅ.mukhas tiṣṭhan //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.10/ In the same manner, in the morning, standing facing east.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.11/ maitrībhyām ahar (upatiṣṭhate/ mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ / mitrojanān yātayati^iti / dvābhyām //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.11/ One worships the day with the two <s>Maitrī</s> verses: "<s>Mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ</s>" (Of <s>Mitra</s>, upholder of men) and "<s>Mitro janān yātayati</s>" (<s>Mitra</s> regulates the people) — with these two.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.12/ supūrvām api pūrvām (upakramya^udita āditye (samāpnuyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.12/ Having begun well before sunrise, one should complete it when the sun has risen.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.13/ anastamita (upakramya supaścād api paścimām //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.13/ Having begun before sunset, one should complete the evening one well after sunset.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.14/ saṃdhyayoś ca saṃpattāv aho.rātrayoś ca saṃtatyai [K: santatiḥ] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.14/ And for the attainment of the <s>sandhyās</s> (twilight junctions), and for the continuity of day and night.

body.text:
Baudh2.4.7.15-1/ api ca^atra prajāpati.gītau ślokau (bhavataḥ /
Baudh2.4.7.15-2ab/ anāgatāṃ tu ye pūrvām anatītāṃ tu paścimām /
Baudh2.4.7.15-2cd/ saṃdhyāṃ na^(upāsate viprāḥ kathaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.4.7.15-1/ And here there are two verses sung by <s>Prajāpati</s>:
Baudh2.4.7.15-2ab/ Those <s>vipras</s> (learned Brāhmaṇas) who do not worship the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight prayer) — the morning one before it has passed, and the evening one before it has elapsed —
Baudh2.4.7.15-2cd/ how are they considered <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>?

body.text:
Baudh2.4.7.15-3ab/ sāyaṃ prātaḥ sadā saṃdhyāṃ ye viprā na^u (upāsate /
Baudh2.4.7.15-3cd/ kāmaṃ tān dhārmiko rājā śūdra.karmasu (yojayed // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.4.7.15-3ab/ Those <s>vipras</s> (learned Brāhmaṇas) who do not worship the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight prayer) always, evening and morning —
Baudh2.4.7.15-3cd/ a righteous king may set them to the tasks of <s>Śūdras</s> — thus it is stated.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.16/ tatra sāyam.atikrame rātry.upavāsaḥprātar.atikrame^ahar.upavāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.16/ In that case, for missing the evening <s>sandhyā</s>, the penance is fasting for the night; for missing the morning <s>sandhyā</s>, fasting for the day.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.17/ sthāna.āsana.phalam (avāpnoti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.17/ One obtains the fruit of standing and sitting (in prayer).

body.text:
Baudh2.4.7.18-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.4.7.18-2ab/ yad upastha.kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ padbhyāṃ vā yat kṛtaṃ (bhavet /
Baudh2.4.7.18-2cd/ bāhubhyāṃ manasā vā^api vācā vā yat kṛtaṃ (bhavet /
