body.translated_text:
Baudh2.4.7.18-1/ And moreover they cite:
Baudh2.4.7.18-2ab/ Whatever sin has been committed by the sexual organ, or whatever has been done by the feet,
Baudh2.4.7.18-2cd/ by the arms, by the mind, or whatever has been done by speech —
Baudh2.4.7.18-2ef/ by worshipping the evening <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight prayer), one is freed from all that.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.19/ rātryā ca^api (saṃdhīyate na ca^enaṃ varuṇo (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.19/ And one is united with the night, and <s>Varuṇa</s> does not seize him.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.20/ evam eva prātar (upasthāya rātri.kṛtāt pāpāt (pramucyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.20/ In the same manner, having worshipped in the morning, one is freed from the sin committed during the night.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.21/ ahnā ca^api (saṃdhīyate mitraś ca^enaṃ (gopāyaty ādityaśca^enaṃ svargaṃ lokam (unnayati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.21/ And one is united with the day, and <s>Mitra</s> protects him, and <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) leads him upward to the heavenly world.

body.text: Baudh2.4.7.22/ sa evam eva^ahar.ahar aho.rātrayoḥ saṃdhiṣu^upatiṣṭhamānobrahma.pūto brahma.bhūto brāhmaṇaḥ śāstram anuvartamāno brahma.lokam(abhijayati^iti (vijñāyate / brahmalokam (abhijayati^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.4.7.22/ Thus, he who day after day worships at the junctions of day and night, purified by <s>Brahman</s>, become one with <s>Brahman</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> following the sacred teaching, conquers the world of <s>Brahman</s> — thus it is known. He conquers the world of <s>Brahman</s> — thus it is known.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.1/ atha hastau (prakṣālya kamaṇḍaluṃ mṛt.piṇḍaṃ ca (saṃgṛhya [K:gṛhya] tīrthaṃ (gatvā triḥ pādau (prakṣālayate trir ātmānaṃ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.1/ Then, having washed his hands, taking a water-vessel and a lump of clay, having gone to a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred bathing place), he washes his feet three times and himself three times.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.2/ atha ha^eke (bruvate / śmaśānam āpo deva.gṛhaṃ goṣṭhaṃ yatra cabrāhmaṇā (aprakṣālya pādau tan na praveṣṭavyam iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.2/ Now some say: A cremation ground, waters, a temple, a cow-pen — and wherever <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are — one should not enter these without having washed one's feet.

body.text:
Baudh2.5.8.3-1/ atha^apo^(abhiprapadyate /
Baudh2.5.8.3-2ab/ hiraṇya.śṛṅgaṃ varuṇaṃ (prapadye tīrthaṃ me (dehi yācitaḥ /
Baudh2.5.8.3-2cd/ yan mayā bhuktam asādhūnāṃ pāpebhyaś ca pratigrahaḥ //

Baudh2.5.8.3-3ab/ yan me manasā vācā karmaṇā vā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam /
Baudh2.5.8.3-3cd/ tan na [K: ma] indro varuṇo bṛhaspatiḥ savitā ca (punantupunaḥ.punaḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.5.8.3-3ab/ "Whatever evil deed has been done by me in mind, speech, or action —
Baudh2.5.8.3-3cd/ may <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and <s>Savitṛ</s> purify me again and again" — thus it is stated.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.4/ atha^añjalinā^apa (upahanti [K: athāñjalinā upahanti] /sumitrā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ (santv iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.4/ Then with joined palms he strikes the water: "May the waters and herbs be friendly to us" — thus.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.5/ tāṃ diśaṃ (nirukṣati yasyām asya diśi dveṣyo (bhavati /durmitrās tasmai bhūyāsur yo^asmān (dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ (dviṣma iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.5/ He sprinkles toward that direction in which his enemy dwells: "May the waters be hostile to him who hates us and whom we hate" — thus.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.6/ atha^apa (upaspṛśya triḥ pradakṣiṇam udakam (āvartayati / yadapāṃ [K: yad arpāṃ] kruraṃ [K: krūraṃ] yad amedhyaṃ yad aśāntaṃ tad(apagacchatād [ḥ: apa gacchatād] iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.6/ Then having touched water, he turns the water around himself three times clockwise: "Whatever is cruel in the waters, whatever is impure, whatever is unpeaceful — may that depart" — thus.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.7/ apsu (nimajjya^(unmajjya //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.7/ He immerses himself in the water and emerges.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.8/ na^apsu sataḥ prayamaṇaṃ (vidyate na vāsaḥ.palpūlanaṃna^upasparśanam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.8/ While standing in the water, there is no stretching out of limbs, no wringing of the garment, and no touching.

body.text: Baudh2.5.8.9/ yady uparuddhāḥ syur etena^(upatiṣṭhate / namo^agnaye^apsumatenama indrāya namo varuṇāya namo vāruṇyai namo^adbhya iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.9/ If the waters are obstructed, one worships with this: "Homage to <s>Agni</s> who dwells in the waters, homage to <s>Indra</s>, homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>, homage to <s>Vāruṇī</s>, homage to the waters" — thus.

body.text:
Baudh2.5.8.10-1/ (uttīrya^(ācamya^ācāntaḥ punar (ācāmet /
Baudh2.5.8.10-2/ āpaḥ (punantu pṛthivīṃ [K: pṛthivī] pṛthivī pūtā(punātu mām / (punantu brahmaṇaspatir brahma pūtā (punātu mām //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.5.8.10-1/ Having come out, having sipped water, and having completed <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping), one should sip again:
Baudh2.5.8.10-2/ "May the waters purify the earth; may the purified earth purify me; may <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> (Lord of Sacred Speech) purify; may <s>Brahman</s>, purified, purify me."

body.translated_text: Baudh2.5.8.11/ Having made purificatory preparations, he sprinkles himself with water: with the three verses beginning "<s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ</s>" (O waters, you are indeed the source of happiness); with the four verses beginning "<s>Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ</s>" (Golden-colored, pure, purifying); and "<s>Pavamānaḥ suvarjanaḥ</s>" (The purifier, creator of good). Having sprinkled with this <s>anuvāka</s> (hymn section), submerged in the water, having held three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls) with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> (sin-destroying hymn), having emerged, having wrung out the garment, having put on clean, unworn garments after washing them, having sipped water, seated on <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), holding <s>darbha</s> grass, facing east, one should repeat the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand times, a hundred times, or an unlimited number of times, but not less than ten.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.1: Now, these are the five great sacrifices — they are indeed the great sessions: the sacrifice to the gods (<s>devayajña</s>), the sacrifice to the ancestors (<s>pitṛyajña</s>), the sacrifice to beings (<s>bhūtayajña</s>), the sacrifice to humans (<s>manuṣyayajña</s>), and the sacrifice to <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmayajña</s>).

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.2: Day after day one should make an offering with '<s>svāhā</s>' — even [with as little as] a piece of wood. Thus one completes this sacrifice to the gods.

body.translated_text:
Baudh2.6.11.7: <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is indeed the <s>brahmayajña</s> (sacrifice to Brahman). Of this <s>brahmayajña</s>, speech is the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle), the mind is the <s>upabhṛt</s> (secondary ladle), the eye is the <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed ladle), the intellect is the <s>sruva</s> (spoon), truth is the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath), and the heavenly world is the <s>udayana</s> (final rising). Whatever heavenly world one who gives this [entire earth] full of wealth would win, that world — and even greater and imperishable — he wins, [K omits: that world he wins,] and he conquers re-death, who, knowing thus,
recites <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study). Therefore <s>svādhyāya</s> should be studied — thus says the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (scriptural passage).

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.8: And they also cite [this verse]: Well-anointed, well-fed, lying on a comfortable bed — whatever sacrificial rite he studies, by that his [sacrifice] is [considered as] offered.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.9: Of this <s>dharma</s> (law) some declare a fourfold division, because [it is said] 'which are unseen' and 'which are four.' This is the doctrine concerning ritual action.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.10: [The fourfold division is] of the <s>aiṣṭika</s> (model sacrifices), <s>pāśuka</s> (animal sacrifices), <s>saumika</s> (Soma sacrifices), and <s>dārvihoma</s> (wood-ladle oblations) [K: <s>dārvīhoma</s>].

Baudh2.6.11.11: On this, this [verse] speaks:
The four paths leading to the gods that extend between heaven and earth —
among these, whichever one brings freedom from decay and freedom from defeat, to that [path] may all the gods assign us here.

body.text: Baudh2.6.11.12/ brahmacārī gṛhastho vānaprasthaḥ parivrājaka iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.12: [The four āśramas are:] the <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), the <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder), the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller), and the <s>parivrājaka</s> (wandering ascetic).

body.text: Baudh2.6.11.13/ brahmacārī guru.śuśrūṣī^ā maraṇāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.13: The <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student) serves his teacher until death.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.14: The <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) follows the practices prescribed in the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> scripture.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.15: The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> (forest hermit) lives in the forest, subsisting on roots and fruits, devoted to austerity, performing ritual ablution with water at the <s>savana</s> (pressing) times, having established the sacred fire according to the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> rite, not eating village food, worshipping gods, ancestors, spirits, humans, and sages, receiving all guests — he may use even alms-food, excluding what is forbidden. He should not stand upon ploughed ground nor enter a village. Wearing matted hair and clothed in bark and deer-skin, he should not eat [stored food] for more than a year.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.16: The <s>parivrājaka</s> (wandering ascetic), having renounced his kinsmen, without possessions, should go forth [K: wander forth] according to the prescribed rule.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.17: Having gone to the forest,

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.28: On this they cite [the following]: <s>Prahlādi</s>, the demon named <s>Kapila</s>, created these divisions while competing with the gods. A wise man should not regard them.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.6.11.29: Because [it is said] 'which are unseen' and 'which are four' — this is the doctrine concerning ritual action — of the <s>aiṣṭika</s> (model sacrifices), <s>pāśuka</s> (animal sacrifices), <s>saumika</s> (Soma sacrifices), and <s>dārvihoma</s> (wood-ladle oblations) [K: <s>dārvīhoma</s>].

Baudh2.6.11.30: On this, this [verse] is recited:
This is the eternal greatness of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — it is not increased by ritual action, nor is it diminished.
Knowing that very self, which is the knower of the path — one is not stained by evil action. (cf. Baudh2.10.17.7)
Baudh2.6.11.31: He should declare:
By which power the sun burns, kindled with splendor — the father honored through the son, womb after womb —
the one who does not know the <s>Veda</s> does not perceive that great, all-pervading <s>Ātman</s> (Self) in the hereafter [K: in the great hereafter].

body.text:

body.translated_text:
Baudh2.6.11.32: Those who move neither hither nor beyond, who are neither <s>brāhmaṇas</s> nor pressers of <s>Soma</s> —
they, resorting to evil speech, weave the weft to their own destruction.

body.text:
Baudh2.6.11.33/ prajābhir agne amṛtatvam (aśyām / jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhir ṛṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇa^ṛṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayāpitṛbhya iti / evam ṛṇa.saṃyoga.vādinyo^asaṃkhyeyā [K: ṛṇasaṃyogādīnyasaṃkhyeyāni] (bhavanti // (cf. Baudh2.9.16.7)

Baudh2.6.11.34-2/ (dhvaṃsate^anyat [K omits: dhvaṃsate 'nyat] praśaṃsann iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.6.11.33: 'Through offspring, O <s>Agni</s>, may I attain immortality.' A <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, indeed, is born with three debts: to the sages through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), to the gods through sacrifice, and to the ancestors through offspring. Thus innumerable [passages] speak of the connection with debts [K: debts and connections etc. are innumerable]. (cf. Baudh2.9.16.7)
Baudh2.6.11.34: The threefold knowledge, <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), procreation, faith, austerity, sacrifice, and giving —
whoever performs these, with them indeed we are; [all] other [doctrine], becoming dust, perishes — [so says he who] praises [the householder's life].
One who praises another [path] perishes [K omits: 'perishes, another praising'].

body.text: Baudh2.7.12.1/ atha śālīna.yāyāvarāṇām ātma.yājināṃ prāṇa.āhutīr(vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.7.12.1: Now we shall explain the <s>prāṇāhutis</s> (breath-oblations) of the <s>śālīnas</s> (settled householders) and <s>yāyāvaras</s> (wandering householders), who are <s>ātmayājins</s> (self-sacrificers).

body.translated_text: Baudh2.7.12.2: At the conclusion of all necessary [duties], having seated oneself facing east in a place that has been swept and smeared, [one receives] the food that is being brought; having saluted [it] with '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar om</s>' (earth, atmosphere, heaven, <s>Oṃ</s>), one should restrain one's speech.

body.translated_text:
Baudh2.7.12.3: Having circumambulated the food that has been placed [before him] with water, using the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances), and having sprinkled water around it clockwise, without releasing [food] from the left hand, [he says] 'You are <s>amṛtopasṭaraṇa</s> (the spreading of immortality).' Having sipped water from the front, he offers the five <s>prāṇāhutis</s> (breath-oblations) with five [portions of] food: 'Established in <s>prāṇa</s>, I offer immortality. Enter me benignly, without burning. To <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Established in <s>apāna</s>, I offer immortality. Enter me benignly, without burning. To <s>apāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Established in <s>vyāna</s>, I offer immortality.
To <s>vyāna</s>, enter me benignly, without burning. To <s>vyāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Established in <s>udāna</s>, I offer immortality. Enter me benignly, without burning. To <s>udāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! Established in <s>samāna</s>, I offer immortality. Enter me benignly, without burning. To <s>samāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' [K omits: 'Established in apāna ... To samāna, svāhā.']
Baudh2.7.12.4: Having offered the five <s>prāṇāhutis</s> (breath-oblations) with five [portions of] food, he should continue eating silently, meditating on <s>Prajāpati</s> with his mind. He should not release speech in between.

body.translated_text: Baudh2.7.12.6: If he sees skin, hair, nails, insects, mouse [droppings], or excrement, he should remove that portion [of food] along with that spot, sprinkle [the rest] with water, scatter ashes [over it], sprinkle again with water, and then continue eating while [verbally] praising [the food].

Baudh2.7.12.7: And they also cite [this verse]:
Seated facing east, one should eat silently, without criticizing the food,
without spilling, with concentrated mind; and after eating, one should touch fire [or water].

body.translated_text: Baudh2.7.12.9: One should not eat too much.

By this food, may you be nourished.'

Nourish <s>prāṇa</s> with food! Having entered <s>udāna</s> with faith, the immortal has been offered. Nourish <s>prāṇa</s> with food! Having entered <s>samāna</s> with faith, the immortal has been

one should eat the remnants silently. Thus is <s>dharma</s> (the law) ordained.

body.text:
Baudh2.7.13.7-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.7.13.7-2ab/ aṣṭau grāsā muner bhakṣyāḥ ṣoḍaśa^araṇya.vāsinaḥ /
Baudh2.7.13.7-2cd/ dvātriṃśat tu [K: dvātriṃśataṃ] gṛhasthasya amitaṃ [K:gṛhasthasyāparimitaṃ] brahmacāriṇaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.7.13.7: And they also cite [this verse]:
Eight morsels are the food of a sage, sixteen for a forest-dweller,
thirty-two for a householder, and unlimited [K: and unrestricted] for a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student).

body.text:
Baudh2.7.13.8ab/ āhita.agnir anaḍvāṃś ca brahmacārī ca te trayaḥ /
Baudh2.7.13.8cd/ aśnanta eva sidhyanti na^eṣāṃ siddhir anaśnatām // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.7.13.8: One who maintains the sacred fires, an ox [that labors], and a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) — these three
succeed by eating; for them there is no success through fasting.

body.text:
Baudh2.7.13.9ab/ gṛhastho brahmacārī vā yo^anaśnaṃs tu tapaś (caret /
Baudh2.7.13.9cd/ prāṇa.agnihotra.lopena avakīrṇī (bhavet tu saḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.7.13.9: A householder or a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) who practices austerity by not eating,
through the neglect of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> (breath-fire-oblation), becomes one who has broken his vow.

body.text: Baudh2.7.13.10/ anyatra prāyaścittāt / prāyaścitte tad eva vidhānam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.7.13.10: Except in the case of a <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation). In [the case of] expiation, the same procedure [applies].

body.text:
Baudh2.7.13.11-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.7.13.11-2ab/ antarā prātar.āśaṃ ca sāyam.āśaṃ tathā^eva ca /
Baudh2.7.13.11-2cd/ sadā.upavāsī (bhavati yo na (bhuṅkte kadācana [K:kadācaneti] //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.7.13.11-1: And further, they cite:
Baudh2.7.13.11-2ab: Between the morning meal and the evening meal likewise,
Baudh2.7.13.11-2cd: one who never eats at any time is always an observer of <s>upavāsa</s> (fasting).

body.text:
Baudh2.7.13.12ab/ prāṇa.agnihotra.mantrāṃs tu niruddhe bhojane (japet /
Baudh2.7.13.12cd/ tretā.agnihotra.mantrāṃs tu dravya.alābhe yathā (japet //iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.7.13.12ab: When food is withheld, one should recite the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> (vital fire-oblation) <s>mantras</s>,
Baudh2.7.13.12cd: just as one would recite the <s>tretāgnihotra</s> (triple fire-oblation) <s>mantras</s> when materials are unavailable.

body.text: Baudh2.7.13.13/ evam ācaran [K: evam evācaran] brahma.bhūyāya (kalpate /brahma.bhūyāya (kalpata iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.7.13.13: One who conducts himself thus [K: one who conducts himself exactly thus] becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s> — he becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.1/ pitryam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ yaśasyaṃ puṣṭi.karma ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.1: [The <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite)] is related to the ancestors, bestows long life, leads to heaven, brings fame, and is an act of nourishment.

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.2/ trimadhus triṇāciketas trisuparṇaḥ pañca.agniḥṣaḍaṅga.vit^śīrṣako jyeṣṭhasāmakaḥ snātaka iti paṅkti.pāvanāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.2: A <s>trimadhu</s> (knower of the three honey verses), a <s>triṇāciketa</s> (thrice-performer of the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire), a <s>trisuparṇa</s> (knower of the three <s>Suparṇa</s> hymns), a <s>pañcāgni</s> (maintainer of five fires), a knower of the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, a <s>śīrṣaka</s>, a singer of the <s>Jyeṣṭha Sāman</s>, and a <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic studentship) — these are the purifiers of the row.

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.3/ tad.abhāve rahasya.vit //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.3: In their absence, a knower of the <s>Rahasya</s> (secret Upaniṣadic texts).

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.4/ ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni^iti śrāddhasya mahimā / tasmādevaṃ.vidaṃ sapiṇḍam apy (āśayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.4: <s>Ṛc</s> verses, <s>Yajus</s> formulas, and <s>Sāman</s> chants — this is the greatness of the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite). Therefore, one should feed even a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> (near kinsman) who possesses such knowledge.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.14.5ab/ rākṣoghnāni ca sāmāni svadhāvanti yajūṃṣi ca /
Baudh2.8.14.5cd/ madhv.ṛco^atha pavitrāṇi (śrāvayed āśayan^śanaiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.14.5ab: <s>Sāmans</s> that destroy <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), <s>Yajus</s> formulas containing <s>svadhā</s>,
Baudh2.8.14.5cd: honey <s>Ṛc</s> verses, and purificatory hymns — one should have these recited softly while feeding [the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>].

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.6/ caraṇa.vato^anūcānān yoni.gotra.mantra.asaṃbaddhān[K.asambandhān]^śucīn mantravatas try.avarān ayujaḥ pūrvedyuḥ prātar evavā (nimantrya sa.darbha.upakḷpteṣv āsaneṣu prāṅ.mukhān (upaveśayatyudaṅ.mukhān vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.6: Having invited — either on the preceding day or in the morning itself — learned men of good conduct, scholars who are not connected [to the host] by descent, <s>gotra</s> (lineage), or <s>mantra</s> [K: who are unrelated], who are pure, who know the <s>mantras</s>, at least three in number, and odd in number — one seats them facing east, or facing north, on seats prepared with <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass).

body.text:
Baudh2.8.14.7/ atha^enāṃs tila.miśrā apaḥ (pratigrāhya gandhair mālyaiśca^(alaṃkṛtya / agnau (kariṣyāmi^iti / anujñāto^gnim (upasamādhāya(saṃparistīrya^ā^agnimukhāt (kṛtvā^annasya^eva [K: kṛtvājyasyaiva]tisra āhutīr (juhoti / somāya pitṛ.pītāya svadhā namaḥ svāhā /yamāya^aṅgirasvate pitṛmate svadhā namaḥ svāhā / agnayekavya.vāhanāya sviṣṭakṛte svadhā namaḥ
svāhā^iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.14.7: Then, having offered them water mixed with sesame seeds, and having adorned them with perfumes and garlands — saying 'I shall make an offering in the fire' — having received permission, one kindles the fire, strews [grass] around it, and having performed the preliminary rite up to the <s>agnimukhā</s> (fire-facing), one offers three oblations of food itself [K: of ghee itself]: '<s>Svadhā</s>, obeisance, <s>svāhā</s> — to <s>Soma</s>, drunk by the ancestors'; '<s>Svadhā</s>, obeisance, <s>svāhā</s> — to <s>Yama</s>, descended from <s>Aṅgiras</s>, accompanied by the ancestors'; '<s>Svadhā</s>, obeisance,
<s>svāhā</s> — to <s>Agni</s>, the carrier of <s>Kavya</s> (offerings to the dead), the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings).'

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.8/ tat.śeṣeṇa^annam (abhighārya^annasya^etā eva tisro [K: tisraāhutīr] (juhuyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.8: Having sprinkled the food with the remainder of that [ghee], one should offer these same three oblations [K: three oblations] of food.

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.9/ vayasāṃ piṇḍaṃ (dadyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.9: One should give a <s>piṇḍa</s> (rice ball offering) for the birds.

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.10/ vayasāṃ hi pitaraḥ pratimayā (caranti^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.10: For it is known through revelation that the ancestors move about in the form of birds.

body.text: Baudh2.8.14.11/ atha^itarat sa.aṅguṣṭhena pāṇinā^(abhimṛśati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.14.11: Then, with the other [hand], he touches [the food] with the palm including the thumb.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.14.12-1/ pṛthivī.samantasya [K: pṛthivīsamaṃ tasya] te^agnir(upadraṣṭā^ṛcas te mahimā dattasya^apramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇas tvā mukhe (juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā vidyāvatāṃprāṇa.apānayor (juhomy akṣitam (asi mā pitqṇāṃ (kṣeṣṭhā amutra^amuṣmiṃloka iti /
Baudh2.8.14.12-2/ antarikṣa.samantasya [K: antarikṣassamaṃ tasya] te vāyur(upaśrotā yajūṃṣi te mahimā dattasya^apramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃdyaur apidhānaṃ brahmaṇas tvā mukhe (juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvāvidyāvatāṃ prāṇa.apānayor (juhomy akṣitam (asi mā pitāmahānāṃ(kṣeṣṭhā amutra^amuṣmiṃ loka iti /
Baudh2.8.14.12-3/ dyu.samantasya [K: dyausamaṃ tasya] ta ādityo^anukhyātāsāmāni te mahimā dattasya apramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇas tvā mukhe (juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā vidyāvatāṃprāṇa.apānayor (juhomy akṣitam (asi mā prapitāmahānāṃ (kṣeṣṭhāamutra^amuṣmiṃ loka iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.14.12-1: 'Equal to the earth — for you, <s>Agni</s> is the witness; the <s>Ṛc</s> verses are your greatness; for the non-neglect of what is given, the earth is your vessel, heaven your cover. I offer you into the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>; I offer you into the <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (outbreath) of learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. You are imperishable; may you not be diminished among the ancestors, in that world yonder.'
Baudh2.8.14.12-2: 'Equal to the atmosphere — for you, <s>Vāyu</s> is the listener; the <s>Yajus</s> formulas are your greatness; for the non-neglect of what is given, the earth is your vessel, heaven your cover. I offer you into the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>; I offer you into the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> of learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. You are imperishable; may you not be diminished among the grandfathers, in that world yonder.'
Baudh2.8.14.12-3: 'Equal to heaven — for you, <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is the proclaimer; the <s>Sāman</s> chants are your greatness; for the non-neglect of what is given, the earth is your vessel, heaven your cover. I offer you into the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>; I offer you into the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> of learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. You are imperishable; may you not be diminished among the great-grandfathers, in that world yonder.'

body.text: Baudh2.8.15.1/ atha vai (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.15.1: Now indeed it is stated:

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.2ab/ agnau karaṇa.śeṣeṇa tad annam (abhighārayet /
Baudh2.8.15.2cd/ nir.aṅguṣṭhaṃ tu yad dattaṃ na tat (prīṇāti vai pitqn //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.2ab: With the remainder of the fire-offering, one should sprinkle that food;
Baudh2.8.15.2cd: but what is given without the thumb does not indeed satisfy the ancestors.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.3ab/ ubhayoḥ śākhayor muktaṃ pitṛbhyo^annaṃ niveditam /
Baudh2.8.15.3cd/ tad antaram (upāsante asurā [K: upāsante 'surā vai]duṣṭa.cetasaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.3ab: The food offered to the ancestors, released between both branches [of the fingers],
Baudh2.8.15.3cd: is intercepted by <s>Asuras</s> (demons) of wicked mind who lurk in between.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.4ab/ yātudhānāḥ piśācāś ca (pratilumpanti tat^haviḥ /
Baudh2.8.15.4cd/ tila.dāne hy adāyāś ca tathā krodha.vaśe^asurāḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.4ab: <s>Yātudhānas</s> (sorcerers) and <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls) plunder that oblation;
Baudh2.8.15.4cd: through the giving of sesame, however, those <s>Asuras</s> who are under the sway of anger become powerless.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.5ab/ kāṣāya.vāsā yān (kurute japa.homa.pratigrahān /
Baudh2.8.15.5cd/ na tad devaṃ.gamaṃ [K: devagamaṃ] bhavati havya.kavyeṣuyat^haviḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.5ab: Whatever recitations, fire-oblations, and gifts one who wears ochre robes performs,
Baudh2.8.15.5cd: that oblation among <s>havya</s> (offerings to gods) and <s>kavya</s> (offerings to ancestors) does not reach the gods.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.6ab/ yac ca dattam anaṅguṣṭhaṃ yac ca^eva (pratigṛhyate /
Baudh2.8.15.6cd/ ācāmati ca yas tiṣṭhan na sa tena (samṛdhyate // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.6ab: And what is given without the thumb, and what is received [likewise],
Baudh2.8.15.6cd: and one who sips water while standing — he does not prosper thereby.

body.text: Baudh2.8.15.7/ ādy.antayor apāṃ pradānaṃ sarvatra //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.15.7: The giving of water [is prescribed] at the beginning and at the end, in all [rites].

body.text: Baudh2.8.15.8/ jaya.prabhṛti yathā.vidhānam //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.15.8: [The recitations] beginning with <s>Jaya</s> are according to the prescribed procedure.

body.text: Baudh2.8.15.9/ śeṣam uktam aṣṭakā.home //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.8.15.9: The rest has been stated in [the section on] the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> (eighth-day) oblation.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.10ab/ dvau daive [K: deve] pitṛ.kārye trīn ekaikam ubhayatra vā /
Baudh2.8.15.10cd/ (bhojayet susamṛddho^api na (prasajyeta [K: prasajjeta] vistare //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.10ab: Two [<s>brāhmaṇas</s>] for a rite for the gods, three for an ancestral rite, or one for each in both cases;
Baudh2.8.15.10cd: even one who is very prosperous should feed [only this many] and not indulge in lavishness.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.11ab/ satkriyāṃ deśa.kālau ca śaucaṃ brāhmaṇa.saṃpadam /
Baudh2.8.15.11cd/ pañca^etān vistaro (hanti tasmāt taṃ (parivarjayet //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.11ab: Proper hospitality, [appropriate] place and time, purity, and the excellence of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> —
Baudh2.8.15.11cd: lavishness destroys these five; therefore one should avoid it.

body.text:
Baudh2.8.15.12ab/ urastaḥ pitaras tasya vāmataś ca pitāmahāḥ /
Baudh2.8.15.12cd/ dakṣiṇataḥ prapitāmahāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ piṇḍa.tarkakāḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.8.15.12ab: In front of him [are seated those representing] the fathers, to his left the grandfathers,
Baudh2.8.15.12cd: to his right the great-grandfathers, and behind him those who examine the <s>piṇḍas</s> (rice ball offerings).

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.1/ prajā.kāmasya^upadeśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.1: [Now follows] the instruction for one who desires offspring.

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.2/ prajanana.nimittā samākhyā^ity aśvināv (ūcatuḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.2: The <s>Aśvins</s> (divine twin physicians) said: 'The designation [of a person] is based on [their] procreation.'

body.text:
Baudh2.9.16.3ab/ āyuṣā tapasā yuktaḥ svādhyāya.ijyā.parāyaṇaḥ /
Baudh2.9.16.3cd/ prajām (utpādayed yuktaḥ sve.sve varṇe [K: vaṃśe]jita.indriyaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.9.16.3ab: Endowed with longevity and <s>tapas</s> (austerity), devoted to <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) and <s>ijyā</s> (sacrifice),
Baudh2.9.16.3cd: one who has controlled his senses should beget offspring diligently, within one's own <s>varṇa</s> (social class) [K: lineage].

body.text:
Baudh2.9.16.4ab/ brāhmaṇasya^ṛṇa.saṃyogas tribhir (bhavati janmataḥ /
Baudh2.9.16.4cd/ tāni mucya^ātmavān (bhavati vimukto dharma.saṃśayāt //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.9.16.4ab: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is born with a threefold debt from birth;
Baudh2.9.16.4cd: having discharged these, one becomes self-possessed, freed from the uncertainty regarding <s>dharma</s> (duty).

body.text:
Baudh2.9.16.5ab/ svādhyāyena ṛṣīn (pūjya somena ca puraṃdaram /
Baudh2.9.16.5cd/ prajayā ca pitqn pūrvān anṛṇo divi (modate //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.9.16.5ab: Having honored the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) through <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) through <s>Soma</s> sacrifice,
Baudh2.9.16.5cd: and the ancestors through offspring — being free of debt, one rejoices in heaven.

body.text:
Baudh2.9.16.6ab/ putreṇa lokāñ (jayati pautreṇa^anantyam [K: pautreṇāmṛtam](aśnute /
Baudh2.9.16.6cd/ atha putrasya pautreṇa nākam eva^(adhirohati // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.9.16.6ab: Through a son one conquers the worlds, through a grandson one attains infinity [K: immortality],
Baudh2.9.16.6cd: and through the grandson of a son one ascends to the highest heaven.

body.text:
Baudh2.9.16.7/ (vijñāyate ca / jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇas tribhir ṛṇavā(jāyate brahmacaryeṇa^ṛṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhya iti /evam ṛṇa.saṃyogaṃ vedo (darśayati // (cf. Baudh2.6.11.33)
Baudh2.9.16.8/ sat.putram (utpādya^ātmānaṃ (tārayati //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.9.16.7: And it is known through revelation: 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is born with three debts — to the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) through <s>brahmacarya</s> (Vedic studentship), to the gods through sacrifice, and to the ancestors through offspring.' Thus the <s>Veda</s> shows the connection with debt. (cf. Baudh2.6.11.33)
Baudh2.9.16.8: Having begotten a virtuous son, one saves oneself.

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.9/ sapta^avarān sapta pūrvān ṣaḍ anyān ātma.saptamān / sat.putram adhigacchānas (tārayaty enaso bhayāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.9: One who obtains a virtuous son saves seven [generations] below, seven above, six others, and himself as the seventh — from the fear of sin.

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.10/ tasmāt prajā.saṃtānam (utpādya phalam (avāpnoti [K: phalaṃ prāpnoti] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.10: Therefore, by producing a line of offspring, one obtains the fruit [of dharma].

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.11/ tasmād yatnavān prajām (utpādayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.11: Therefore, one should strive diligently to beget offspring.

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.12/ auṣadha.mantra.saṃyogena //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.12: By means of herbs, <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), and their combination.

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.13/ tasya^upadeśaḥ śruti.sāmānyena^(upadiśyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.13: The instruction for this is taught on the basis of Vedic authority.

body.text: Baudh2.9.16.14/ sarva.varṇebhyaḥ phalavattvād [K: phalattvād] iti /phalavattvād [K: phalattvād] iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.9.16.14: [This applies] to all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), because it bears fruit — because it bears fruit.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.1/ atha^ataḥ saṃnyāsa.vidhiṃ (vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.1: Now, from here, we shall explain the procedure for <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation).

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.2/ so^ata eva brahmacaryavān (pravrajati^ity ekeṣām //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.2: According to some, one who has [completed] <s>brahmacarya</s> (Vedic studentship) may renounce directly from that [stage].

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.3/ atha śālīna.yāyāvarāṇām anapatyānām //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.3: And [it is also prescribed] for <s>śālīnas</s> (settled householders) and <s>yāyāvaras</s> (wandering householders) who are without offspring.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.4/ vidhuro vā prajāḥ svadharme (pratiṣṭhāpya vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.4: Or one who is bereft [of his wife], or one who has established his offspring in their proper duties.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.5/ saptatyā ūrdhvaṃ saṃnyāsam (upadiśanti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.5: They prescribe <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) after [the age of] seventy.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.6/ vānaprasthasya vā karma.virāme //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.6: Or for a <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller), upon the cessation of ritual duties.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.17.7ab/ eṣa nityo mahimā brāhmaṇasya na karmaṇā (vardhate nokanīyān /
Baudh2.10.17.7cd/ tasya^eva^ātmā padavit taṃ (viditvā na karmaṇā (lipyatepāpakena // iti // (cf. Baudh2.6.11.30)
Baudh2.10.17.8/ apunarbhavaṃ (nayati^iti nityaḥ //
Baudh2.10.17.9/ mahad enaṃ (gamayati^iti mahimā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.9: [It is called] 'greatness' because it leads one to the great [<s>Brahman</s>].

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.10/ keśa.śmaśru.loma.nakhāni (vāpayitvā^(upakalpayate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.10: Having shaved the hair of the head, beard, body hair, and nails, one prepares [for renunciation].

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.11/ yaṣṭayaḥ śikyaṃ jala.pavitraṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ pātram iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.11: [The equipment consists of:] staffs, a carrying sling, a water-strainer, a <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water pot), and a bowl.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.12/ etat (samādāya grāma.ante grāma.sīmānte^agny.agārevā^ājyaṃ payo dadhi^iti trivṛt (prāśya^upavaset //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.12: Having taken up these, at the village boundary, at the village border, or in the fire-house, one consumes a triple [mixture of] ghee, milk, and yogurt, and then observes a fast.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.13/ apo vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.13: Or [just] water.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.14/ oṃ bhūḥ sāvitrīṃ (praviśāmi tat savitur vareṇyam / oṃbhuvaḥ sāvitrīṃ (praviśāmi bhargo devasya dhīmahi / oṃ suvaḥ sāvitrīṃ(praviśāmi dhiyo yo naḥ (pracodayād iti / paccho(pad.śas)^ardharcaśastataḥ samastayā ca vyastayā ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.14: '<s>Oṃ bhūḥ</s>, I enter the <s>Sāvitrī</s> — <s>tat savitur vareṇyam</s>'; '<s>Oṃ bhuvaḥ</s>, I enter the <s>Sāvitrī</s> — <s>bhargo devasya dhīmahi</s>'; '<s>Oṃ suvaḥ</s>, I enter the <s>Sāvitrī</s> — <s>dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt</s>.' [One recites it] foot by foot, half-verse by half-verse, then as a whole and in parts.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.15/ ātmānam ātmana [K omits: ātmānam ātmana] āśramādāśramam (upanīya brahma.pūto (bhavati^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.15: Having led oneself [K omits: having led oneself] from <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage) to <s>āśrama</s>, one becomes purified by <s>Brahman</s> — thus it is known through revelation.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.17.16-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.10.17.16-2ab/ āśramād āśramaṃ (gatvā huta.homo jita.indriyaḥ /
Baudh2.10.17.16-2cd/ bhikṣā.bali.pariśrāntaḥ paścād (bhavati bhikṣukaḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.17.16-1: And further, they cite:
Baudh2.10.17.16-2ab: Having gone from <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage) to <s>āśrama</s>, having performed oblations, with senses conquered,
Baudh2.10.17.16-2cd: exhausted by [the discipline of] alms-giving and <s>bali</s> (food offerings), one finally becomes a <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant).

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.17/ sa eṣa bhikṣur ānantyāya //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.17: This <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) [attains] infinity.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.18/ purā^ādityasya^astamayād gārhapatyam(upasamādhāya^anvāhāryapacanam (āhṛtya jvalantam āhavanīyam(uddhṛtya gārhapatya ājyaṃ (vilāpya^(utpūya sruci catur.gṛhītaṃ(gṛhītvā samidvaty āhavanīye pūrṇa.āhutiṃ (juhoti / oṃ svāhā^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.18: Before sunset, having kindled the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household) fire, having brought the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern) fire, having taken up the blazing <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering) fire, having melted ghee in the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, having purified it and taken a four-fold portion in the ladle, one offers a full oblation in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> with fuel, [saying] '<s>Oṃ svāhā</s>.'

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.19/ etad brahma.anvādhānam iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.19: This is known through revelation as the <s>brahmānvādhāna</s> (the placing of the sacred fire into <s>Brahman</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.20/ atha sāyaṃ hute^agnihotra uttareṇa gārhapatyaṃ tṛṇāni(saṃstīrya teṣu dvaṃdvaṃ nyañci pātrāṇi (sādayitvādakṣiṇena^āhavanīyaṃ brahma.āyatane darbhān (saṃstīrya teṣukṛṣṇa.ajinaṃ ca^(antardhāya^etāṃ rātriṃ (jāgarti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.20: Then, after the evening <s>agnihotra</s> (fire oblation) has been offered, to the north of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire one spreads grass, and on it one places the [ritual] vessels upside down in pairs; and to the south of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, in the place of <s>Brahman</s>, one spreads <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), and having placed a black antelope skin between [the grasses], one keeps vigil through that night.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.21/ ya evaṃ vidvān brahma.rātrim (upoṣya brāhmaṇo^agnīn [K:upoṣyāgnīn] (samāropya (pramīyate sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ (tarati (taratibrahma.hatyām //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.21: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who, possessing this knowledge, fasts on the night of <s>Brahman</s>, places the fires within himself, and then dies — he crosses over all sin, he crosses over [even] the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>).

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.22/ atha brāhme muhūrta (utthāya kāla eva prātar.agnihotraṃ(juhoti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.22: Then, having risen at the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (auspicious pre-dawn hour), one offers the morning <s>agnihotra</s> (fire oblation) at the proper time.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.23/ atha pṛṣṭhyāṃ (stīrtvā^apaḥ (praṇīya vaiśvānaraṃdvādaśa.kapālaṃ (nirvapati / sā prasiddha.iṣṭiḥ (saṃtiṣṭhate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.23: Then, having spread [grass] on the back [of the altar], having brought forward water, one prepares the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> offering on twelve potsherds. That established <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice) is thus completed.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.24/ āhavanīye^agnihotra.pātrāṇi (prakṣipaty amṛnmayānyanaśmamayāni [K: prakṣiped amṛṇmayāny anāyasāni] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.24: One casts the <s>agnihotra</s> vessels into the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire — those that are not made of clay nor of stone [K: not made of clay nor of metal].

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.25/ gārhapatye^araṇī / (bhavataṃ naḥ samanasāv iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.25: [One places] the fire-churning sticks into the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire, saying]: 'May you two be of one mind for us.'

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.26/ ātmany [K: athātmany] agnīn (samāropayate / yā te agneyajñiyā tanūr iti tris trir ekaikaṃ (samājighrati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.26: He places the fires upon himself. With [the verse] 'That body of yours which belongs to the sacrificial fire,' he smells each one three times, three times.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.27/ atha^antarvedi tiṣṭhan / oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ saṃnyastaṃmayā saṃnyastaṃ mayā saṃnyastaṃ mayā^iti / trir upāṃśu^(uktvā triruccaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.27: Then, standing within the <s>vedi</s> (sacrificial enclosure): '<s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>suvaḥ</s> — it has been renounced by me, it has been renounced by me, it has been renounced by me.' He utters this three times in a low voice and three times aloud.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.28/ triṣatyā hi devā iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.28: For it is known [from revelation]: 'The gods are three hundred [and thirty-three].'

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.29/ abhayaṃ sarva.bhūtebhyo matta iti ca^apāṃ pūrṇam añjaliṃ(ninayati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.29: [Saying] 'Safety from me to all beings,' he pours down a handful full of water.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.17.30-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.10.17.30-2ab/ abhayaṃ sarva.bhūtebhyo (dattvā yaś (carate muniḥ /
Baudh2.10.17.30-2cd/ na tasya sarva.bhūtebhyo bhayaṃ ca^api^iha [K: cāpi ha](jāyate // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.17.30: And they also cite [the following verse]:
Having given safety to all beings, the <s>muni</s> (sage) who wanders [thus] —
from all beings no fear arises for him in this world.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.31/ sa vācaṃyamo (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.31: He observes <s>vācaṃyama</s> (restraint of speech).

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.32/ sakhā mā [K: me] (gopāya^iti daṇḍam (ādatte //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.32: With [the verse] 'O friend, protect me,' [K: 'protect me'] he takes up the staff.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.33/ yad asya pāre rajasa iti śikyaṃ (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.33: With [the verse] 'That which is beyond the dust,' he takes the sling.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.34/ yena devāḥ pavitreṇa^iti jala.pavitraṃ (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.34: With [the verse] 'By which purifying [instrument] the gods [purify],' he takes the water-strainer.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.35/ yena devā jyotiṣā^ūrdhvā (udāyann iti kamaṇḍaluṃ (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.35: With [the verse] 'By which light the gods rose upward,' he takes the <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water-pot).

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.36/ sapta.vyāhṛtibhiḥ pātraṃ (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.36: With the seven <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) he takes the bowl.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.17.37/ yaṣṭayaḥ śikyaṃ jala.pavitraṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ pātram ity etat(samādāya yatra^āpas tatra [K: tad] (gatvā (snātva^apa (ācamyasurabhimatyā^abliṅgābhir vāruṇībhir hiraṇyavarṇābhiḥ pāvamānībhiriti (mārjayitvā^antar.jala.gato^aghamarṣaṇena ṣoḍaśa prāṇa.āyāmān(dhārayitvā^(uttīrya vāsaḥ (pīḍayitvā^anyat prayataṃ vāsaḥ(paridhāya^apa (ācamya / oṃ bhūr
bhuvaḥ suvar iti / jala.pavitram(ādāya (tarpayati / oṃ bhūs (tarpayāmi / oṃ bhuvas (tarpayāmi / oṃsuvas (tarpayāmi / oṃ mahas (tarpayāmi / oṃ janas (tarpayāmi / oṃ tapas(tarpayāmi / oṃ satyaṃ (tarpayāmi^iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.17.37: Having collected the staffs, sling, water-strainer, <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water-pot), and bowl, he goes to where there is water. Having bathed, having sipped water, having purified himself with [the hymns] <s>Surabhimatī</s>, <s>Abliṅgā</s>, <s>Vāruṇī</s>, <s>Hiraṇyavarṇā</s>, and <s>Pāvamānī</s>, having entered the water and held sixteen <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-restraints) with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> [hymn], having come out, having wrung out his garment, having put on another clean garment, having sipped water — [reciting] '<s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūḥ</s>,
<s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>suvaḥ</s>' — taking the water-strainer, he makes libations: '<s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūḥ</s>, I satiate. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, I satiate. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>suvaḥ</s>, I satiate. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>mahaḥ</s>, I satiate. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>janaḥ</s>, I satiate. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>tapaḥ</s>, I satiate. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>satyam</s>, I satiate.'

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.38/ devavat [K omits devavat] pitṛbhyo^añjalim (ādāya [K:upādāya] / oṃ bhūḥ svadhā / oṃ bhuvaḥ svadhā / oṃ suvaḥ svadhā / oṃbhūr bhuvaḥ suvar mahar nama iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.38: As for the gods, taking a handful [of water] for the ancestors [K omits 'as for the gods']: '<s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūḥ</s> <s>svadhā</s>. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhuvaḥ</s> <s>svadhā</s>. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>suvaḥ</s> <s>svadhā</s>. <s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūḥ</s> <s>bhuvaḥ</s> <s>suvaḥ</s> <s>mahaḥ</s> <s>namaḥ</s>.'

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.39/ atha / ud u tyam / citram iti / dvābhyām ādityam (upatiṣṭhate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.39: Then, with [the two verses] 'Up that [bright one]' and '<s>Citram</s> (the brilliant one),' he worships the sun.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.40/ om iti brahma brahma vā eṣa jyotir ya eṣa (tapaty eṣa vedo[K: om ... eṣa jyotiḥ ya eṣa jyotiḥ ya eṣa tarpatyaiṣa vedā] ya eṣa(tapati [K: ya eva tarpayati] vedyam eva^etad ya eṣa (tapati [K: tarpayati]/ evam eva^eṣa ātmānaṃ (tarpayati / ātmane namas.(karoti / ātmābrahma^ātmā jyotiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.40: '<s>Oṃ</s>' is <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Brahman</s> indeed is that light which shines. That is the <s>Veda</s> [K: '<s>Oṃ</s>... that light which shines, that light which shines, which satisfies, that is the <s>Vedas</s>'] which shines [K: which satisfies]. That which shines [K: satisfies] is indeed the knowable. Thus he satisfies his own self. He makes obeisance to the self. The self is <s>Brahman</s>, the self is light.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.41/ sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva (āvartayet^śatakṛtvo^aparimitakṛtvo vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.41: He should repeat the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand times, or a hundred times, or an unlimited number of times.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.42/ oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar iti jala.pavitram [K: pavitram](ādāya^apo (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.42: [Reciting] '<s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūḥ</s> <s>bhuvaḥ</s> <s>suvaḥ</s>,' taking the water-strainer [K: the purifier], he takes water.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.43/ na^ata [K: na cāta] ūrdhvam anuddhṛtābhir adbhiraparisrutābhir aparipūtābhir vā^(ācāmet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.43: From this point onward, he should not sip water that has not been drawn up, not filtered, or not purified.

body.text: Baudh2.10.17.44/ na ca^ata ūrdhvaṃ śuklaṃ vāso (dhārayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.17.44: And from this point onward, he should not wear white garments.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.1/ eka.daṇḍī tri.daṇḍī vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.1: [He should be] either <s>ekadaṇḍī</s> (carrying a single staff) or <s>tridaṇḍī</s> (carrying a triple staff).

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.2/ atha^imāni vratāni (bhavanti / ahiṃsā satyam astainyaṃmaithunasya ca varjanam / tyāga ity eva //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.2: Now, these are the vows: <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing), abstinence from sexual intercourse, and <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) — these five.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.3/ pañca^eva^upavratāni (bhavanti / akrodhoguru.śuśrūṣā^apramādaḥ śaucam āhāra.śuddhiś ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.3: There are likewise five sub-vows: freedom from anger, service of the teacher, vigilance, purity, and purity of food.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.4/ atha bhaikṣa.caryā / brāhmaṇānāṃ śālīna.yāyāvarāṇāmapavṛtte vaiśvadeve bhikṣāṃ (lipseta //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.4: Now, [regarding] the begging-round: he should seek alms from <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>śālīna</s> (settled) and <s>yāyāvara</s> (wandering) [types], after the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering has been completed.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.5/ bhavat.pūrvāṃ (pracodayet [K: pracodayāt] //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.5: He should make his request beginning with the address '<s>bhavat</s>' (reverend sir).

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.6/ godoha.mātram [K: godohanamātram] (ākāṅkṣet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.6: He should wait [only] for the time [it takes to] milk a cow.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.7/ atha bhaikṣa.caryād (upāvṛtya [K: upāvṛttaḥ] śucau deśe(nyasya hasta.pādān (prakṣālya^ādityasya^agraṃ [K: agre] (nivedayet /ud u tyam / citram iti / brahmaṇe (nivedayate / brahma jajñānam iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.7: Then, having returned from the begging-round, having placed [the food] in a clean spot, having washed his hands and feet, he should first offer it to the sun with [the verses] 'Up that [bright one]' and '<s>Citram</s> (the brilliant one).' He offers to <s>Brahman</s> with [the verse] '<s>Brahman</s> was born first.'

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.8/ (vijñāyate / ādhāna.prabhṛti yajamāna eva^agnayo (bhavanti/ tasya prāṇo gārhapatyo^apāno^anvāhāryapacano vyāna āhavanīyaudāna.samānau sabhya.āvasathyau / pañca vā ete^agnaya ātma.sthāḥ /ātmany eva (juhoti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.8: It is known [from revelation]: 'From the establishment of the sacred fires onward, the fires become the sacrificer himself. His <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, his <s>apāna</s> (inbreath) is the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire, his <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath) is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, his <s>udāna</s> (upward breath) and <s>samāna</s> (equalizing breath) are the <s>Sabhya</s> and <s>Āvasathya</s> fires. These five fires are situated in the self. He makes offerings into the self alone.'

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.9/ sa eṣa ātma.yajña ātma.niṣṭha ātma.pratiṣṭha ātmānaṃkṣemaṃ nayati^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.9: 'This is the sacrifice of the self, established in the self, grounded in the self; it leads the self to well-being' — thus it is known [from revelation].

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.10/ bhūtebhyo dayā.pūrvaṃ (saṃvibhajya śeṣam adbhiḥ(saṃspṛśya^auṣadhavat (prāśnīyāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.10: Having compassionately shared with living beings, he should eat the remainder, touching it with water, as though it were medicine.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.18.11/ (prāśya^apa (ācamya jyotiṣmatyā^ādityam (upatiṣṭhate / udvayaṃ tamasas pari^iti / vāṅ ma āsan nasoḥ prāṇa iti (japitvā // [K:prāśyāpa ācamya vāṅ ma āsan nasoḥ prāṇa iti japitvājyotiṣmatyādityam upatiṣṭhate ud vayaṃ tamasas parīti ]
Baudh2.10.18.12ab/ ayācitam asaṃkḷptam upapannaṃ yadṛcchayā /
Baudh2.10.18.12cd/ āhāra.mātraṃ (bhuñjīta kevalaṃ prāṇa.yātrikam // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.18.11: Having eaten, having sipped water, he worships the sun with the <s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> [verse] — 'Up beyond the darkness we' — having recited 'May speech [abide] in my mouth, breath in my nostrils.' [K: Having eaten, having sipped water, having recited 'May speech [abide] in my mouth, breath in my nostrils,' he worships the sun with the <s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> — 'Up beyond the darkness we.']
Baudh2.10.18.12: One should eat only food that is unasked for, unplanned, and obtained by chance —
just enough for sustenance, solely for keeping body and breath together.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.18.13-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh2.10.18.13-2ab/ aṣṭau grāsā muner bhakṣyāḥ ṣoḍaśa^araṇya.vāsinaḥ /
Baudh2.10.18.13-2cd/ dvātriṃśat tu [K: dvātriṃśataṃ] gṛhasthasya amitaṃbrahmacāriṇaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.18.13: And they also cite [the following verse]:
Eight morsels are the food of a <s>muni</s> (sage), sixteen for a forest-dweller,
thirty-two for a householder, and unlimited for a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student).

body.text:
Baudh2.10.18.14ab/ bhaikṣaṃ vā sarva.varṇebhya eka.annaṃ vā dvijātiṣu /
Baudh2.10.18.14cd/ api vā sarva.varṇebhyo na ca^eka.annaṃ dvijātiṣu // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.18.14: Alms may be [collected] from all <s>varṇas</s> (classes), or food from one [house only] among the twice-born;
or even from all <s>varṇas</s>, but not food from one [house only] among the twice-born.

body.text:
Baudh2.10.18.15-1/ atha yatra^upaniṣadam ācāryā (bruvate tatra^(udāharanti /
Baudh2.10.18.15-2/sthāna.mauna.vīra.āsana.savana.upasparśana.caturtha.ṣaṣṭha.aṣṭama.kāla.vrata.yuktasya kaṇa.piṇyāka.yāvaka.dadhi.payo.vratatvaṃ ca^iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.18.15: Now, where teachers declare the <s>Upaniṣad</s> (esoteric teaching), they cite the following:
For one who is engaged in the observances of [alternating between] standing, silence, the heroic posture, the <s>savana</s> (pressing ritual), ritual bathing, and fasting on the fourth, sixth, and eighth [days] — the prescribed diet consists of grains, oil-cake, barley gruel, curds, and milk.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.16/ tatra maune yuktas traividya.vṛddhair ācāryair munibhiranyair vā^āśramibhir bahu.śrutair dantair [K omits dantair] dantānsaṃdhāya^antarmukha eva yāvad.artha.saṃbhāṣī [K: yāvadarthaṃsambhāṣīta] na strībhir [K omits: na strībhir] na yatra lopo(bhavati^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.16: Regarding silence: one who is engaged in it should converse only as much as necessary, with teeth pressed together and face turned inward, [only] with learned elders versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>, teachers, <s>munis</s> (sages), or other <s>āśramins</s> (those in the stages of life) of great learning and self-control — not with women. [For] 'Where there would be a lapse [in the vow]' — thus it is known [from revelation].

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.17/ sthāna.mauna.vīra.āsanānām anyatamena saṃprayogaḥ / natrayaṃ (saṃnipātayet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.17: One should employ any one of standing, silence, or the heroic posture. One should not combine all three.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.18/ yatra gataś ca yāvan.mātram (anuvratayed āpatsu na yatralopo (bhavati^iti (vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.18: Wherever he has gone, he should observe the vow to the extent possible. 'In emergencies, [one may relax the rule] where there would be no lapse' — thus it is known [from revelation].

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.19/ sthāna.mauna.vīra.āsana.savana.upasparśana.caturtha.ṣaṣṭha.aṣṭama.kāla.vrata.yuktasya / aṣṭau tāny avrataghnāni [K: avratadhvani]āpo mūlaṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ / havir brāhmaṇa.kāmyā ca guror vacanamauṣadham iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.19: For one engaged in the observances of standing, silence, the heroic posture, the <s>savana</s>, ritual bathing, and fasting on the fourth, sixth, and eighth [days] — these eight things do not break the vow: water, roots, ghee, milk, <s>havis</s> (oblation material), the wish of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the word of the teacher, and medicine.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.20/ sāyaṃ.prātar.agnihotra.mantrāñ (japet //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.20: He should recite the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation) mantras at evening and morning.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.21/ vāruṇībhiḥ [K: vāruṇobhis] sāyaṃ saṃdhyām (upasthāya [K:upatiṣṭhate] maitrībhiḥ prātaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.21: He should worship the evening twilight with <s>Vāruṇī</s> [verses] and the morning [twilight] with <s>Maitrī</s> [verses].

body.text:
Baudh2.10.18.22ab/ anagnir aniketaḥ (syād aśarmā^āśaraṇo muniḥ /
Baudh2.10.18.22cd/ bhaikṣa.arthī grāmam (anvicchet svādhyāye vācam(utsṛjed // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh2.10.18.22: The <s>muni</s> (sage) should be without fire, without a dwelling, without shelter, without refuge;
he should seek a village for alms, and he should release his voice in <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study).

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.23/ (vijñāyate ca / parimitā vā ṛcaḥ parimitāni sāmāniparimitāni yajūṃṣi / atha^etasya^eva^anto na^(asti yad brahma / tatpratigṛṇata (ācakṣīta / sa pratigara iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.23: And it is known [from revelation]: 'The <s>ṛcs</s> (verses) are limited, the <s>sāmans</s> (chants) are limited, the <s>yajus</s> (sacrificial formulas) are limited. But of this — of <s>Brahman</s> — there is no end. One who receives it should declare it. That is the <s>pratigara</s> (response).'

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.24/ evam eva^eṣa ā śarīra.vimokṣaṇād vṛkṣa.mūlikoveda.saṃnyāsī //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.24: Thus indeed, he is one who dwells at the root of a tree, a renouncer of the <s>Vedas</s>, until the release from the body.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.25/ vedo vṛkṣaḥ / tasya mūlaṃ praṇavaḥ / praṇava.ātmako vedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.25: The <s>Veda</s> is a tree. Its root is <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>). The <s>Veda</s> has <s>Praṇava</s> as its essence.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.26/ praṇavaṃ dhyāyan sapraṇavo [K: praṇavo brahma praṇavaṃdhyāyet praṇavo] brahma.bhūyāya (kalpata iti ha^(uvāca prajāpatiḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.26: 'One who meditates on <s>Praṇava</s> [K: '<s>Praṇava</s> is <s>Brahman</s>; one who meditates on <s>Praṇava</s>'] becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>' — thus spoke <s>Prajāpati</s>.

body.text: Baudh2.10.18.27/ sapta.vyāhṛtibhir brahma.bhājanaṃ (prakṣālayed iti /(prakṣālayed iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh2.10.18.27: With the seven <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) he should wash the <s>Brahman</s>-vessel — he should wash [it].

body.text: Baudh3.1.1/ atha śālīna.yāyāvara.cakracara.dharma.kāṅkṣiṇāṃ navabhirvṛttibhir vartamānānām //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.1: Now, [the rules] for those who desire the <s>dharma</s> (law) of the <s>śālīna</s> (settled householder), <s>yāyāvara</s> (wandering householder), and <s>cakracara</s> (itinerant), who live by nine modes of livelihood.

body.text: Baudh3.1.2/ teṣāṃ tad.vartanād vṛttir ity (ucyate //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.2: Their [mode of] livelihood is called <s>vṛtti</s> because they sustain themselves by it.

body.text: Baudh3.1.3/ śālā.āśrayatvāt^śālīnatvam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.3: The state of being a <s>śālīna</s> [derives] from dwelling in a house (<s>śālā</s>).

body.text: Baudh3.1.4/ vṛttyā varayā (yāti^iti yāyāvaratvam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.4: The state of being a <s>yāyāvara</s> [derives from the fact that] one goes with an excellent livelihood.

body.text: Baudh3.1.5/ anukrameṇa caraṇāc [K: anukramacaraṇāc] cakracaratvam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.5: The state of being a <s>cakracara</s> [derives] from going about in a circuit.

body.text: Baudh3.1.6/ tā (anuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.6: We shall explain these in order.

body.text: Baudh3.1.7/ ṣaṇṇivartanī kauddālī [K: koddālī] dhruvā saṃprakṣālanīsamūhā phālanī [K: pālinī] śiloñchā [K: siloñchā] kāpotāsiddhecchā^iti nava^etāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.7: [The nine are:] <s>ṣaṇnivartanī</s> (six-field gleaning), <s>kauddālī</s> (hoe-gleaning), <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed), <s>saṃprakṣālanī</s> (washing-gleaning), <s>samūhā</s> (sweeping), <s>phālanī</s> (ploughshare-gleaning) [K: <s>pālinī</s>], <s>śiloñchā</s> (ear-gleaning) [K: <s>siloñchā</s>], <s>kāpotā</s> (pigeon-mode), and <s>siddhecchā</s> (accepting what comes ready) — these are the nine.

body.text: Baudh3.1.8/ tāsām eva vānyā^api daśamī vṛttir [K: vṛddhir] (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.8: Of these, there is also another, a tenth mode of livelihood [K: growth].

body.text: Baudh3.1.9/ ā navavṛtteḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.9: Up to the ninth mode of livelihood.

body.text: Baudh3.1.10/ keśa.śmaśru.loma.nakhāni (vāpayitvā^(upakalpayate //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.10: Having had his hair, beard, body-hair, and nails shaved, he prepares himself.

body.text: Baudh3.1.11/ kṛṣṇa.ajinaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ yaṣṭiṃ vīvadhaṃ kutapahāram [K:kuthahārim] iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.11: [He prepares] a black antelope skin, a <s>kamaṇḍalu</s> (water-pot), a staff, a carrying-pole, and a blanket-wrap [K: a blanket-carrier].

body.text: Baudh3.1.12/ traidhātavīyena^iṣṭvā (prasthāsyati vaiśvānaryā vā //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.12: Having performed the <s>Traidhātavīya</s> sacrifice, he will set out; or [having performed] the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> [offering].

body.text: Baudh3.1.13/ atha [K omits atha] prātar udita āditye yathā.sūtram agnīn(prajvālya gārhapatya ājyaṃ (vilāpya^(utpūya sruk.sruvaṃ (niṣṭapya(saṃmṛjya sruci catur.gṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā^āhavanīye vāstoṣpatīyaṃ(juhoti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.13: Then, in the morning after the sun has risen, having kindled the fires according to the prescribed rules, having melted ghee on the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, having purified it, having heated the ladle and the dipping-spoon, having wiped them, having taken four portions [of ghee] in the ladle, he makes the <s>Vāstoṣpatīya</s> offering in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.

body.text: Baudh3.1.14/ vāstoṣpate prati (jānīhy asmān iti puronuvākyām (anūcya /vāstoṣpate śagmayā saṃsadā ta iti yājyayā (juhoti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.14: Having recited the invitatory verse 'O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, receive us favorably,' he makes the offering with the sacrificial verse 'O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, with a pleasant assembly for you.'

body.text: Baudh3.1.15/ sarva eva^āhita.agnir ity eke //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.15: According to some, every [householder] who has established the sacred fires [should perform this].

body.text: Baudh3.1.16/ yāyāvara ity eke //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.16: According to some, [only] the <s>yāyāvara</s> (wandering householder) [should perform this].

body.text: Baudh3.1.17/ (nirgatya grāma.ante grāma.sīmānte vā^(avatiṣṭhate / tatrakuṭīṃ maṭhaṃ vā (karoti kṛtaṃ vā (praviśati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.17: Having gone out, he settles at the village boundary or at the border of the village. There he builds a hut or a <s>maṭha</s> (hermitage), or he enters one already built.

body.text: Baudh3.1.18/ kṛṣṇa.ajina.ādīnām upakḷptānāṃ yasminn [K: yasmin yasminn]arthe yena yena yat.prayojanaṃ tena tena tat (kuryāt //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.18: Of the black antelope skin and other prepared [articles], for whatever purpose, with whichever [article], for whatever use, he should employ that [article] accordingly.

body.text: Baudh3.1.19/ prasiddham agnīnāṃ paricaraṇam / prasiddhaṃdarśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajanam / prasiddhaḥ pañcānāṃ mahatāṃ yajñānāmanuprayogaḥ / utpannānām oṣadhīnāṃ nirvāpaṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.19: The tending of the sacred fires is well-known. The worship through the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon) sacrifices is well-known. The subsidiary performance of the five great sacrifices is well-known. The offering of plants that have grown is to be observed.

body.text: Baudh3.1.20/ viśvebhyo devebhyo juṣṭaṃ (nirvapāmi^iti vā tūṣṇīṃ vā tāḥ(saṃskṛtya (sādhayati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.20: [Saying] 'I offer [this] to all the gods as pleasing,' or silently, he prepares and cooks those [plants].

body.text: Baudh3.1.21/ tasya^adhyāpana.yājana.pratigrahā (nivartante^anye cayajña.kratava iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.21: For him, teaching, officiating at sacrifices, and accepting gifts cease — as do the other sacrificial rites.

body.text: Baudh3.1.22/ haviṣyaṃ ca vrata.upāyanīyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ (bhavati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.22: And the <s>haviṣya</s> (oblation food) and the introductory [offering] for the vow are to be observed.

body.text: Baudh3.1.23/ tad yathā [K omits: tad yathā] sarpir.miśraṃ dadhi.miśramakṣāra.lavaṇam apiśitam aparyuṣitam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.23: That is, namely [K omits: that is, namely]: mixed with ghee, mixed with curds, without alkali or salt, not containing meat, and not stale.

body.text: Baudh3.1.24/ brahmacaryam ṛtau vā (gacchati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.24: <s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), or [conjugal relations only] during the fertile season.

body.text: Baudh3.1.25/ parvaṇi.parvaṇi keśa.śmaśru.loma.nakha.vāpanaṃ śauca.vidhiś ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.1.25: At every <s>parvan</s> (lunar junction), shaving of the hair, beard, body hair, and nails, and the prescribed rules of purification.

body.text:
Baudh3.1.26-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh3.1.26-2ab/ (śrūyate dvividhaṃ śaucaṃ yat^śiṣṭaiḥ paryupāsitam /
Baudh3.1.26-2cd/ bāhyaṃ nirlepa.nirgandham antaḥ.śaucam ahiṃsakam [K: ahiṃsanam] //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.1.26: And they also cite [this verse]:
Purification is heard to be twofold, as practiced by the learned:
external [purity is] freedom from impurity and odor; internal purity is non-violence [K: <s>ahiṃsana</s>].

body.text:
Baudh3.1.27ab/ adbhiḥ (śudhyanti gātrāṇi buddhir jñānena (śudhyati [K:śuddhyatīti] /
Baudh3.1.27cd/ ahiṃsayā ca bhūta.ātmā manaḥ satyena (śudhyati // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.1.27: The limbs are purified by water, the intellect is purified by knowledge,
the self of beings is purified by non-violence, and the mind is purified by truth. Thus.

body.text: Baudh3.2.1/ yathā^u etat ṣaṇṇivartanī^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.1: As also [the livelihood called] <s>ṣaṇṇivartanī</s> (six-plot cultivation).

body.text: Baudh3.2.2/ ṣaḍ eva nivartanāni nirupahatāni (karoti / svāmine bhāgam(utsṛjaty anujñātaṃ vā (gṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.2: He cultivates exactly six plots (<s>nivartanas</s>) without damaging [them]; he gives a share to the landowner, or takes [only] what has been permitted.

body.text:
Baudh3.2.3/ prāk prātar.āśāt karṣī (syād asyūta.nāsikābhyāṃsamuṣkābhyām atudann ārayā muhur.muhur abhyucchandayan // [=
Baudh2.2.4.20-21]
Baudh3.2.4/ etena vidhinā ṣaṇnivartanāni [K: ṣaṇṇivartanāni] (karoti^itiṣaṇṇivartanī //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.2.3: Before the morning meal, he should be a ploughman, [working] with an unperforated nose-rope and testicle-bands, not striking [the oxen], using a goad, frequently urging [them] on. [= Baudh2.2.4.20-21]
Baudh3.2.4: By this prescribed rule he cultivates six plots — thus [it is called] <s>ṣaṇṇivartanī</s> (six-plot cultivation).

body.text: Baudh3.2.5/ kauddālī^iti / jala.abhyāśe kuddālena vā phālena vā tīkṣṇa.kāṣṭhena vā (khanati bījāny (āvapati kanda.mūla.phala.śāka.oṣadhīr (niṣpādayati //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.5: [The livelihood called] <s>kauddālī</s> (hoeing): Near water, with a hoe or a ploughshare or a sharp stick, he digs, sows seeds, and produces tubers, roots, fruits, vegetables, and herbs.

body.text: Baudh3.2.6/ kuddālena (karoti^iti kauddālī //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.6: Because he works with a hoe (<s>kuddāla</s>), [it is called] <s>kauddālī</s>.

body.text: Baudh3.2.7/ dhruvayā vartamānaḥ śuklena vāsasā śiro (veṣṭayati / bhūtyaitvā śiro (veṣṭayāmi^iti / brahma.varcasam (asi brahma.varcasāya tvā^itikṛṣṇa.ajinam (ādatte^abliṅgābhiḥ pavitram / balam (asi balāya [ḥ:valāya] tvā^iti kamaṇḍalum / dhānyam (asi puṣṭyai tvā^iti vīvadham /sakhā mā gopāya^iti daṇḍam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.7: Living by the <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed livelihood), he wraps his head with a white garment [saying]: 'For prosperity, I wrap my head.' [Saying] 'You are <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual splendor), [I take] you for <s>brahmavarcas</s>,' he takes a black antelope skin; with the <s>abliṅga</s> verses [he takes] a water-strainer. [Saying] 'You are strength, [I take] you for strength,' [he takes] a water-pot. [Saying] 'You are grain, [I take] you for nourishment,' [he takes] a carrying-pole. [Saying] 'O friend, protect me,' [he takes] a staff.

body.text:
Baudh3.2.8-1/ atha^(upaniṣkramya vyāhṛtīr (japitvā diśām anumantraṇaṃ (japati /
Baudh3.2.8-2ab/ pṛthivī ca^antarikṣaṃ ca dyaur nakṣatrāṇi yā diśaḥ /
Baudh3.2.8-2cd/ agnir vāyuś ca sūryaś ca (pāntu māṃ pathi devatāḥ // iti //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.2.8: Then, having gone forth, having recited the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), he recites the invocation of the directions:
'May the earth and the atmosphere and the sky, the stars, and the directions,
may <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Sūrya</s> — may these deities protect me on my path.' Thus.

body.text: Baudh3.2.9/ mānastokīyaṃ (japitvā grāmaṃ (praviśya gṛha.dvāre.gṛha.dvāraātmānaṃ vīvadhena saha darśanāt saṃdarśanī^ity (ācakṣate //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.9: Having recited the <s>Mānastokīya</s> [hymn], entering the village, [standing] at door after door, showing himself together with his carrying-pole — from this visible display, [it is] called <s>saṃdarśanī</s> (the showing).

body.text: Baudh3.2.10/ vṛtter vṛtter avārttāyāṃ tayā^eva tasya dhruvaṃ vartanāddhruvā^iti parikīrtitā //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.10: [When proceeding] from one livelihood to another, when no [other] livelihood [is available], because he subsists permanently by that very [fixed livelihood], it is called <s>dhruvā</s> (the fixed one).

body.text: Baudh3.2.11/ saṃprakṣālanī^iti / utpannānām oṣadhīnāṃ prakṣepaṇam /nikṣepaṇaṃ na^asti nicayo vā / bhājanāni (saṃprakṣālya (nyubjati^itisaṃprakṣālanī //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.11: [The livelihood called] <s>saṃprakṣālanī</s> (the rinsing): The distribution of herbs that have grown — there is no storing up, nor accumulation. Having rinsed the vessels, he turns them upside down — thus [it is called] <s>saṃprakṣālanī</s>.

body.text: Baudh3.2.12/ samūhā^iti / avārita.sthāneṣu pathiṣu vā kṣetreṣuvā^apratihata.avakāśeṣu vā yatra yatra^oṣadhayo (vidyante tatra tatrasamūhanyā (samuhya tābhir (vartayati^iti samūhā //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.12: [The livelihood called] <s>samūhā</s> (the gleaning): In unenclosed places, or on paths, or in fields, or in unrestricted open spaces — wherever herbs are found, there he gathers [them] by sweeping together and subsists on them — thus [it is called] <s>samūhā</s>.

body.text: Baudh3.2.13/ phālanī^ity [K: pālanīty] ahiṃsikā^ity eva^idam uktaṃ(bhavati / tuṣa.vihīnāṃs taṇḍulān (icchati sajjanebhyo bījāni vā /phālayati^iti phālanī [K: pālayatīti pālanī] //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.13: [The livelihood called] <s>phālanī</s> [K: <s>pālanī</s>] — this is said to mean <s>ahiṃsikā</s> (the non-violent one): He seeks husked rice grains from virtuous people, or seeds. He splits [the husks] — thus [it is called] <s>phālanī</s> [K: he preserves — thus <s>pālanī</s>].

body.text: Baudh3.2.14/ śiloñchā^iti [K: siloñcheti] / avārita.sthāneṣu pathiṣu vākṣetreṣu vā^apratihata.avakāśeṣu vā yatra yatra^oṣadhayo (vidyante tatratatra^ekaikaṃ kaṇiśam (uñchayitvā kāle.kāle śilair (vartayati^itiśiloñchā [K: siloñchā] //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.14: [The livelihood called] <s>śiloñchā</s> [K: <s>siloñchā</s>] (stone-gleaning): In unenclosed places, or on paths, or in fields, or in unrestricted open spaces — wherever herbs are found, there, having gleaned one ear of grain at a time, he subsists at each season by [grinding with] stones — thus [it is called] <s>śiloñchā</s> [K: <s>siloñchā</s>].

body.text: Baudh3.2.15/ kāpotā^iti / avārita.sthāneṣu pathiṣu vā [K omits vā]kṣetreṣu vā^apratihata.avakāśeṣu vā yatra yatra^oṣadhayo (vidyante tatratatra^aṅgulībhyām ekaikām oṣadhim (uñchayitvā saṃdaṃśanāt [K:sandarśanāt] kapotavad iti kāpotā //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.15: [The livelihood called] <s>kāpotā</s> (the pigeon-like): In unenclosed places, or on paths [K omits: or], or in fields, or in unrestricted open spaces — wherever herbs are found, there, having gleaned one herb at a time with [two] fingers, because of picking as a pigeon [does] — thus [it is called] <s>kāpotā</s>.

body.text: Baudh3.2.16/ siddhecchā^iti / vṛttibhiḥ śrānto vṛddhatvād dhātu.kṣayād vāsajjanebhyaḥ siddham annam (icchati^iti siddhecchā //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.16: [The livelihood called] <s>siddhecchā</s> (seeking cooked food): Exhausted by [other] livelihoods, due to old age or deterioration of bodily constitution, he seeks cooked food from virtuous people — thus [it is called] <s>siddhecchā</s>.

body.text: Baudh3.2.17/ tasya^ātmani samāropaṇaṃ [K: tasyātmasamāropaṇaṃ] (vidyatesaṃnyāsivad upacāraḥ pavitra.kāṣāya.vāso.varjam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.17: For him there is known a self-elevation [K: self-elevation]; the conduct is like that of a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> (renunciant), except for the water-strainer and ochre garments.

body.text: Baudh3.2.18/ vānyā^api vṛkṣa.latā.vally.oṣadhīnāṃ ca tṛṇa.oṣadhīnāṃ caśyāmāka.jartila.ādīnām / vanyābhir [K: vānyābhir] (vartayati^itivānyā //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.2.18: Also [the livelihood called] <s>vānyā</s> (the forest-produce): [Subsisting] on trees, creepers, vines, herbs, grasses, and plants such as <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) and <s>jartila</s> (wild sesame) and the like. He subsists on forest [produce] — thus [it is called] <s>vānyā</s> [K: <s>vānyā</s>].

body.text:
Baudh3.2.19-1/ atha^apy (udāharanti /
Baudh3.2.19-2ab/ mṛgaiḥ saha parispandaḥ saṃvāsas tebhir[!] eva ca /
Baudh3.2.19-2cd/ tair eva sadṛśī vṛttiḥ pratyakṣaṃ svarga.lakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.2.19: And they also cite [this verse]:
Moving about with the deer, dwelling together with them,
having a livelihood similar to theirs — [this is] a visible sign of heaven.

body.text:
Baudh3.2.19-3/ pratyakṣaṃ svarga.lakṣaṇam iti // [Baudh3.2.19 = Baudh3.3.22]
Baudh3.3.1/ atha vānaprastha.dvaividhyam [K: vānaprasthasya dvaividhyam] //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.2.19 (cont.): A visible sign of heaven. Thus. [Baudh3.2.19 = Baudh3.3.22]
Baudh3.3.1: Now, the twofold division of the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) [K: the twofold division of the forest-dweller].

body.text: Baudh3.3.2/ pacamānakā apacamānakāś ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.2: Those who cook and those who do not cook.

body.text: Baudh3.3.3/ tatra pacamānakāḥ pañcavidhāḥ sarva.āraṇyakā vaituṣikāḥkanda.mūla.bhakṣāḥ phala.bhakṣāḥ śāka.bhakṣāś ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.3: Among these, those who cook are of five kinds: the <s>sarvāraṇyakas</s> (all-forest [dwellers]), the <s>vaituṣikas</s> (husk-removers), the tuber-and-root eaters, the fruit eaters, and the vegetable eaters.

body.text: Baudh3.3.4/ tatra sarva.āraṇyakā nāma dvividhā dvividham āraṇyamāśrayanta indra.avasiktā retovasiktāś [retas.avasiktāś] ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.4: Among these, those called <s>sarvāraṇyakas</s> (all-forest [dwellers]) are of two kinds, resorting to two kinds of forest [produce]: the <s>indrāvasiktas</s> (rain-watered) and the <s>retovasiktas</s> (seed-sown) [<s>retasavasiktas</s>].

body.text: Baudh3.3.5/ tatra^indra.avasiktā nāma vallī.gulma.latā.vṛkṣāṇām(ānayitvā (śrapayitvā sāyaṃ.prātar.agnihotraṃ (hutvāyaty.atithi.vratibhyaś ca (dattvā^atha^itarat^śeṣa.bhakṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.5: Among these, the <s>indrāvasiktas</s> (rain-watered) [are those who], having brought [produce] from vines, shrubs, creepers, and trees, having cooked [it], having offered the evening and morning <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation), and having given to travelers, guests, and those observing vows, then eat the remainder.

body.text: Baudh3.3.6/ retovasiktā [retas.avasiktā] nāma māṃsaṃvyāghra.vṛka.śyena.ādibhir anyatamena vā hatam (ānayitvā (śrapayitvāsāyaṃ.prātar.agnihotraṃ (hutvā yaty.atithi.vratibhyaś ca(dattvā^atha^itarat^śeṣa.bhakṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.6: The <s>retovasiktas</s> (seed-sown) [<s>retasavasiktas</s>] [are those who], having brought meat killed by a tiger, wolf, hawk, or other [such animal], having cooked [it], having offered the evening and morning <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation), and having given to travelers, guests, and those observing vows, then eat the remainder.

body.text: Baudh3.3.7/ vaituṣikās tuṣa.dhānya.varjaṃ taṇḍulān (ānayitvā (śrapayitvāsāyaṃ.prātar.agnihotraṃ (hutvā yaty.atithi.vratibhyaś ca(dattvā^atha^itarat^śeṣa.bhakṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.7: The <s>vaituṣikas</s> (husk-removers), having brought rice grains freed from husks and grain, having cooked [them], having offered the evening and morning <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation), and having given to travelers, guests, and those observing vows, then eat the remainder.

body.text: Baudh3.3.8/ kanda.mūla.phala.śāka.bhakṣāṇām apy evam eva //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.8: For the tuber, root, fruit, and vegetable eaters, the same procedure [applies].

body.text: Baudh3.3.9/ pañca^eva^apacamānakā unmajjakāḥ pravṛttāśino mukhenādāyinastoyāhārā vāyubhakṣāś ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.9: Those who do not cook are likewise five: the <s>unmajjakas</s> (surface-gatherers), the <s>pravṛttāśins</s> (hand-eaters), the <s>mukhenādāyins</s> (mouth-takers), the <s>toyāhāras</s> (water-subsisting), and the <s>vāyubhakṣas</s> (air-eaters).

body.text: Baudh3.3.10/ tatra^unmajjakā nāma loha.aśma.karaṇa.varjam //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.10: Among these, the <s>unmajjakas</s> (surface-gatherers) [eat] without [using implements of] metal or stone.

body.text: Baudh3.3.11/ hastena^(ādāya pravṛttāśinaḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.11: The <s>pravṛttāśins</s> (hand-eaters) take [food] with the hand.

body.text: Baudh3.3.12/ mukhenādāyino mukhena^(ādadate //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.12: The <s>mukhenādāyins</s> (mouth-takers) take [food] with the mouth.

body.text: Baudh3.3.13/ toya.āhārāḥ kevalaṃ toyāhārāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.13: The <s>toyāhāras</s> (water-subsisting) subsist on water alone.

body.text: Baudh3.3.14/ vāyubhakṣā nirāhārāś ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.14: The <s>vāyubhakṣas</s> (air-eaters) are those who take no food at all.

body.text: Baudh3.3.15/ iti [K omits iti] vaikhānasānāṃ vihitā daśa dīkṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.15: Thus [K omits: thus] these ten <s>dīkṣās</s> (consecrated observances) are prescribed for the <s>Vaikhānasas</s> (forest hermits).

body.text: Baudh3.3.16/ yaḥ sva.śāstram [K: śāstram] (abhyupetya daṇḍaṃ ca maunaṃ ca^apramādaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.16: He who, having accepted his own scripture, [observes] the staff, silence, and vigilance.

body.text: Baudh3.3.17/ vaikhānasāḥ (śudhyanti nirāhārāś ca^iti //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.17: The <s>Vaikhānasas</s> are purified, and [so are] those who take no food. Thus.

body.text: Baudh3.3.18/ śāstra.parigrahaḥ sarveṣāṃ brahma.vaikhānasānām //
body.translated_text: Baudh3.3.18: The acceptance of scripture [is enjoined] for all <s>Brahma-Vaikhānasas</s> (brahmanical forest hermits).

body.text:
Baudh3.3.19ab/ na (druhyed daṃśa.maśakān himavāṃs tāpaso (bhavet /
Baudh3.3.19cd/ vana.pratiṣṭhaḥ saṃtuṣṭaś cīra.carma.jala.priyaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.3.19: One should not harm biting insects and mosquitoes; the ascetic should be [firm as] the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya),
established in the forest, content, delighting in bark garments, animal skins, and water.

body.text:
Baudh3.3.20ab/ atithīn (pūjayet pūrvaṃ kāle tv āśramam āgatān /
Baudh3.3.20cd/ deva.vipra.agnihotre ca yuktas tapasi tāpasaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.3.20: The ascetic should first honor guests who come to his hermitage at the proper time,
and should be devoted to [worship of] gods, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation), and austerity.

body.text:
Baudh3.3.21-1ab/ kṛcchrāṃ vṛttim asaṃhāryāṃ sāmānyāṃ mṛga.pakṣibhiḥ /
Baudh3.3.21-1cd/ tad ahar jana.saṃbhārāṃ kaṣāya.kaṭuka.āśrayām //
body.translated_text:
Baudh3.3.21: [Having adopted] a hard livelihood, impossible to take away, shared with deer and birds,
gathered each day from the people, based on astringent and bitter [foods],

body.text:
Baudh3.3.21-2ab/ (parigṛhya śubhāṃ vṛttim etāṃ durjana.varjitām /
Baudh3.3.21-2cd/ vana.vāsam (upāśritya brāhmaṇo na^(avasīdati //
body.translated_text:
having adopted this auspicious livelihood, shunned by the wicked,
having resorted to forest-dwelling, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> does not decline.

body.text:
Baudh3.3.22-1ab/ mṛgaiḥ saha parispandaḥ saṃvāsas tebhir[!] eva ca /
